issue_comments.body:
Implemented in #9 (branch `fix/1-sync-state-healthy`, head `fb7c7d7`).

**What changed**
- UTF-8 on every text path: explicit `encoding="utf-8"` for the `gh`/`git` subprocess decode; stdout/stderr reconfigured to UTF-8 at CLI entry. Non-ASCII titles/bodies round-trip exactly; JSON output is never truncated by a cp1252 pipe.
- `last_error` is recorded on every failure path before propagating (the recorder covers the whole DB-touching body, including the prologue and the JSONL sidecar — lock-landing experiments drove two review rounds); unexpected crashes and pre-sync storage faults are reported as `{"ok": false}` result objects, not tracebacks.
- `status` now reports `complete` per repo, backed by a `full_sync_pending` marker: an interrupted full sync reads `complete: false`; the resuming clean run stamps `last_full_sync_at`.
- Repo slugs are canonical lowercase at three boundaries (sync write, CLI dispatch, query layer) — `--repo ZaxbyHub/X` and `zaxbyhub/x` are one repo everywhere.
- `PRAGMA user_version` migration framework (forward-only, per-migration transactions, refuses newer versions); migration 1→2 adds the marker column and case-folds + merges existing case-split databases in place.

**How to use it**
Nothing new to learn: `status` first (the bundled skill now says so), `sync` when no corpus exists. All existing commands work unchanged; output is now always UTF-8.

**Migration steps**
None required. The first command that opens an existing database upgrades it in place (one-time write; a read like `search` may perform it). Legacy rows that never recorded a full sync read `complete: false` and self-heal on the next clean sync. Already-garbled text from pre-fix cp1252 syncs is not repaired by this change — re-run `sync --force` for those; counting them is #2's `doctor`. The read-only `sql` command never migrates.

Verification: 91 tests green (baseline 70), all ten frozen acceptance checks replayed PASS, three-model review (plan critic ×5 rounds, implementation reviewer ×3 rounds with mutation probes, final critic with an independent mutation probe) — evidence and the checkpoint anchor receipt are in the PR body.

item.body:
_Remediation issue. Generated from the first-class agent review of 2026-09-30 (maintainer-local report, informed by a GLM 5.3 long-session field report); claims re-checked against origin/main e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b on 2026-09-30. One issue = one PR. Tracking: #8._

## Summary
An agent reading `status` today cannot tell a healthy corpus from a damaged one:
- On Windows, `gh` output is decoded with the locale codec (cp1252). That silently garbles non-ASCII text, and some byte sequences crash the reader thread with an exception `sync_repo` does not catch, so `last_error` stays null.
- A resumed full sync is recorded as incremental, so `last_full_sync_at` stays NULL on complete corpora and nothing signals completeness.
- Repo slugs are case-sensitive, so one repo can be stored twice in the same DB.
- CLI output crashes mid-JSON on emoji or CJK titles when stdout is cp1252.

This PR makes sync state trustworthy:
- UTF-8 on every input and output path.
- `last_error` recorded on every failure path.
- A `complete` flag backed by a `full_sync_pending` marker.
- Case-folded slugs, with a migration that merges existing duplicates.
- The `PRAGMA user_version` migration framework that the later schema slots (B-01, C-02) build on.
- The bundled skill's first action changes from `sync` to `status`, the zero-code mitigation for agents that start a cold rebuild from a worktree.

GLM's field report said an interrupted full sync leaves the DB "hollow forever". That is mostly wrong. The listing is sorted by `updated` ascending and the watermark advances per item, so an interruption during ingest resumes correctly. The real hollow cases are:
- the crash paths above (this issue)
- a failure during listing, which throws away the whole buffered listing ([Workstream C] PR 1)

## Audit provenance
- Review findings P0-2a (input encoding), P0-2b (output encoding), P0-2c (`last_error` coverage), P0-2d (completeness), P0-2h (slug case), "migrations" (from P1-2), and P0 skill "First action".
- [repro] `subprocess.run(..., text=True)` on UTF-8 bytes for "ā" under the cp1252 locale → `UnicodeDecodeError` in `_readerthread`, `proc.stdout = None`.
- [repro] `zaxbygraph item 1 --format json | tail` on a row titled `Crash 🚀 起動` → output truncated at `"title": ` (cp1252 stdout).
- [repro] Read-only scan of 17 `history.db` files on the maintainer's machine:
  - 8 contain garbled rows. `E:\ZCode\opencode-swarm` has 19 bodies with `\xe2\u20ac\u201d` (an em dash stored as `â€”`) against 1,768 stored correctly, which shows syncs ran with and without `PYTHONUTF8`.
  - The three ~3,003-item `ZaxbyHub/opencode-swarm` DBs all have `last_full_sync_at = NULL`.
  - `E:\ZCode\trainingapp` holds both `ZaxbyHub/trainingapp` (138 items) and `zaxbyhub/trainingapp` (132 items).
- Master re-check: STILL-PRESENT at e2ef892.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. `gh` stdout is decoded with the locale codec. [github.py#L61](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/github.py#L61) (also [repo.py#L53](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/repo.py#L53))
   ```py
   text=True,
   ```
2. Only two exception types record `last_error`; a decode error, an `AttributeError` on `proc.stdout = None`, or `KeyboardInterrupt` escapes with state looking clean. [sync.py#L161](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/sync.py#L161)
   ```py
   except (GitHubError, sqlite3.Error) as exc:
   ```
3. Full vs incremental is decided once at run start, so a run that resumes an interrupted full sync is recorded as incremental and `last_full_sync_at` is never set. [sync.py#L67](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/sync.py#L67)
   ```py
   full = since is None
   ```
4. Slugs keep their case, and every table keys on `repo`. [repo.py#L14](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/repo.py#L14)
   ```py
   def validate_slug(slug: str) -> str:
   ```
5. JSON output uses `ensure_ascii=False` against a stdout that is cp1252 on Windows. [cli.py#L40](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/cli.py#L40)
   ```py
   json.dump(data, sys.stdout, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)
   ```
6. There is no migration mechanism: the schema is `CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS` plus a fixed `schema_version` meta row. [db.py#L8](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/db.py#L8)
   ```py
   SCHEMA_VERSION = "1"
   ```
7. The bundled skill's first instruction is a full `sync`, so an agent in a fresh worktree starts a cold rebuild (see `skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md`, `## First action`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN the gh source returns a payload containing "ā", "—" and "🚀" under a cp1252 locale THE SYSTEM SHALL store all three unchanged in `items.title` / `items.body`. [P0-2a]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_github.GhDecodeTests.test_utf8_payload_roundtrips_under_cp1252_locale -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_github.py (new)
  - why: RED at main: github.py#L61 decodes with `locale.getpreferredencoding()`. The probe above raised `UnicodeDecodeError` and returned `stdout=None`.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN `item N --format json` prints an item whose title contains an emoji to a stdout configured as cp1252 THE SYSTEM SHALL emit complete JSON that `json.loads` accepts. [P0-2b]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_cli.CliEncodingTests.test_item_emoji_title_under_cp1252_stdout -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_cli.py
  - why: RED at main: cli.py#L40 writes non-ASCII to cp1252 stdout; the repro truncated at `"title": `.
- [ ] AC3: WHEN an exception other than `GitHubError`/`sqlite3.Error` escapes the sync loop THE SYSTEM SHALL record its message in `sync_state.last_error` before propagating. [P0-2c]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_sync.SyncStateTests.test_unexpected_exception_records_last_error -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_sync.py
  - why: RED at main: sync.py#L161 catches only two types.
- [ ] AC4: WHEN a sync with no prior watermark is interrupted after ingesting some items, and is then re-run to a clean finish THE SYSTEM SHALL report `status.complete == false` after the interruption and `true` after the resume. [P0-2d]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_sync.SyncStateTests.test_resumed_full_sync_reports_complete -v
  - expect: FAIL (no `complete` field at main)
  - files: tests/test_sync.py
  - why: RED at main: sync.py#L67 marks the resumed run incremental; the three opencode-swarm DBs show the resulting NULL.
- [ ] AC5: WHEN sync runs with `--repo ZaxbyHub/X` and later with `--repo zaxbyhub/x` THE SYSTEM SHALL keep exactly one `sync_state` row and one set of items for that repo. [P0-2h]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_sync.SyncStateTests.test_slug_case_folds -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_sync.py
  - why: RED at main: repo.py#L14 preserves case; reproduced in `E:\ZCode\trainingapp`.
- [ ] AC6: WHEN a v1 database (no `user_version`) containing case-split duplicate repos is opened by the new code THE SYSTEM SHALL migrate it to the current `user_version`, merge the duplicates keeping the fresher row per item, and preserve every other row. [migrations, P0-2h]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_migrations.MigrationTests.test_v1_db_upgrades_and_merges_case_split_repos -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_migrations.py (new)
  - why: RED at main: no migration mechanism exists (db.py#L8).
- [ ] AC7: WHEN `skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md` is read THE SYSTEM SHALL name `status` (not `sync`) as the first action, and state that `sync` runs only when no corpus is found. [skill]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_docs.SkillDocTests.test_first_action_is_status_not_sync -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_docs.py (new)
  - why: RED at main: `## First action` is `zaxbygraph sync --repo OWNER/REPO`.
- [ ] AC8: WHEN a sqlite error occurs mid-sync THE SYSTEM SHALL still record `last_error` and remain resumable.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_sync.SyncTests.test_sqlite_error_mid_sync_records_last_error_and_is_resumable -v
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_sync.py
  - why: GREEN at main; widening the exception handling must not regress it.
- [ ] AC9: WHEN a full sync is followed by an incremental one THE SYSTEM SHALL pass `since` from the watermark.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_sync.SyncTests.test_full_then_incremental_since -v
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_sync.py
  - why: GREEN at main; `full_sync_pending` must not alter watermark semantics.
- [ ] AC10: WHEN a 429 hits an extra GET mid-sync THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the items ingested before it.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_sync.SyncTests.test_429_on_extra_get_leaves_earlier_items -v
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_sync.py
  - why: GREEN at main.

## Constraints and invariants
- The runtime stays stdlib-only. Python 3.11+. SQLite ≥ 3.35.
- An existing DB must upgrade in place through the migration framework. No forced full resync.
- Migrations are forward-only, idempotent and ordered, and each runs in its own transaction.
- Canonical slug storage must be lowercase, or GitHub's `full_name` normalized consistently. Displayed output may keep the original case, but every lookup must case-fold.
- The UTF-8 fix does not repair rows already stored garbled. Those need `sync --force`; counting them belongs to `doctor` ([Workstream A] PR 2).

## Suggested approach (non-binding)
- `subprocess.run(..., encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")` in `github.py` and `repo.py`.
- `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")` / `sys.stderr.reconfigure(...)` at the top of `cli.main`.
- In the outer handler of `sync_repo`, catch `BaseException`, record `last_error`, then re-raise. Write `sync_started_at` at start.
- Set `full_sync_pending = 1` when a run begins with `issues_since IS NULL`. Clear it on any clean finish (whichever run started the full sync) and set `last_full_sync_at` then. `status.complete = NOT full_sync_pending AND last_error IS NULL`.
- A `migrations` list of `(version, callable)` applied under `PRAGMA user_version`. Migration 2 adds the `sync_state` columns and case-folds and merges `repo` across every table.

## Scope
- In scope: all of the above.
- Out of scope:
  - global DB store, read-only open, repo scoping on queries, `doctor` (owned by [Workstream A] PR 2)
  - JSON error envelope (owned by [Workstream A] PR 3)
  - streamed listing and the listing-loss case (owned by [Workstream C] PR 1)

## Files expected to change
- src/zaxbygraph/github.py
- src/zaxbygraph/repo.py
- src/zaxbygraph/sync.py (hotspot)
- src/zaxbygraph/store.py
- src/zaxbygraph/db.py (hotspot, schema lane head)
- src/zaxbygraph/schema.sql (hotspot)
- src/zaxbygraph/query.py (`status`)
- src/zaxbygraph/cli.py (hotspot)
- skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md
- tests/test_github.py, tests/test_migrations.py, tests/test_docs.py (new); tests/test_sync.py, tests/test_cli.py

## Defect class and known siblings
- Class: silent failure / false-healthy state (it looks like success when it isn't), plus a Windows portability defect.
- Known siblings: every other `subprocess.run(text=True)` call; the `status` "empty DB vs empty repo" ambiguity (owned by [Workstream A] PR 2).
- Guard that should have caught it: CI runs on windows-latest, but no fixture carries non-ASCII payloads and no test interrupts a full sync and then resumes it.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: none
- Schema after: none (lane head: introduces the migration framework)
- Gated on: none

## Tier and risk triggers
- Tier: M
- Risk triggers: schema/migrations, data durability (duplicate merge), Windows encoding

## Verification
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests` (baseline at main: `Ran 70 tests ... OK`)
- Manual:
  1. On Windows without `PYTHONUTF8`, sync a repo that has non-ASCII issue text, then `zaxbygraph item N | python -c "import json,sys; json.load(sys.stdin)"`.
  2. Copy `E:\ZCode\trainingapp\.swarm\zaxbygraph\history.db`, open it with the new build, and confirm one `zaxbyhub/trainingapp` corpus.
- Environment: CI runs windows-latest and ubuntu-latest on Python 3.11 and 3.12. Windows is the primary target.

## Related GitHub issues
- Tracking epic: #8

## Definition of done
- All ACs verified with evidence; PR body `Closes #<n>` with a `## Closure evidence` section listing each AC's argv and result.

item.title: [Workstream A] PR 1 of 3: Sync state stops looking healthy after crashes, garbled text and case-split repos

issue_comments.body:
Delivered via PR #10 (head ac290278b22f331d3456188abe47895415b7b26f, branch `fix/2-worktree-global-store`; CI green on windows-latest + ubuntu-latest x Python 3.11/3.12).

## What changed

- **The graph is keyed by repo, not by checkout.** Resolution order: `--db` > `ZAXBYGRAPH_DB` > the user-level store `<root>/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/history.db` (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\zaxbygraph` on Windows / `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/zaxbygraph` elsewhere, `ZAXBYGRAPH_HOME` overrides) > a legacy in-repo DB under the main worktree (migration continuity) > the would-be store path. Every worktree, clone, and subagent of a repo now resolves the same graph.
- **Reads stop creating empty ones.** All nine read commands open read-only, never create, and when no corpus exists for the resolved repo they exit **3** with the resolved path and the exact `zaxbygraph sync --repo <slug>` command. A DB holding other repos exits **2** and lists them; a pre-#9 mixed-case legacy DB gets an actionable "same repo with pre-fold casing → `doctor --consolidate`" message.
- **Every read is repo-scoped by default** (`--repo` > git origin; `--repo ''` stays an explicit no-filter). `sql` result rows carrying a `repo` column are filtered to the resolved repo.
- **Sync lock**: `<db>.sync.lock` — a second sync joins with `{ok: true, joined: true}` and zero GitHub calls; `--wait` blocks; dead same-host holders are recovered atomically; foreign-host locks are never stolen.
- **New `where`**: prints the full resolution chain (cwd → git common dir → slug → DB path → exists/items/watermark/complete, legacy DBs found, the serving DB, sync-lock holder).
- **New `doctor [--consolidate] [--scan DIR]`**: reports scattered legacy DBs (per-DB item + garbled-row counts); `--consolidate` copies the freshest complete corpus into the store — originals are never modified (v1/mixed-case candidates are migrated on a temp copy; repo values case-folded on adoption).

## How to use it

No flags needed for the normal flow: `zaxbygraph status` in any checkout of a repo answers identically; `zaxbygraph where` shows which DB you are reading and why; `zaxbygraph doctor` reports (and `--consolidate` adopts) the old scattered DBs.

## Migration

No migration required for correctness — existing in-repo DBs keep working via the legacy fallback, and `sync` upgrades in place. To consolidate scattered DBs into the new store (the maintainer's 17-DB situation), run once per repo, e.g.:

```bash
zaxbygraph doctor --consolidate --repo OWNER/REPO --scan ~/.zmem/zaxbygraph/OWNER/REPO
```

Originals are copied, never deleted. Behavior changes to note: `status` on a fresh path now exits 3 (was empty-JSON exit 0); the store lives outside the repo, so `history.db` no longer appears under checkouts.

## Acceptance checkpoint anchor (external publication)

`issue-tracer-checkpoint-v1 slug=2-worktree-global-store manifest=f655132bec93971b6f769caf6ff656b1233de173 semantics=7f4fa90b5374acb82af08ca50d8e17ca0fcca0c2 tree=03b50d84c59a32dab6e5bc1bd2688a69260e9785`

Verify locally with: `repro-check.sh verify-anchor --slug 2-worktree-global-store --receipt '<literal above>'`

Full acceptance evidence (AC1–AC11, closure gates) in the PR body.

item.body:
_Remediation issue. Generated from the first-class agent review of 2026-09-30 (maintainer-local report, informed by a GLM 5.3 long-session field report); claims re-checked against origin/main e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b on 2026-09-30. One issue = one PR. Tracking: #8._

## Summary
The graph's location is derived from the **checkout**, not from the **repo**:
- `find_git_root` stops at the first `.git` entry. In a linked worktree that entry is a file, so every worktree resolves to its own `.zaxbygraph/history.db` or `.swarm/zaxbygraph/history.db`.
- Every read command opens the DB through `connect()`, which runs `mkdir` and `init_schema`. So `search`, `open` or `status` run from the wrong cwd **creates a new empty graph** and returns `[]` with exit 0.
- The agent then concludes "no prior art", or runs `sync` and starts a full cold rebuild. This is the maintainer's reported friction point: agents in worktrees can't find the graph, or build a new one.

Separately, query commands never apply the default repo, although `--repo` help says "default: git origin":
- `open`, `search`, `churn` and `sql` mix every repo in the DB.
- `item N` returns any repo's #N.
- `path` picks `SELECT repo FROM items LIMIT 1`.

This PR:
- keys the graph by repo slug in a user-level store
- makes reads non-creating with a distinct "no corpus" exit code
- resolves the repo on every command
- serializes syncs with a lock
- adds `where` / `doctor` to explain resolution and consolidate the existing scattered DBs

## Audit provenance
- Review findings P0-1 (all) and P0-2e.
- [repro] In a scratch repo (`git init main` with origin `acme/widget`, then `git worktree add ../feature`), `zaxbygraph search anything --format json` run in `feature/` returned `{"items": [], "comments": []}` with exit 0 and created `feature/.zaxbygraph/history.db`.
- [repro] With `acme/widget` and `other/repo` rows in one DB, `zaxbygraph open --format json` run inside the `acme/widget` worktree returned rows from both repos.
- [repro] Read-only scan of the maintainer's machine found **17 separate `history.db` files**:
  - `ZaxbyHub/opencode-swarm` ×3, about 190 MB each (~575 MB of duplicates, each a separate cold sync).
  - `ZaxbyHub/ragappv3`: 3 populated copies plus 2 empty ones (`ragappv3-568`, `E:\ClaudeCode\RAGAPPv3`).
  - `zaxbysauce/zmem` ×5 with differing counts (195 / 198 / 219 / 267 / 267), some stored inside other repos' DBs.
  - Empty DBs at `~/.swarm/zaxbygraph/` and `zaxby-hyperv-mcp/.zaxbygraph/`.
  - A slug-keyed layout `~/.zmem/zaxbygraph/<owner>/<repo>/history.db` already exists, created by other tooling.
- Master re-check: STILL-PRESENT at e2ef892.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. Root discovery stops at a worktree's `.git` *file*. [paths.py#L9](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/paths.py#L9)
   ```py
   if (candidate / ".git").exists():
   ```
2. The default DB path is derived from that checkout root. [paths.py#L31](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/paths.py#L31)
   ```py
   def default_db_path(cwd: Path | None = None) -> Path:
   ```
3. Every command, reads included, opens through a creating connect. [cli.py#L57](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/cli.py#L57) → [db.py#L29](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/db.py#L29)
   ```py
   db_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   ```
4. `item` without `--repo` matches any repo's number. [query.py#L106](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L106)
   ```py
   row = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM items WHERE number = ?", (number,)).fetchone()
   ```
5. `path` without `--repo` picks an arbitrary repo. [query.py#L227](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L227)
   ```py
   row = conn.execute("SELECT repo FROM items LIMIT 1").fetchone()
   ```
6. Nothing prevents two concurrent syncs of the same repo into one DB. Per-item `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` makes each row atomic, not the whole run. [sync.py#L103](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/sync.py#L103)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN a read command runs in a linked worktree of a repo that already has a synced graph THE SYSTEM SHALL read that same graph (same resolved path, same item count) and create no new DB file. [P0-1]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_paths.WorktreeResolutionTests.test_worktree_resolves_to_existing_graph -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_paths.py (new)
  - why: RED at main: paths.py#L9 stops at the worktree; the repro created `feature/.zaxbygraph/history.db`.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN two separate clones with the same origin slug run `status` THE SYSTEM SHALL resolve the same DB path under the user-level store. [P0-1]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_paths.GlobalStoreTests.test_two_clones_share_one_db -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_paths.py
  - why: RED at main: each clone resolves `<clone>/.zaxbygraph/history.db`.
- [ ] AC3: WHEN any read command (`status search item related churn open path sql export-graph`) runs where no graph exists for the resolved repo THE SYSTEM SHALL create no file or directory, exit 3, and print a message naming the resolved path and the exact `zaxbygraph sync --repo <slug>` command. [P0-1]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_cli.NoCorpusTests.test_reads_never_create_and_exit_3 -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_cli.py
  - why: RED at main: db.py#L29 plus `init_schema`; the repro exited 0 and created a DB.

[P0-1, P0-2a follow-up]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING

  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_cli.CliTests.test_search_json_shape -v
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_cli.py

- Slugs are case-folded ([Workstream A] PR 1 lands first).

- Lock file `history.db.sync.lock` with `{pid, host, started_at}`, created via `os.open(O_CREAT|O_EXCL)`, with a stale check.

- Out of scope:

PR: https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/pull/11 (feat: one self-describing JSON envelope for every command, errors included)

**What changed** — every command's JSON output is now one self-describing envelope `{ok, db, repo, freshness{synced_at, age_s, complete}, data, truncated}` (+ `error{code, message, hint?}` on failures). Errors answer on **stdout** in JSON mode with coded errors (`no_such_column` carries a hint listing the real columns; probe is PRAGMA-free), while stderr keeps the one-line `error:` echo and gains an identity line (`# db=… repo=… items=… synced=… complete=…`) on every successful read. New: `zaxbygraph schema [TABLE]` (live DDL + per-column notes), `--format jsonl|compact`, `--fields a,b`, `sql --rows objects|array` + `--limit`, `item N --max-body-chars N`. `export-graph`/`sync`/`doctor`/`where` converged on the same emitter. Exit codes (0/1/2/3), the read-only SQL safety layers, and the DB schema are unchanged.

**How to use** — parse stdout as JSON and branch on `ok`; the payload you used to get at the top level is under `data`. Stream safely with `--format jsonl` (any `head -n` prefix parses). Discover the schema with `zaxbygraph schema [TABLE]` instead of a doc path.

**Migration** (breaking by design — the issue's decided hard switch, v0.2.0): move top-level payload reads under `data` (`data["ok"]` keeps working — `ok` is promoted to the envelope root for every command, including `sync`); `churn`/`open` payloads are arrays under `data`; pass `--rows array` to `sql` if you need the old positional rows; switch stderr-parsing error handling to reading `ok`/`error.code` from stdout.

Verified: 129-test suite green (Windows host; CI runs Windows+Ubuntu × 3.11/3.12); frozen acceptance checks 9/9 (RED at base bf0b548, GREEN at head 8d01506); independent plan-critic, implementation-reviewer (3 rounds), and final-critic gates all APPROVE. Full trace: `.agents/issue-traces/3-json-envelope-output-contract/`.

_Remediation issue. Generated from the first-class agent review of 2026-09-30 (maintainer-local report, informed by a GLM 5.3 long-session field report); claims re-checked against origin/main e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b on 2026-09-30. One issue = one PR. Tracking: #8._

## Summary
Agents consume this CLI through pipes, and the output contract works against that:
- **Errors in JSON mode go only to stderr.** With `2>/dev/null`, or when stdout is piped into a parser, a failed query produces an empty stdout, which surfaces as a confusing `JSONDecodeError` in the caller.
- **Result shapes aren't uniform or self-describing.** `open` and `churn` return bare arrays. `sql` returns `{columns, rows}` with positional rows. Nothing states which DB and repo answered, or how fresh it is.
- **The schema isn't discoverable.** The skill points at `../../docs/schema.md`, a relative link that breaks once the skill is installed outside the repo (for example `~/.claude/skills/zaxbygraph/`).
- **Pretty-printed JSON** is about 5 lines per row, and cutting it with `head` truncates it mid-array.

This PR ships **one breaking output-contract change, all at once** so consumers adapt once:
- a uniform envelope
- structured errors on stdout, with column hints for SQL
- object rows
- a `schema` command
- JSONL / compact / `--fields` modes
- a stderr identity line
- a real TTY table
- `--max-body-chars`

## Audit provenance
- Review findings P0-2f, P0-2g, the "`schema` command" (GLM #1 build item), and P2-2.
- [repro] `zaxbygraph sql "select pr_number from pr_files" --format json 2>/dev/null` → empty stdout, exit 1. GLM hit the same failure (`pr_number` vs the real column `number`) and saw it as a Python `JSONDecodeError`.
- [repro] `~/.claude/skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md` links `../../docs/schema.md`, which resolves to `~/.claude/docs/schema.md`; `ls` says it doesn't exist. (`docs/schema.md` does exist in the repo.)
- GLM field report: a `head -60` on pretty JSON silently truncated the open-PR query, and output shapes were re-learned across sessions from stored lessons.
- Master re-check: STILL-PRESENT at e2ef892.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. Errors are written to stderr only, even when JSON output is selected. [cli.py#L187](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/cli.py#L187)
   ```py
   print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
   ```
2. Output is pretty-printed, with no compact or line-oriented mode. [cli.py#L40](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/cli.py#L40)
   ```py
   json.dump(data, sys.stdout, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)
   ```
3. `open` returns a bare list, and `churn` likewise. [query.py#L211](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L211)
   ```py
   def open_items(conn: sqlite3.Connection, repo: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
   ```
4. `sql` returns positional rows with a fixed 200-row cap and no `--limit` flag. [query.py#L402](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L402)
   ```py
   def run_sql(conn: sqlite3.Connection, sql: str, limit: int = 200) -> dict:
   ```
5. The default format switches on TTY, and "text" mode just dumps JSON for nested values. [cli.py#L35](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/cli.py#L35)
   ```py
   return not sys.stdout.isatty()
   ```

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN `sql` fails because a column doesn't exist, with JSON output selected THE SYSTEM SHALL write `{"ok": false, "error": {"code": "no_such_column", "message": ..., "hint": ...}}` to **stdout**, where `hint` lists the real columns of the referenced table, and exit 1. [P0-2f]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_cli.ErrorContractTests.test_sql_bad_column_json_error_on_stdout_with_hint -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_cli.py
  - why: RED at main: cli.py#L187 writes to stderr only; the repro produced an empty stdout.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN any command succeeds with JSON output THE SYSTEM SHALL return an object with `ok`, `db`, `repo`, `freshness{synced_at, age_s, complete}`, `data` and `truncated`. [P0-2g]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_cli.EnvelopeTests.test_every_command_returns_envelope -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_cli.py
  - why: RED at main: `open`/`churn` return bare arrays (query.py#L211) and no command reports `db`/`freshness`.
- [ ] AC3: WHEN `sql` returns rows THE SYSTEM SHALL return them as objects keyed by column by default, keep `--rows array` for positional output, and honour a `--limit` flag. [P0-2g]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_cli.EnvelopeTests.test_sql_rows_are_objects_and_limit_flag -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_cli.py
  - why: RED at main: query.py#L402 returns positional rows with a hard-coded limit.
- [ ] AC4: WHEN `zaxbygraph schema` or `zaxbygraph schema pr_files` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL print the DDL and per-column notes generated from the live DB, including the TEXT-typed `edges.src_id`/`dst_id` and the NULL-unless-patches caveat for `pr_files.patch`. [schema]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_cli.SchemaCommandTests.test_schema_command_lists_columns_and_notes -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_cli.py
  - why: RED at main: no `schema` subcommand.
- [ ] AC5: WHEN `--format jsonl` is selected THE SYSTEM SHALL emit one self-contained JSON object per line, so any `head -n` prefix parses line by line. WHEN `--fields a,b` is given THE SYSTEM SHALL project rows to those keys. [P2-2]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_cli.FormatTests.test_jsonl_prefix_parses_and_fields_projects -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_cli.py
  - why: RED at main: only `json|text` exist (cli.py#L40).
- [ ] AC6: WHEN `item N --max-body-chars 500` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL truncate the body and each comment body to 500 chars and mark them `truncated: true`. [P2-2]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_cli.FormatTests.test_item_max_body_chars -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_cli.py
  - why: RED at main: no such flag.
- [ ] AC7: WHEN any read command runs THE SYSTEM SHALL write exactly one identity line to stderr: `# db=<path> repo=<slug> items=<n> synced=<age> complete=<yes|no>`. [P2-2]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_cli.FormatTests.test_stderr_identity_line -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_cli.py
  - why: RED at main: nothing is written to stderr on success.
- [ ] AC8: WHEN the maintainer decides how to ship the breaking envelope THE SYSTEM SHALL implement it: either a hard switch in v0.2, or envelope behind `--format json2` for one release with a deprecation notice on the old shape.
  - class: NON-EXECUTABLE(PRODUCT_DECISION)
- [ ] AC9: WHEN a write or stacked statement is submitted to `sql` THE SYSTEM SHALL still reject it with exit 2.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_cli.CliTests.test_sql_write_rejected tests.test_query.QueryTests.test_sql_rejects_stacked_statements -v
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_cli.py, tests/test_query.py
  - why: GREEN at main; the new error envelope must keep exit-code semantics.
- [ ] AC10: WHEN a broad SQL query runs THE SYSTEM SHALL still fetch at most limit+1 rows.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_query.QueryTests.test_run_sql_never_materializes_full_result_set -v
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_query.py
  - why: GREEN at main.

## Constraints and invariants
- Exit codes keep their meaning: 0 = ok, 1 = runtime, 2 = bad request, 3 = no corpus (from [Workstream A] PR 2).
- The SQL safety layers (prefix check, stacked-statement scan, `query_only`, `mode=ro`, authorizer) are untouched.
- The skill's "Output shapes" section and `docs/schema.md` are rewritten in the same PR. The skill must stop linking `../../docs/schema.md` and point to `zaxbygraph schema` instead.

## Suggested approach (non-binding)
- A single `emit(result, err=None)` in `cli.py` owns the envelope, the formats and the identity line. Query functions keep returning plain data.
- The column hint comes from `PRAGMA table_info` via a separate trusted connection, never through the user SQL path.
- Column notes live in a dict next to `schema.sql` so `schema` and `docs/schema.md` can't drift. A doc test compares them.

## Scope
- In scope: all of the above, plus the skill/README/`docs/schema.md` updates for the new shapes.
- Out of scope:
  - MCP tool schemas (owned by [Workstream D] PR 1, which reuses the envelope)
  - search result fields `matched_mode` / `total_matches` (owned by [Workstream B] PR 1)

## Files expected to change
- src/zaxbygraph/cli.py (hotspot)
- src/zaxbygraph/query.py
- new src/zaxbygraph/schema_notes.py
- skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md
- docs/schema.md
- README.md
- tests/test_cli.py, tests/test_query.py

## Defect class and known siblings
- Class: pipe-hostile, non-self-describing output contract.
- Known siblings: `sync` already reports failure as a stdout result object (the good pattern to generalize); `export-graph` bypasses `_emit`.
- Guard that should have caught it: no test parses stdout with stderr discarded.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: [Workstream A] PR 2 (freshness/identity data and exit code 3 come from it; both rewrite `cli.py`)
- Schema after: none
- Gated on: AC8 maintainer decision (breaking vs `json2`)

## Tier and risk triggers
- Tier: M
- Risk triggers: breaking output contract (skills, frontier-audit-enhance collectors, and any scripts parsing current shapes)

## Verification
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`
- Manual: `zaxbygraph sql "select pr_number from pr_files" 2>/dev/null | python -m json.tool` should print the error object. `zaxbygraph open --format jsonl | head -3` should give 3 parseable lines.
- Environment: CI runs windows-latest and ubuntu-latest on Python 3.11 and 3.12.

## Related GitHub issues
- Tracking epic: #8

## Definition of done
- All ACs verified with evidence; PR body `Closes #<n>` with a `## Closure evidence` section listing each AC's argv and result, plus a migration note for consumers of the old shapes.

**Delivered: PR #12 — https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/pull/12** (Workstream B, PR 1 of 1 of epic #8)

**What changed**
- `search` now answers natural-language queries: tokens are porter-stemmed (`reconnect` finds `reconnection`), ranked by bm25 (title-weighted 10/1/3, recency tie-break), and comment hits merge into their parent item (`matching_comments` + `comment_snippet`) instead of a separate unranked list.
- AND→OR fallback: when the strict all-tokens pass finds fewer hits than the page, the query retries with stopwords removed and tokens OR-joined; `matched_mode` reports which pass produced the page.
- `total_matches` + `corpus_items` distinguish "no hits in N items" from an empty corpus; `index_stale` flags a database that predates the schema (reads never migrate).
- Schema v2→v3: both FTS tables rebuild in place with the porter tokenizer on the next `sync` — no resync; the migration rolls back whole on failure (regression-tested).

**Migration** — no action required: the first `sync` after upgrade rebuilds the FTS index in place (seconds at ~3k items). Until then, `search` reports `index_stale: true`. Once migrated, older zaxbygraph builds refuse the database (forward-only schema).

Full trace: 8 frozen acceptance checks (6 RED→GREEN at base `4789858`), 158-test suite green, three independent review/critic approvals. Checkpoint anchor receipts: [pre-implementation](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/issues/4#issuecomment-5969956751).

_Remediation issue. Generated from the first-class agent review of 2026-09-30 (maintainer-local report, informed by a GLM 5.3 long-session field report); claims re-checked against origin/main e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b on 2026-09-30. One issue = one PR. Tracking: #8._

## Summary
`search` is the command agents use for novelty and prior-art checks, and today it has a false-negative failure mode:
- `fts_query` quotes every whitespace token and joins them, which FTS5 treats as an implicit **AND of every word**, stopwords included.
- There's no stemming, so a natural-language query like `memory leak in websocket reconnect` returns **0 hits** even when a directly relevant issue exists ("WebSocket reconnect leaks memory").
- Results are ordered by `updated_at`, not relevance.
- Comment hits come back as a separate unranked list.

An empty result reads as "no prior art", the most dangerous wrong answer this tool can give. This PR:
- rebuilds FTS with the porter tokenizer
- ranks by bm25 (title-weighted) with recency as the tie-break
- adds an AND→OR fallback that reports which mode produced the results
- merges comment hits into their parent items
- reports `total_matches` and `corpus_items`, so "no hits in N items" is distinguishable from "empty corpus"

## Audit provenance
- Review finding P1-3.
- [repro] On a 3-row fixture:
  - `search("memory leak in websocket reconnect")` → `[]`, where `fts_query` produced `"memory" "leak" "in" "websocket" "reconnect"`.
  - `search("memory")` returned `[2, 1]`, most recently updated first, not by relevance.
  - `search("reconnect")` did not match the `reconnection` row.
- GLM field report: `search` quality wasn't assessed in that session, and the "0 hits, exit 0 read as no prior art" failure was hit twice by dispatched agents (there compounded by the wrong-DB issue, owned by [Workstream A] PR 2).
- Master re-check: STILL-PRESENT at e2ef892.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. Every token is quoted and implicitly ANDed. [query.py#L20](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L20)
   ```py
   return " ".join(quoted)
   ```
2. Results are ranked by recency. [query.py#L77](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L77)
   ```py
   sql += " ORDER BY items.updated_at DESC LIMIT ?"
   ```

  - expect: FAIL

- [ ] AC6: WHEN an existing pre-migration DB is opened THE SYSTEM SHALL rebuild both FTS tables with the new tokenizer through the migration framework, with no resync, and every existing row stays searchable. [P1-3, migrations]

  - expect: FAIL

issue_comments.body:
PR: #13 — feat: cold sync stops exhausting the rate limit and losing the listing

**What changed**

- The issues listing now streams one page per `gh` call and commits each
  page as it arrives, so a mid-listing 502/rate limit keeps every page
  already delivered together with its watermark — the next run resumes
  instead of restarting the corpus from zero (AC1).
- New default `--source graphql`: one aliased GraphQL query per listing
  page replaces the old ~5 REST calls per PR (comments, reviews, review
  comments, files, pull details); connections that overflow their page are
  flagged and completed through the per-item REST fallback (AC2/AC3).
  `--source rest` keeps the plain REST source. Patches always come from
  REST, so `--include-patches` still works.
- Rate limits are budgeted, not fatal: an exhausted core limit is slept out
  until the reported reset and retried; the window is reported as
  `rate_limit_remaining` / `rate_limit_reset_at` in the sync result and in
  `status` (new `sync_state` columns, schema v4) (AC4).
- After a completed full sync, a source deletion oracle marks stored items
  gone as `deleted`/`transferred` (rows kept, `fetch_log` trail); a 404/410
  on an item's own fetch marks it deleted too (AC5).

**How to use it**

`zaxbygraph sync --repo OWNER/REPO` — same command as before; GraphQL is
the default source. Add `--source rest` for the old behavior. No migration
action is needed for existing databases (schema v3→v4 applies automatically
on the next sync; the new columns are diagnostic).

**Evidence**

Eight frozen acceptance checks (authored independently before the fix,
proven RED on main and GREEN on this branch), full suite 188 tests OK, a
live two-source parity smoke against real GitHub (identical corpora;
GraphQL ~4.4× faster wall time on this repo), independent reviewer and
final-critic approvals. Full closure evidence in the PR body; trace
artifacts in `.agents/issue-traces/5-cold-sync-rate-limit-and-listing-loss/`.

No migration required. Merge is gated on maintainer approval.

item.body:
_Remediation issue. Generated from the first-class agent review of 2026-09-30 (maintainer-local report, informed by a GLM 5.3 long-session field report); claims re-checked against origin/main e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b on 2026-09-30. One issue = one PR. Tracking: #8._

## Summary
A cold sync of a ~3,000-item repo takes about 45 minutes and can exhaust the 5,000/h REST budget, which is how several copies of the same corpus ended up being rebuilt. There are two causes:

1. **Call volume.** Each PR costs one listing share plus up to 5 `gh` subprocess calls (issue comments, pull, reviews, review comments, files). About 3k items therefore means about 12k REST calls.
2. **All-or-nothing listing.** `gh api --paginate` output is buffered in full before the first item is ingested. A 502 or rate-limit error during listing throws away every page already downloaded, the watermark stays NULL, and the next run starts from zero.

This PR replaces per-item REST fan-out with GraphQL bulk pages (REST fallback only for connections that overflow). It also ingests and advances the watermark page by page, with a resumable full-sync cursor, and reads the rate-limit budget: it reports the budget and sleeps until reset instead of dying. Items that come back 404/410 are recorded as deleted or transferred.

## Audit provenance
- Review finding P2-1.
- [repro] With a fake `gh` that prints one valid issues page and then exits 1 with `gh: HTTP 502 Bad Gateway`, `sync_repo` raised `SyncError`, left **0 items ingested**, and left the watermark `None`.
- GLM field report, plus a prior-session lesson: a full sync used the entire 5,000/h budget and hit 502s mid-run. A ~3,000-item cold start takes about 45 min.
- Master re-check: STILL-PRESENT at e2ef892.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. Listing is one paginated call whose full output is buffered and parsed before anything is yielded. [github.py#L98](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/github.py#L98), [github.py#L75](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/github.py#L75)
   ```py
   data = self._api(f"repos/{self.slug}/issues?{qs}", paginate=True)
   ```
2. Every PR fans out into separate REST calls. [sync.py#L92-L99](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/sync.py#L92-L99)
   ```py
   pull_raw = source.get_pull(number)
   reviews = source.list_reviews(number)
   review_comments = source.list_review_comments(number)
   ```
3. No rate-limit headers are read. A 403/429 is classified from stderr text and aborts the run. [github.py#L50](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/github.py#L50)
   ```py
   def _api(self, path: str, paginate: bool = False) -> object:
   ```

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN the listing fails on page k+1 after pages 1..k were returned THE SYSTEM SHALL have ingested every item from pages 1..k, advanced the watermark past them, and resume from there on the next run. [P2-1]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_sync.StreamingTests.test_listing_failure_keeps_pages_already_returned -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_sync.py
  - why: RED at main: github.py#L98 buffers the full listing; the fake-`gh` repro left 0 items and a NULL watermark.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN syncing a fixture of 50 PRs, each with comments, reviews, review comments and files that fit their first page THE SYSTEM SHALL issue at most 3 GitHub calls. [P2-1]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_sync.GraphQLTests.test_bulk_page_call_budget -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_sync.py, tests/fixtures.py
  - why: RED at main: sync.py#L92-L99 issues about 5 calls per PR (about 250 for this fixture).
- [ ] AC3: WHEN a nested connection (comments, files, reviews) exceeds its first GraphQL page THE SYSTEM SHALL fetch the rest (GraphQL cursor or REST fallback) and store every record. [P2-1]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_sync.GraphQLTests.test_overflowing_connection_is_completed -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_sync.py
  - why: RED at main: no GraphQL path exists.
- [ ] AC4: WHEN the remaining rate-limit budget reaches the floor, or a secondary rate limit is returned THE SYSTEM SHALL sleep until the reported reset (injectable clock) and continue, and SHALL include `rate_limit{remaining, reset_at}` in the sync result and in `status`. [P2-1]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_sync.RateLimitTests.test_waits_for_reset_and_reports_budget -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_sync.py
  - why: RED at main: github.py#L50 reads no headers, and a rate limit aborts the run.
- [ ] AC5: WHEN a previously stored item returns 404/410, or is reported transferred THE SYSTEM SHALL set its state to `deleted` / `transferred` instead of leaving it stale. [P2-1]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_sync.StreamingTests.test_deleted_item_is_marked -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_sync.py
  - why: RED at main: there's no deletion handling.
- [ ] AC6: WHEN a full sync is followed by an incremental one, or a comment-only update arrives THE SYSTEM SHALL keep today's watermark semantics.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_sync.SyncTests.test_full_then_incremental_since tests.test_sync.SyncTests.test_comment_only_update_advances_watermark -v
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_sync.py
  - why: GREEN at main.
- [ ] AC7: WHEN a 429 hits mid-sync, or pagination duplicates a record THE SYSTEM SHALL keep earlier items and not raise on duplicates.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_sync.SyncTests.test_429_on_extra_get_leaves_earlier_items tests.test_sync.SyncTests.test_duplicate_comment_and_pr_file_from_pagination_do_not_raise -v
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_sync.py
  - why: GREEN at main.
- [ ] AC8: WHEN a PR's identity and watermark are stored THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the issue-list id and `updated_at`, not the pull's.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_store.StoreTests.test_pr_keeps_issue_id_and_list_watermark -v
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_store.py
  - why: GREEN at main; the GraphQL ids must map to the same identity rules.

## Constraints and invariants
- Auth stays through `gh` (`gh api graphql`). No token is stored. Stdlib only.
- Everything stored is still mechanically extracted, with no model involvement.
- Each item is still one transaction. The watermark never moves past an item that wasn't committed.
- `--include-patches` must still work. GraphQL doesn't expose patches, so REST `pulls/{n}/files` is used when patches are requested.
- The `GitHubSource` protocol stays mockable. Fixtures cover both GraphQL and REST shapes.

## Suggested approach (non-binding)
- A `GraphQLSource` that pages `repository.issues` / `pullRequests` ordered by `UPDATED_AT ASC`, with a `filterBy.since` equivalent. Nested `comments(first:100)`, `reviews(first:50)`, `files(first:100)`, `labels`, and `rateLimit{cost remaining resetAt}`.
- Streaming: yield page by page, and persist the page cursor in `sync_state.full_sync_cursor`.
- Keep `GhApiSource` as the fallback, selectable with `--source rest`.

## Scope
- In scope: all of the above.
- Out of scope:
  - timeline events and closing references (owned by [Workstream C] PR 2, which extends this query)
  - the sync lock (owned by [Workstream A] PR 2)

## Files expected to change
- src/zaxbygraph/github.py
- new src/zaxbygraph/graphql.py
- src/zaxbygraph/sync.py (hotspot)
- src/zaxbygraph/store.py
- src/zaxbygraph/db.py (a `sync_state` column, via migration)
- tests/test_sync.py, tests/fixtures.py

## Defect class and known siblings
- Class: operability and cost; all-or-nothing work unit.
- Known siblings: `list_releases` has the same buffered-paginate shape.
- Guard that should have caught it: no test injects a failure *inside* listing pagination, and no test counts calls.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: [Workstream A] PR 1 (migration framework, `last_error` on every path); [Workstream A] PR 2 (sync lock, so parallel worktrees cannot double-spend the budget)
- Schema after: [Workstream B] PR 1 (adds `sync_state` columns)
- Gated on: none

## Tier and risk triggers
- Tier: L
- Risk triggers: data completeness (identity mapping between GraphQL and REST), external API contract, rate limits

## Verification
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`
- Manual: `zaxbygraph sync --repo ZaxbyHub/opencode-swarm --force` into a scratch `--db`. Record wall time, call count and rate-limit usage against the ~45 min / ~12k-call baseline, and compare item, comment and file counts against a REST-built copy.
- Environment: CI runs windows-latest and ubuntu-latest on Python 3.11 and 3.12.

## Related GitHub issues
- Tracking epic: #8

## Definition of done
- All ACs verified with evidence; PR body `Closes #<n>` with a `## Closure evidence` section listing each AC's argv and result, plus the manual before/after numbers.

PR opened: https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/pull/14 — "what closed #N from timeline links, with provenance on every edge" (head e2e13ba962b57c447eb739da0174953fb6829b14).

**What changed** (schema v5): edges carry a `source` provenance column inside the unique key (`keyword` / `timeline` / `closing_ref` / `payload`); keyword closing links renamed to `closes_keyword`; `closes` is now backed by timeline `closed` events and PR `closingIssuesReferences`; new relations `cross_referenced` (repo-qualified for foreign sources), `closed_by_commit`, `merged_commit`, `merged_by`, `reverts` — so "what closed #N" is answerable from merge-commit auto-close, UI links, and timeline cross-references, and the graph joins to `git log` via `commit:<sha>` nodes.

Existing v4 databases migrate automatically on the next sync (forward-only, ids/counts preserved). Migration: automatic; no flags change. A v4 database read before its next sync reports `index_stale` in search results — run a sync to migrate.

item.body:
_Remediation issue. Generated from the first-class agent review of 2026-09-30 (maintainer-local report, informed by a GLM 5.3 long-session field report); claims re-checked against origin/main e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b on 2026-09-30. One issue = one PR. Tracking: #8._

## Summary
The graph layer (`related`, `path`, `item.edges`) went unused in a long real session, because the edges can't answer the question agents actually ask: "what closed #N?" The only `closes` edges come from closing-keyword regexes over bodies, comments and reviews. So these are all invisible:
- merge-commit auto-close
- links made in the GitHub UI or development sidebar
- timeline-only cross-references

The agent fell back to PR titles and `git log`. When the connectivity layer is known to be incomplete, agents rightly stop trusting it.

This PR:
- ingests timeline `closed` events (with `commit_id` / closer) and `cross-referenced` events
- ingests PR `closingIssuesReferences` as one more source
- records **provenance** on every edge in a new `edges.source` column
- keeps keyword links as a separate, weaker `closes_keyword` relation
- adds `merged_by`, `reverts` and item→commit edges, so the forge graph joins to `git log` and Graphify

## Audit provenance
- Review finding P1-2.
- GLM field report: "which PR actually closed #2950" was invisible to the graph and was answered from titles and `git log` instead. "A first-class version of this tool lives or dies on edge completeness."
- Maintainer's own promoted lesson `zmem-github-issues-pull-requests-api`: `closedByPullRequestsReferences` is frequently unpopulated. The timeline API (`cross-referenced` / `closed` events) is the reliable source, verified on ZaxbyHub/ragappv3 #308 → #305 in 2026-07. So `closingIssuesReferences` is **unverified** here and must be treated as one tagged source, not as ground truth.
- [repro] `GhApiSource` has no timeline method; no code path fetches timeline events.
- Master re-check: STILL-PRESENT at e2ef892.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. `closes` is derived only from keyword regexes. [extract.py#L6](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/extract.py#L6), [extract.py#L41](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/extract.py#L41)
   ```py
   _CLOSE_KW = r"(?:close[sd]?|fix(?:e[sd])?|resolve[sd]?)"
   ```
2. Edges carry no provenance beyond a free-text `evidence` and a constant confidence. [schema.sql#L130](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/schema.sql#L130)
   ```sql
   confidence TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (confidence IN ('EXTRACTED')),
   ```
3. The source protocol has no timeline fetch. [github.py#L32](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/github.py#L32)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN an issue's timeline contains a `closed` event carrying a `commit_id` THE SYSTEM SHALL store an edge `item:<issue> closed_by_commit commit:<sha>` with `source='timeline'`. WHEN that commit is a stored PR's `merge_commit` THE SYSTEM SHALL also store `item:<pr> closes item:<issue>` with `source='timeline'`. [P1-2]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_edges.TimelineEdgeTests.test_closed_event_with_commit_links_pr_and_issue -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_edges.py (new), tests/fixtures.py
  - why: RED at main: there's no timeline ingestion (github.py#L32 protocol).
- [ ] AC2: WHEN an issue's timeline contains a `cross-referenced` event from a same-repo PR or issue THE SYSTEM SHALL store `cross_referenced` with `source='timeline'`. WHEN the source is another repo THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the edge with a repo-qualified node id, never attaching it to a same-numbered local item. [P1-2]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_edges.TimelineEdgeTests.test_cross_referenced_same_and_foreign_repo -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_edges.py
  - why: RED at main: no timeline ingestion.
- [ ] AC3: WHEN a PR body says "Fixes #12" THE SYSTEM SHALL store `closes_keyword` with `source='keyword'` (renamed from `closes`), and `closes` SHALL be reserved for timeline or closing-reference-backed links. [P1-2]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_edges.ProvenanceTests.test_keyword_edges_are_labelled_weaker -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_edges.py
  - why: RED at main: keyword matches are stored as `closes` with no source (extract.py#L41).
- [ ] AC4: WHEN a PR has `closingIssuesReferences` THE SYSTEM SHALL store each as `closes` with `source='closing_ref'`. WHEN timeline and closing-ref disagree THE SYSTEM SHALL keep both edges, each with its own source. [P1-2]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_edges.ProvenanceTests.test_closing_refs_stored_with_own_source -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_edges.py
  - why: RED at main: not fetched.
- [ ] AC5: WHEN a merged PR is ingested THE SYSTEM SHALL store `merged_by` (actor) and `item → commit` (merge commit) edges. WHEN a PR title starts with `Revert "` or its body contains `This reverts commit <sha>` THE SYSTEM SHALL store a `reverts` edge. [P1-2]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_edges.CommitEdgeTests.test_merged_by_commit_and_reverts -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_edges.py
  - why: RED at main: none of these relations exist.
- [ ] AC6: WHEN a pre-migration DB is opened THE SYSTEM SHALL add `edges.source` through the migration framework, backfill existing keyword edges as `closes_keyword` / `source='keyword'`, and keep every other edge. [P1-2, migrations]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_migrations.MigrationTests.test_edges_source_migration_backfills_keyword_edges -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_migrations.py
  - why: RED at main: no `source` column (schema.sql#L130).
- [ ] AC7: WHEN a body references another repo's `owner/repo#N` or URL THE SYSTEM SHALL never attach a keyword edge to the same-numbered local item.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_extract.ClosingTests.test_cross_repo_url_does_not_attach_locally tests.test_extract.ClosingTests.test_cross_repo_does_not_poison_bare_hash -v
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_extract.py
  - why: GREEN at main.
- [ ] AC8: WHEN a destination item is upserted THE SYSTEM SHALL keep inbound mentions, and a review body's closing keyword SHALL still produce an edge.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_store.StoreTests.test_inbound_mention_survives_destination_upsert tests.test_extract.ReviewBodyTests.test_review_body_closes -v
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_store.py, tests/test_extract.py
  - why: GREEN at main; the relation rename must preserve this behavior under `closes_keyword`.

## Constraints and invariants
- Still EXTRACTED only: every new edge comes straight from a GitHub API field, never inferred.
- Timeline fields are fetched inside the GraphQL page query from [Workstream C] PR 1 (`timelineItems(itemTypes:[CLOSED_EVENT, CROSS_REFERENCED_EVENT])`), not as a new per-item REST fan-out.
- Consumers get the `closes` → `closes_keyword` rename in the release notes and the skill's "Interpreting `closes` correctly" section.

## Suggested approach (non-binding)
- Extend the C-01 GraphQL query with `timelineItems` and `closingIssuesReferences(first:25)`.
- `extract.edges_from_timeline(repo, number, events)` → tuples with `source`.
- Migration: `ALTER TABLE edges ADD COLUMN source TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'keyword'`, rename the existing rows, and add `source` to the unique key.

## Scope
- In scope: all of the above.
- Out of scope:
  - the `what_closed` / `file_history` query commands built on these edges (owned by [Workstream D] PR 1)
  - repo-qualified node ids in `export-graph` beyond what AC2 needs

## Files expected to change
- src/zaxbygraph/extract.py
- src/zaxbygraph/graphql.py
- src/zaxbygraph/store.py
- src/zaxbygraph/schema.sql (hotspot)
- src/zaxbygraph/db.py (migration, hotspot)
- src/zaxbygraph/query.py (`related`/`path` relation sets)
- skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md
- docs/schema.md
- tests/test_edges.py (new); tests/test_migrations.py, tests/fixtures.py

## Defect class and known siblings
- Class: incomplete evidence presented as a complete graph.
- Known siblings: `path` treats only `touches|closes|mentions` as structural (it must include the new relations); `export-graph` node ids aren't repo-qualified.
- Guard that should have caught it: no fixture includes a UI-linked or auto-closed issue.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: [Workstream C] PR 1 (GraphQL page query)
- Schema after: [Workstream C] PR 1
- Gated on: none

## Tier and risk triggers
- Tier: M
- Risk triggers: schema/migrations, contract change (relation rename)

## Verification
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`
- Manual: on a scratch sync of ZaxbyHub/ragappv3, `item 308` must show a `source='timeline'` link to #305, the known-good case from the zmem lesson.
- Environment: CI runs windows-latest and ubuntu-latest on Python 3.11 and 3.12.

## Related GitHub issues

item.body:
_Remediation issue. Generated from the first-class agent review of 2026-09-30 (maintainer-local report, informed by a GLM 5.3 long-session field report); claims re-checked against origin/main e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b on 2026-09-30. One issue = one PR. Tracking: #8._

## Summary
zaxbygraph is a CLI plus a skill, not an MCP server, so every agent must work out for itself:
- which cwd the graph lives in
- the column names
- the output shapes
- whether an error went to stderr
- whether the data is fresh

It then re-learns all of that in every session. This PR adds `zaxbygraph mcp`, a stdio MCP server that is a thin adapter over `query.py` with no logic of its own:
- typed tools, each returning the [Workstream A] PR 3 envelope, including structured errors
- the schema served as a resource instead of a relative doc link
- repo resolution through the [Workstream A] PR 2 slug-keyed store: explicit `repo` argument → MCP roots (when the client sends them) → the server's cwd git remote
- a non-blocking background sync when data is stale

It also turns the proven hand-written queries into first-class tools (`pr_overlap`, `file_history`, `what_closed`), with the same commands on the CLI.

## Audit provenance
- Review findings P1-1 (all) and the product-query items.
- [repro] `zaxbygraph mcp` → `invalid choice: 'mcp'`, exit 2. Nothing in `src/` or in the maintainer's `~/.claude.json` registers an MCP server.
- GLM field report:
  - The strongest single moment was a hand-written `pr_files … WHERE number IN (…)` collision check ("productize the collision check").
  - A first `pr_files` query failed on a guessed column name.
  - Output shapes were re-learned across sessions.
  - Every subagent prompt had to hard-code `cd <repo root>`.
- Master re-check: STILL-PRESENT at e2ef892.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. There is no MCP entry point. The CLI's subcommands are fixed. [cli.py#L212](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/cli.py#L212)
   ```py
   sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
   ```
2. Repo and DB resolution depend on the process cwd. [cli.py#L58](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/cli.py#L58)
   ```py
   path = Path(args.db) if getattr(args, "db", None) else default_db_path()
   ```
3. There are no overlap, file-history or closure queries; agents write them by hand in `sql`. [query.py#L196](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/e2ef892ab11cf54a9aac8a3b058b49b4991e9c4b/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L196) (`churn` is the only file-level query)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN a client sends `initialize` then `tools/list` over stdio to `zaxbygraph mcp` THE SYSTEM SHALL return a protocol-conformant response listing `graph_status, search, get_item, related, path, pr_overlap, file_history, what_closed, open_items, sql, sync`, each with a JSON input schema. [P1-1]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_mcp.McpProtocolTests.test_initialize_and_tools_list -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_mcp.py (new)
  - why: RED at main: the repro exited 2 with `invalid choice: 'mcp'`.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN a tool is called without `repo` from a server whose cwd is a linked worktree THE SYSTEM SHALL resolve the same slug-keyed DB as the main checkout. WHEN the client supplies roots THE SYSTEM SHALL prefer them over the server cwd. [P1-1]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_mcp.McpResolutionTests.test_worktree_and_roots_resolve_same_db -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_mcp.py
  - why: RED at main: no server; the CLI resolves per checkout (cli.py#L58).
- [ ] AC3: WHEN a tool is called for a repo with no corpus, or with invalid SQL THE SYSTEM SHALL return a tool result with `isError: true` and the envelope error object (`code`, `message`, `hint`), and SHALL NOT create a DB. [P1-1]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_mcp.McpErrorTests.test_no_corpus_and_bad_sql_are_structured_errors -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_mcp.py
  - why: RED at main: no server.
- [ ] AC4: WHEN `pr_overlap` is called with PR numbers THE SYSTEM SHALL return each pair's shared file paths (an empty list for disjoint pairs). WHEN `file_history` is called with a path THE SYSTEM SHALL return the PRs that touched it, newest first, each with the issues it closed. WHEN `what_closed` is called with an issue THE SYSTEM SHALL return closing PRs and commits with each edge's `source`. The same three SHALL exist as CLI commands. [P1-1]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_query.ProductQueryTests.test_pr_overlap_file_history_what_closed -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_query.py
  - why: RED at main: these queries don't exist (only `churn`, query.py#L196).
- [ ] AC5: WHEN a read tool is called and `freshness.age_s` exceeds the configured threshold THE SYSTEM SHALL answer immediately from the current data, start one locked incremental sync in the background, and report `freshness.refreshing: true`. [P1-1]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_mcp.McpFreshnessTests.test_stale_read_answers_now_and_refreshes_in_background -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_mcp.py
  - why: RED at main: no server, no staleness policy.
- [ ] AC6: WHEN `resources/read` is called for `zaxbygraph://schema` THE SYSTEM SHALL return the same DDL and column notes as the `schema` CLI command. [P1-1]
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_mcp.McpResourceTests.test_schema_resource_matches_cli -v
  - expect: FAIL
  - files: tests/test_mcp.py
  - why: RED at main: no server.
- [ ] AC7: WHEN the maintainer records the implementation choice THE SYSTEM SHALL implement it: hand-written stdlib JSON-RPC (keeps zero dependencies) or an optional `zaxbygraph[mcp]` extra on the official Python SDK. The staleness threshold defaults to the recorded value (proposed 15 min).
  - class: NON-EXECUTABLE(PRODUCT_DECISION)
- [ ] AC8: WHEN SQL arrives through the MCP `sql` tool THE SYSTEM SHALL apply the same read-only guards as the CLI (prefix, stacked statements, `query_only`, authorizer).
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m unittest tests.test_query.QueryTests.test_readonly_conn_denies_pragma_query_only_off tests.test_query.QueryTests.test_readonly_conn_denies_load_extension tests.test_query.QueryTests.test_sql_rejects_stacked_statement_hidden_in_string_literal -v
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_query.py
  - why: GREEN at main; the MCP tool must reuse `connect_readonly_query` / `assert_read_sql`, not reimplement them.

## Constraints and invariants
- The server is an adapter: every tool calls an existing `query.py` / `paths.py` function, and stdout carries only protocol frames (logs go to stderr).
- The `sync` tool never blocks the caller. It returns a job id, and `graph_status` reports progress. It uses the [Workstream A] PR 2 lock.
- Tool results are bounded: every list tool takes `limit` and returns `truncated` / `next_cursor`, and `get_item` takes `max_body_chars`.
- The skill documents both surfaces, and when MCP is configured the skill tells agents to prefer it.

## Suggested approach (non-binding)
- `src/zaxbygraph/mcp_server.py` implementing `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `resources/list`, `resources/read`, and `roots/list` handling.
- Registration examples for Claude Code (`claude mcp add zaxbygraph -- zaxbygraph mcp`) and opencode in the README.
- Background refresh: a daemon thread per repo, guarded by the sync lock.

## Scope
- In scope: all of the above.
- Out of scope:
  - remote/HTTP transport
  - write tools of any kind beyond `sync`

## Files expected to change
- new src/zaxbygraph/mcp_server.py
- src/zaxbygraph/cli.py (hotspot, `mcp` / `overlap` / `file-history` / `what-closed` subcommands)
- src/zaxbygraph/query.py
- pyproject.toml (optional extra, per AC7)
- README.md
- skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md
- tests/test_mcp.py (new); tests/test_query.py

## Defect class and known siblings
- Class: missing typed agent surface; implicit, cwd-dependent contract.
- Known siblings: frontier-audit-enhance Phase 1 collectors currently shell out to the CLI and could switch to the MCP tools.
- Guard that should have caught it: none, because this is a new surface.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: [Workstream A] PR 3 (envelope, error contract, `schema`); [Workstream C] PR 2 (`what_closed` needs timeline and closing-ref edges)
- Schema after: none
- Gated on: AC7 maintainer decision

## Tier and risk triggers
- Tier: L
- Risk triggers: new public interface, concurrency (background sync thread)

## Verification
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`
- Manual:
  1. `claude mcp add zaxbygraph -- zaxbygraph mcp`.
  2. From a Claude Code session in a ragappv3 worktree, call `graph_status` and `pr_overlap` for two open PRs without passing `repo`.
  3. Confirm that the resolved DB is the shared one and that no new DB file appeared.
- Environment: CI runs windows-latest and ubuntu-latest on Python 3.11 and 3.12.

## Related GitHub issues
- Tracking epic: #8

## Definition of done
- All ACs verified with evidence; PR body `Closes #<n>` with a `## Closure evidence` section listing each AC's argv and result, plus the manual Claude Code session check.
