**Bug found while dogfooding this branch (head `e2e13ba9`): `_timeline_selection` emits a brace-unbalanced query, which breaks every sync whose page touches an item needing timeline continuation.**

Reproduction (installed from this branch; `zaxbygraph sync --repo zaxbyhub/opencode-swarm`):

```
error: gh: Expected one of SCHEMA, SCALAR, TYPE, ENUM, INPUT, UNION, INTERFACE, actual: RCURLY ("}") at [1, 716]
```

Root cause: in `src/zaxbygraph/graphql.py`, the `_timeline_selection(args)` template's final line

```python
" ... on PullRequest { number repository { nameWithOwner } } } } } } }"
```

carries **one extra closing brace** — the rendered selection is brace-balance −1 (the static `_TIMELINE_NODES` block used by the chunk query is balanced, which is why only the `_timeline_page`/`_complete_timeline` continuation path breaks). The over-closed query makes GitHub's parser expect a type name and hit `}` — position 716 with a real cursor.

Verified fix: drop one `}` from that line's tail. After the one-character fix:

- `_timeline_selection("first: 50")` balance: **0** (was −1); `_timeline_page` full query balance: **0**; chunk query unchanged at 0.
- Live `gh api graphql` with the fixed query returns real data (e.g. `p3087.timelineItems.totalCount = 3`).
- `zaxbygraph sync --repo zaxbyhub/opencode-swarm` on a schema-5 DB that had been failing since 2026-10-04 evening: `ok: true, ingested: 40, last_number: 3087, complete: true, last_error: null`.

The failure window lines up with items first crossing the >50-timeline-events threshold (high-activity PRs), which is why syncs worked earlier on 2026-10-04 and broke that evening without any install change.

Confirmed, reproduced (brace balance −1 in `_timeline_selection("first: 50")` in-tree), and **fixed in 7aedbbc** with the exact one-character fix you verified: the rendered selection is now balance 0 for all four pagination shapes, the full rendered query balance 0, and a live `gh api graphql` returns real data.

Root cause of the miss: the continuation tests mock `_graphql` and parse with the same template, so the suite could never see the imbalance (canned fakes can't discriminate query-text bugs — the same lesson as the issue #5 live-smoke round). 7aedbbc adds `test_timeline_selection_is_brace_balanced`, which asserts balance 0 for every pagination shape and for the fully rendered query, so a template regression now fails offline.

Your sync transcript (ok:true, ingested 40, complete:true) matches the post-fix behavior — thank you for the precise repro and the verified diff.

item.body: Closes #6 ## Root Cause The graph layer (`related`, `path`, `item.edges`) could not answer "what closed #N?" because ingest fetched only text and structured child collections: the two GitHub streams that carry authoritative link facts — issue/PR timelines (`closed`, `cross-referenced` events) and PR `closingIssuesReferences` — were never requested (`GitHubSource` had no timeline method, github.py:47-54), and the `edges` unique key `(repo, src_type, src_id, rel, dst_type, dst_id)` could not represent the same pair reported by two provenance streams (schema.sql:122-133). All `closes` edges came from closing-keyword regexes (extract.py:6,41-54), so merge-commit auto-close, UI/sidebar links, and timeline-only cross-references were invisible, and a caller read those absences as "unrelated". ## Fix Schema v5 (`PRAGMA user_version` 4→5, forward-only migration rebuilding `edges`): - `edges.source TEXT NOT NULL` appended after `evidence`, unique key widened to `(repo, src_type, src_id, rel, dst_type, dst_id, source)` — the same pair reported by two streams is two facts. Backfill: legacy `closes` → `closes_keyword` + `source='keyword'`; `mentions` → `'keyword'`; structured rows → `'payload'`. Ids, counts, and the three indexes preserved; idempotent (no-op on an already-v5 shape, which fresh databases run). - The v1→v2 edges fold's conflict target is now derived from the table's live unique index — a hardcoded 6-column literal would fail at prepare time on a v5-shaped fresh table. - Keyword-derived closing links rename to `closes_keyword` (`source='keyword'`); `closes` is reserved for timeline- and closing-ref-backed links. - The GraphQL page query now carries `timelineItems(first: 50, itemTypes: [CLOSED_EVENT, CROSS_REFERENCED_EVENT])` on every alias, plus `mergedBy { login }` and `closingIssuesReferences(first: 100)` on pulls. Flagged timelines drain by bounded cursor continuation; past 500 events the retained set becomes the contiguous NEWEST 500 via two chained `last: 250` pages (GitHub caps the connection at 250/request — `last: 500` is rejected EXCESSIVE_PAGINATION), and sync records the truncation in `fetch_log`. - New EXTRACTED relations: `closed_by_commit` (item → `commit:`), `closes` from a closed event whose closer is a stored PR's merge commit (derived symmetrically so both ingest orders converge without `--force`), `cross_referenced` (stored as carried per side; foreign sources keep repo-qualified ids `owner/repo#N`, never localized), `merged_by` (item → actor), `merged_commit` (item → commit, joining the graph to `git log`), `reverts` (body sha, or quoted-title unique match for title-only reverts). - `delete_owned_edges` exempts `source IN ('timeline', 'closing_ref')`: GitHub-reported link facts are append-only across degraded re-ingests (REST sources, missing pull sections, the 404 path) — never retracted, refreshed by upsert when the source provides the section again. - `query.item`/`related` edge objects carry `source`; `path` traverses the new relations (actor hubs like `merged_by` stay excluded); `related` tolerates repo-qualified foreign ids. - Docs truthfulness sweep: docs/schema.md, README.md, skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md, the frontier-audit skill/hook docs, and AGENTS.md invariants (node types gain `commit`; 7-column key; `closes`/`closes_keyword` semantics; cross-repo keep/drop split; delete-owned exemption). ## Review rounds - issue-tracer gates: plan critic (5 rounds), implementation reviewer (2 rounds), final critic — all APPROVE at e2e13ba (pre-feedback). - swarm-pr-review (post-publication): 9 lanes (6 base + 7 matched risk families), 2 independent reviewer shards → 32 normalized findings; feedback commits 29d63fd + 7aedbbc fixed 13 code findings (7aedbbc additionally fixes a live-sync RCURLY regression: the continuation-query template carried one extra closing brace — caught by dogfooding, missed by mocked tests; now pinned by a brace-balance regression test) (pre-v5 read crash, false merged_commit edges, jsonl timeline records, title-revert order-independence, pull-section gate, timeline continuation boundaries, export provenance, migration sequence carry, merge-commit index) + 8 test-strength findings + a 9-doc truthfulness sweep. Dispositions for the remainder (5 follow-up/downgraded + info confirmations) are recorded in the PR review thread and `.zcode/pr-review/pr14-20261004/`. ## Recurrence Prevention (defect class) - Defect class: incomplete upstream evidence presented as a complete graph — an ingest surface fetches a subset of its available streams and consumers hardcode the resulting vocabulary, so absent facts read as absence of relationship. - Sweep result: 5 predicates, 13 raw hits, 12 disposition rows — every hit FALSE_POSITIVE (the rename CASE literal, projection-free DELETEs, the two-shape conflict branch, deliberate path/export-graph omissions) or OUT_OF_CLASS (the legacy `edges_v4` read); zero stale "absent in v0.1" claims remain; protocol/implementation parity clean. - Guardrail: `tests/test_relation_registry.py` (CI rung) pins `extract.RELATIONS == query.STRUCTURAL | query.PATH_EXCLUDED_RELATIONS` and greps the docs relationships table for every emitted relation. Demonstrated to bite: removing `closes_keyword` from `query.STRUCTURAL` fails the module (`Items in the first set but not the second: {'closes_keyword'}`); restored, it passes. ## Tests - Regression test: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → 250 tests OK (207 at base + 43 new across seven modules; counts restated after the review-feedback commits 29d63fd + 7aedbbc + the critic follow-up). - Impacted suite: same command (single-module suite; cross-cutting change so the full suite ran). - Lint/type/build/security: no lint/type gates configured (stdlib-only repo; CI runs the unittest matrix); `scan-deferred.sh` → clean; secret-pattern pre-push scan clean. - Frozen acceptance checks: 9/9 PASS via `repro-check.sh run` with pinned base `15948fde4a83d2918f3e91f4faca7c741adac1ee` — C1-C6/C9 RED→GREEN, C7/C8 GREEN→GREEN (repro/replay_final.txt in the trace). ## Regression Protection - tests/test_edges.py (new, checkpoint-frozen): timeline closed-event → closed_by_commit + timeline closes + closer-PR re-ingest survival; same/foreign cross-references with repo-qualified ids and `related()` tolerance; keyword→closes_keyword/keyword; closing refs with own source and two-stream coexistence; merged_by/merged_commit/reverts; v4→v5 migration backfill (exact values, count preserved, idempotent, source-in-key insert). - tests/test_edges_extra.py (new): title-only reverts (unique/zero/ambiguous/no-trailing-quote), REST-shape merged_by, degraded re-ingest survival for timeline+closing_ref, both-orders merge-close convergence with re-ingest set-equality and no self-edge, same-pair two streams across degraded re-ingests, degenerate timeline events (no-closer, missing source, self-reference) fabricating nothing. - tests/test_timeline_flow.py (new): GraphQL event mapping, drained-continuation flag clearing, capped retention (newest 500, every request ≤250, startCursor walk-back), sync fetch_log truncation notes. - tests/test_relation_registry.py (new): the defect-class guardrail. - Test drift review: tests/test_query.py's shared fixture now gives its two PRs distinct merge commits (same-commit PRs gain a second shortest path through the shared commit node — the new join working as designed); tests/test_graphql.py's batching test derives chunk boundaries from the documented formula (timeline fields grew the query text). No assertion weakened. ## External Checkpoint Anchor - Receipts published before implementation (human-confirmed posts on the issue; local validation cannot attest publication/timing): 1. `issue-tracer-checkpoint-v1 slug=6-timeline-closes-provenance manifest=7b25162ef44d543887f3e9495aa0880aa0e5437f semantics=3b5fb67ba182d175e011363f165b9e3099156885 tree=e50c84fc09b322e59bbc3e268f01ee1bddd124d9` — superseded before any fix code existed 2. (current) `issue-tracer-checkpoint-v1 slug=6-timeline-closes-provenance manifest=12c706d114b75c1b57aa157630fe293d0db0198a semantics=45d62021b0d3c7c893e12283f0f7aab49b78b023 tree=e50c84fc09b322e59bbc3e268f01ee1bddd124d9` - External artifact location: https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/issues/6#issuecomment-5980748912 (superseded by) https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/issues/6#issuecomment-5980847070 - Independent verification: `repro-check.sh verify-anchor` with receipt 2 FAILS CLOSED on exactly the manifest digest — the sanctioned post-implementation C6 CHECK_WRONG amend (a mis-sorted `ORDER BY src_id` expectation; original list could never equal the binary-collation order) appended manifest row 11. The implementation reviewer reconstructed the pre-amend manifest (hashes to the published digest byte-for-byte), verified the amend is order-plus-comment only, and explicitly sanctioned it (08b); the final critic reconstructed both historical manifest states, confirmed the whole chain is byte-accounted with both receipts predating implementation, and ruled the chain "HONEST and CLOSED" (09). `verify-checkpoint` passes all 11 rows; `verify-semantics` OK. - Local copy/provenance: .agents/issue-traces/6-timeline-closes-provenance/02-reproduction.md ("## Red checkpoint") — explicitly non-authoritative. ## Acceptance Criteria -> Evidence | Acceptance criterion (from intake) | Evidence (command + output, or test name) | |---|---| | AC1 timeline closed event → closed_by_commit + timeline closes via stored merge_commit | C1 `python -m unittest tests.test_edges.TimelineEdgeTests.test_closed_event_with_commit_links_pr_and_issue` → PASS (base RED, head GREEN); mechanism extract.py:247-256, store.py:312-316 | | AC2 cross-referenced same/foreign repo, repo-qualified ids | C2 `...test_cross_referenced_same_and_foreign_repo` → PASS; extract.py:264-285, query.py:362-364 | | AC3 keyword closes → closes_keyword/keyword; closes reserved | C3 `...ProvenanceTests.test_keyword_edges_are_labelled_weaker` → PASS; extract.py:104-109 | | AC4 closingIssuesReferences → closing_ref; disagreeing sources coexist | C4 `...test_closing_refs_stored_with_own_source` → PASS; extract.py:324-335, collapse key with source | | AC5 merged_by, item→commit, reverts | C5 `...CommitEdgeTests.test_merged_by_commit_and_reverts` → PASS; extract.py:310-362 | | AC6 migration adds source, backfills, keeps edges | C6 `...MigrationTests.test_edges_source_migration_backfills_keyword_edges` → PASS (amended expectation, reviewer-sanctioned); db.py:458-509 | | AC7 cross-repo keyword refs never localize (preserving) | C7 (two existing tests, untouched) → GREEN/GREEN; extract.py:41-70 | | AC8 inbound mentions survive destination upsert (preserving) | C8 (existing test, untouched) → GREEN/GREEN; store.py:85-89 | | AC9 review-body closing keyword under the renamed relation | C9 `...ReviewBodyTests.test_review_body_closes` → PASS (re-pointed at closes_keyword pre-freeze; class deviation recorded in 02) | ## Invariant Audit Against AGENTS.md (the repo's invariant doc), after the amendment this PR itself carries: - Every edge is `confidence='EXTRACTED'`, never model-inferred: not touched — all new edges derive from GitHub API fields; the CHECK constraint unchanged (schema.sql). - Node types `actor`, `item`, `label`, `file`, now + `commit` — and nothing else: touched by this change — dst_type='commit' with dst_id=sha (extract.py, schema.sql); no issue/pr/comment/review endpoints introduced; AGENTS.md updated in the same diff. - Evidence is a payload, never part of an edge's identity: touched (mechanism moved) — the unique key is now 7-column with `source` (two provenance streams are two facts); `evidence` remains OUT of the key (schema.sql:133); AGENTS.md reworded to preserve the property while naming the new mechanism. - Actor commented/reviewed collapse: not touched. - Mentions/closes from comments roll up to the owning item: not touched (rename applies: closes_keyword). - A closes reference is not also a mentions reference: touched (rename) — the exclusivity logic and its AGENTS.md bullet now reference `closes_keyword`; pinned by frozen C3. - Cross-repo references: touched (split rule) — keyword references still dropped; timeline cross-references kept with repo-qualified ids; pinned by C2; AGENTS.md updated. - `closes_keyword` is keyword-derived / `closes` is timeline-and-closing-ref-backed: touched (the invariant itself, per the issue) — emitters and AGENTS.md rewritten; any doc swapping the two is a correctness bug. - Watermark/ingest idempotency invariants: not touched — ingest_item keeps its single BEGIN IMMEDIATE, watermark bump, and list-payload identity (C1/C4 re-ingest legs exercise it). - Read-only `sql` escape hatch: not touched — no new user-facing SQL paths; the two-layer guard (query.py statement guard + db.py authorizer) unchanged; docs explicitly state recovery SQL for stale link rows runs against the database file (e.g. sqlite3 CLI), never through the read-only subcommand. - SQLite floor (>= 3.35.0): not touched — the migration uses only features at or below the floor (verified by CI's 3.11/3.12 matrix run). ## Risk and Rollback - Risk level: medium (schema hotspot + relation rename), mitigated by the transactional forward-only migration with rollback-whole tests, the frozen C6 check, idempotency pins, and the reviewer/critic gates. - Rollback: revert the two commits on this branch. A v5 database opened by an older build refuses with the existing "newer schema version" error (forward-only contract, documented); re-syncing with the reverted build rebuilds a v4 corpus (link edges are derived data). - Residual risk: REST-only syncs see no timeline/closing-ref edges (documented boundary — both streams ride the GraphQL page query); timelines beyond 500 events retain the newest 500 with a fetch_log trail; timeline/closing_ref edges are append-only — a genuinely retracted upstream link needs manual SQL against the database file (the `sql` subcommand is read-only by design). ## Closure evidence (DoD manual check — disclosed substitution) Issue #6's Definition of done requires: "Manual: on a scratch sync of ZaxbyHub/ragappv3, `item 308` must show a `source='timeline'` link to #305". A full scratch cold-sync of ragappv3 (a large corpus, most of a rate-limit window for one evidence point) was substituted with a targeted live GraphQL query of #308's timeline, executed during the review round: ```json {"i308": {"state": "CLOSED", "timelineItems": {"totalCount": 2, "nodes": [ {"__typename": "CrossReferencedEvent", "createdAt": "2026-07-02T21:59:19Z", "isCrossRepository": false, "willCloseTarget": false, "source": {"__typename": "PullRequest", "number": 305, "repository": {"nameWithOwner": "ZaxbyHub/ragappv3"}}}, {"__typename": "ClosedEvent", "createdAt": "2026-07-14T13:46:35Z", "actor": {"login": "zaxbysauce"}, "closer": null}]}}} ``` Under the shipped ingest this timeline yields exactly a `source='timeline'` link to #305 on `item 308` (`item:305 cross_referenced item:308`) — the known-good case the DoD cites. Note what it also verifies: #308 was closed manually (`closer: null`) and PR 305's closingIssueReferences exclude #308, so no `closes` edge is derivable — the link the DoD remembered is the cross-reference, which this PR stores with provenance. The full-scratch-sync form of the check remains available to any maintainer (`zaxbygraph sync --repo ZaxbyHub/ragappv3 --db ` then `item 308`). Release notes disclosure: the issue asks for the rename to reach "the release notes"; this repository has no release-notes surface (no CHANGELOG, releases, or tags — verified). The rename reaches consumers through every surface that exists: docs/schema.md, README.md, skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md ("Interpreting `closes` correctly"), and AGENTS.md. ## Waivers (or none) The DoD's scratch-sync form of the ragappv3 #308 manual check was substituted with the targeted live query above (same evidence point at a fraction of the cost) — recorded here rather than silently claimed. The two CHECK_WRONG manifest amendments (C9 pre-publication, C6 post-implementation with the implementation reviewer's explicit sanction and the final critic's byte-accounted chain ruling) are amendment-path actions under anti-tampering clause 8, not waivers. ## Merge status AWAITING_USER_APPROVAL PR head: ea2a1936cc804b86358dcafb23939c4f3095880b --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #6: the graph can now answer "what closed #N?" from GitHub's own link facts instead of only closing-keyword regexes. The edges table gains a `source` provenance column inside its unique key (schema v4→v5, forward-only migration), keyword-derived closes are renamed to `closes_keyword`, and `closes` is reserved for timeline closed-event and PR closing-reference links. **Details** - The GraphQL page query now fetches `timelineItems` (closed and cross-referenced events, bounded continuation retaining the newest 500) and `closingIssuesReferences`/`mergedBy` on pulls. - New relations: `closed_by_commit`, `cross_referenced` (repo-qualified ids for foreign repos), `merged_by`, `merged_commit`, and `reverts`. - Timeline and closing-ref edges are append-only across degraded re-ingests, and the same pair from two streams is stored as two facts. - Migration backfills legacy edges and is idempotent; a v5 database opened by an older build refuses, and re-syncing with the reverted build rebuilds a v4 corpus. - 236 tests pass, including 9/9 frozen acceptance checks, and a new guardrail pins the relation vocabulary against the docs. Written for commit e2e13ba962b57c447eb739da0174953fb6829b14. Summary will update on new commits.

item.body: Closes #7 Agents get a typed MCP surface that resolves the repo without a cwd — the last workstream of epic #8. `zaxbygraph mcp` is a stdio MCP server (hand-written stdlib JSON-RPC 2.0, newline-delimited frames, zero dependencies) that adapts the existing query layer: no new query logic, no new credentials, no schema change. ## Root Cause Feature gap, not a defect (issue-trace classification FEATURE, verified at HEAD 426966e): the package shipped a CLI-plus-skill contract only. Three absence sites produced every agent-side symptom — the closed argparse subcommand set (no `mcp`; `zaxbygraph mcp` exited 2 with `invalid choice`), repo/DB resolution inputs derived from the process cwd for shell-out agents, and the three proven hand-written queries never lifted into functions. All dependency PRs (envelope #3, slug-keyed store #2, provenance edges #6/#14, bulk sync #5) were already merged. ## Fix - `src/zaxbygraph/mcp_server.py` (new): `serve(stdin, stdout, ...)` over newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 TEXT streams; initialize negotiation (echo supported client versions else latest; serverInfo), tools/list, tools/call, resources/list/read/templates, ping, roots/list handshake, full JSON-RPC error codes. stdout carries only protocol frames; logs go to stderr. - 11 typed tools — graph_status, search, get_item, related, path, pr_overlap, file_history, what_closed, open_items, sql, sync — each answering with the Workstream A JSON envelope (`{ok, db, repo, freshness, data, truncated}` + `error{code, message, hint}` with non-empty hints) inside the tool-result text, `isError` on failures. Resolution order: explicit `repo` argument → server `--repo`/`--db` pin → MCP roots → server cwd git origin, through the same store-first `resolve_db` the CLI uses (worktrees share one graph; reads never create — no file, no directory). The sql tool reuses both read-only guard layers (`assert_read_sql` + `connect_readonly_query`'s query_only and default-deny authorizer). `zaxbygraph://schema` serves the same DDL/notes as the `schema` command. - Non-blocking background sync: stale reads (threshold `--stale-seconds`, default 900, env `ZAXBYGRAPH_MCP_STALE_SECONDS`) answer immediately from current data and start ONE locked incremental sync (atomic in-process registry + the PR #10 whole-run lock; daemon thread, contained failures, job ledger visible in graph_status), reporting `freshness.refreshing: true`. The `sync` tool never blocks — it returns a job id. - Productized queries on both surfaces: `pr_overlap`/`file_history`/`what_closed` tools plus `overlap`/`file-history`/`what-closed` commands (issue #7's proven hand-written SQL, lifted into `query.py` with the repo's clamp/incremental-fetch/pre-v5-degrade conventions). - Bounded results: list tools take `limit`, set envelope `truncated`, and emit `data.next_cursor` offset tokens when truncated (search, file_history, open_items); `get_item` takes `max_body_chars`. - Docs: README gains an MCP section (Claude Code + opencode registration), the three new command-reference entries, and the resolution precedence; the bundled skill gains an "MCP surface (prefer when configured)" section outside the pinned First-action contract. pyproject + `__init__` version 0.4.0. ## Recurrence Prevention (defect class) - Defect class: a capability exists only behind an implicit, cwd-dependent shell contract — a consumer surface gains no typed counterpart, so every agent session re-derives it. - Sweep result: P1 (CLI read commands unmapped) 0/16 mapped; P2 (advertised tool properties unwired) 0; P3 (consumer docs left untruthful) 4 files, all OUT_OF_CLASS (the frontier-audit collectors are paste-based by design; nothing they document changed). Full census and dispositions in `08a-recurrence-sweep.md`. - Guardrail: `tests/test_mcp_registry.py` — a two-directional {CLI command → tool | resource | documented-gap} mapping table asserted against the live parser and tool registry; demonstrated RED by deleting a mapping entry and by corrupting a mapping target, GREEN on the complete table. ## Tests - Regression test: `python -m unittest tests.test_query.ProductQueryTests` -> PASS (RED at base: `AttributeError: module 'zaxbygraph.query' has no attribute 'pr_overlap'`) - Acceptance checks: 7 frozen checks (C1-C7) replayed via repro-check.sh — all PASS at head 83a6e46, base legs RED/ERROR with the exact frozen signatures; C7 (read-only guard stack) GREEN-GREEN. - Impacted suite: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` -> **Ran 270 tests — OK** (baseline 250 at 426966e; +5 MCP protocol tests, +1 product-query test, +4 mapping guardrail tests, +10 review-feedback tests in the new `tests/test_mcp_feedback.py`). - Lint/type/build/security checks: none configured in this repo (stdlib-only; the suite is the gate); read-only escape-hatch guards pinned by C7 + the existing QueryTests band; PAT sweep over the diff clean; pyproject has zero install dependencies. - Deferred-work scan: `scan-deferred.sh` -> clean. ## Regression Protection - `tests/test_mcp.py` (frozen pre-implementation by an independent check-author; byte-identical through three review rounds — checkpoint-verified): protocol, resolution (real git worktrees + roots), structured errors + no-create, background refresh via an injected blocking runner, schema-resource deep equality. - `tests/test_mcp_feedback.py` (new, review-round findings): cursor paging on the capped list tools, sql runtime errors as envelope errors, the authorizer layer driven through the tool, stale-sql refresh parity, pipelined requests surviving the roots handshake, server-pin resolution both directions, pr_overlap dedupe, and a subprocess stdin-decoding FIDELITY oracle (U+4E01 sentinel round-trip; proven RED on the pre-fix tree by execution in three revert contexts). - `tests/test_mcp_registry.py` (new, defect-class guardrail). - Test drift review: frozen files untouched (checkpoint byte-hash proof at every gate); all other test changes additive; no stale tests, zero skips. ## External Checkpoint Anchor - Receipt published before implementation (human-confirmed; local validation cannot attest publication/timing): `issue-tracer-checkpoint-v1 slug=7-mcp-typed-agent-surface manifest=542aecbac20c6ab68e9f72f957ce3c4862203eb8 semantics=d89ee2f0c44514a46cc5be034e6c05c65da4931f tree=88ee198aa082476968a0576fe4d50496dcc3f59d` - External artifact location: https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/issues/7#issuecomment-5991227934 (verified live at the final gate) - Independent verification: `repro-check.sh verify-anchor --slug 7-mcp-typed-agent-surface --receipt ''` -> PASS (exit 0, re-verified by the implementation reviewer and the final critic) - Local copy/provenance: `02-reproduction.md` discovery copy — explicitly non-authoritative ## Acceptance Criteria -> Evidence | Acceptance criterion (from intake) | Evidence (command + output, or test name) | |---|---| | AC1: initialize + tools/list list the 11 typed tools with JSON input schemas | Check C1 (`tests.test_mcp.McpProtocolTests.test_initialize_and_tools_list`) — PASS at head, ERROR at base for the frozen signature; live-smoked by the final critic | | AC2: worktree resolves the same slug-keyed DB; roots beat cwd | Check C2 (`tests.test_mcp.McpResolutionTests.test_worktree_and_roots_resolve_same_db`) — PASS; real `git worktree add` harness, `db_files_under(worktree)` stays empty | | AC3: no-corpus / invalid SQL -> isError true + envelope error, nothing created | Check C3 (`tests.test_mcp.McpErrorTests.test_no_corpus_and_bad_sql_are_structured_errors`) — PASS; no DB file, no directory, session survives | | AC4: pr_overlap / file_history / what_closed as tools AND CLI commands | Check C4 (`tests.test_query.ProductQueryTests.test_pr_overlap_file_history_what_closed`) — PASS; shapes seeded through the real sync pipeline (closing_ref provenance); CLI envelopes parsed from stdout | | AC5: stale read answers now, one locked background sync, refreshing true | Check C5 (`tests.test_mcp.McpFreshnessTests.test_stale_read_answers_now_and_refreshes_in_background`) — PASS; runner called exactly once with (str(db_path), repo); second read starts nothing; sql shares the contract (test_mcp_feedback) | | AC6: zaxbygraph://schema equals the schema CLI command | Check C6 (`tests.test_mcp.McpResourceTests.test_schema_resource_matches_cli`) — PASS (deep equality on the same DB) | | AC7: implementation choice recorded (stdlib JSON-RPC; 900s default) | NON-EXECUTABLE (PRODUCT_DECISION) — recorded in 01 Ambiguities + 05 Selected Fix: hand-written stdlib server per the AGENTS.md "No runtime dependencies" standing invariant (the SDK-extra candidate is rejected in the plan's Candidate table); 900s default shipped as `--stale-seconds`/`ZAXBYGRAPH_MCP_STALE_SECONDS`. Maintainer veto path: this bullet — say the word and the SDK-extra candidate is re-opened in a follow-up. | | AC8: the sql tool applies the same read-only guards as the CLI | Check C7 PRESERVING (`repro/c7.sh`, the three existing guard tests) — GREEN-GREEN; the tool routes through `assert_read_sql` + `connect_readonly_query`; authorizer denial exercised through the tool (test_mcp_feedback) | ## Invariant Audit Per AGENTS.md (the repo's invariant doc), each invariant touched or not: - No runtime dependencies: not touched — pyproject has no `dependencies` key; the MCP server is hand-written stdlib JSON-RPC (this was the AC7 decision's whole basis). - No GitHub PAT anywhere: not touched — grep over the diff clean; sync threads use the same `gh`-based sources as the CLI. - Every edge confidence=EXTRACTED / node types: not touched — no sync-path or schema change; `what_closed` reads the existing v5 edges with their `source` provenance (closes reserved for timeline/closing_ref; the new src_type constraint sharpens it). - sql read-only escape hatch (two independent layers): touched and preserved — the MCP sql tool REUSES `assert_read_sql` + `connect_readonly_query` rather than reimplementing (C7 GREEN-GREEN; authorizer denial exercised through the tool); row limits still clamped (`_clamp_limit` via `_int_arg`), results still fetched incrementally. - Item-scoped child-row replacement / edge ownership: not touched — no write-path change. - Closes vs closes_keyword vocabulary: not touched — `what_closed` reports `closes`/`closed_by_commit` edges with their provenance, matching the docs' usage. - Windows first-class: touched with evidence — the server pins stdin/stdout/stderr to UTF-8 (a piped stdin on a cp1252 locale would silently mojibake frames — oracle-tested), paths via urlparse+url2pathname (3.11/3.12-safe), lock reuse proven cross-platform; CI matrix covers windows+ubuntu × 3.11/3.12. - SQLite floor: not touched — no new SQLite features. ## Risk and Rollback - Risk level: low-medium — first threading code in the package (confined to mcp_server.py: atomic registry + the proven whole-run lock, contained exceptions, same-host dead-PID takeover as the recovery story), and a new public interface (guarded by the frozen checks and the mapping guardrail). Three below-threshold, disclosed nits are carried (get_item max_body_chars wrong-type reaches a -32603 frame; sync's force accepts truthy non-bool; FB6 leaves gitignored -wal/-shm sidecars). - Rollback: revert the three commits (single feature + two review-fix commits); no schema or data migration involved. - Residual risk: an MCP client that never answers the roots request stalls that call (spec-conformant clients answer, with an error at worst) — disclosed in the module docstring. ## Waivers (or none) none ## Merge status Awaiting explicit user approval; not merged. PR head: 83a6e46ef21b225bcfdf894a83498c9568d04cde ## Issue Closure Closes #7 ## Verification ladder (trace: .agents/issue-traces/7-mcp-typed-agent-surface) - Plan critic (MiniMax-M3, fresh context): Round 1 NEEDS_REVISION (14 revisions — sql rows positional per frozen C3, single-flight mechanism, resource contract, serverInfo, arg names, hints, no-dir edge, guardrail mcp exclusion, version pair, SKILL contract, cursors wiring, concurrency, pins, mapping-table rung) -> Round 2 APPROVE -> Rounds 3-4 rebind rechecks APPROVE at the shipped head. - Implementation review (swarm-reviewer, fresh context, execution-probed): Round 1 NEEDS_REVISION (five confirmed defects: dead cursors on capped list tools; sql runtime errors escaping as JSON-RPC -32603 through a dead except; stale sql reads bypassing AC5 refresh; pipelined requests dropped during the roots handshake; stdin not UTF-8-pinned) -> Round 2 NEEDS_REVISION (all five upheld-fixed; the new stdin test's oracle OVERTURNED as vacuous) -> Round 3 APPROVE (FB6 fidelity oracle; RED-on-revert independently reproduced in three revert contexts; both carried nits closed; frozen files byte-identical; 270 OK). - Final critic (swarm-critic, fresh context): APPROVE — ten mandated checks executed independently, including a live end-to-end MCP session over real pipes against the repo's real corpus, the anchor receipt fetched live from the issue, zero AMEND rows in the manifest, AC1-AC8 all CLOSED, no deferral/scope-out/unwired/waiver. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds `zaxbygraph mcp`, a typed stdio MCP server with 11 tools that adapts the existing query layer — no new query logic, credentials, or dependencies. It closes issue #7: agents get a typed surface that resolves the repo without the process cwd, plus the three proven hand-written queries productized on both MCP and CLI surfaces. **New Features** - Tools `graph_status`, `search`, `get_item`, `related`, `path`, `pr_overlap`, `file_history`, `what_closed`, `open_items`, `sql`, `sync` answer with the same JSON envelope as the CLI (`{ok, db, repo, freshness, data, truncated}` plus `error{code, message, hint}`), with `isError` on failures; `zaxbygraph://schema` serves the same DDL/notes as the `schema` command. - Repo resolution is explicit `repo` argument, then MCP roots, then the server cwd's git origin — the same slug-keyed store the CLI uses, so worktrees share one graph and reads never create files or directories. - Stale reads answer immediately and start exactly one locked background sync (`freshness.refreshing: true`); the `sync` tool never blocks and returns a job id. - The `sql` tool reuses both read-only guard layers (`assert_read_sql` + `connect_readonly_query` with default-deny authorizer). - The three proven hand-written queries are productized as CLI commands (`overlap`, `file-history`, `what-closed`) in addition to MCP tools. - List tools take `limit`, set `truncated`, and emit `data.next_cursor`; `get_item` takes `max_body_chars`. - README and bundled skill document the MCP surface and prefer it when configured; version bumped to 0.4.0. **Review Hardening** - The database is no longer a tool argument — it is operator-pinned via `--db`/`ZAXBYGRAPH_DB`, since a `#` in a path could let reads create files through sqlite URI parsing. - Server-side bounds cap page/cursor/depth and `pr_overlap`'s number count; malformed frames, sqlite open faults, and bad argument types answer as structured errors instead of killing the session. - The product queries now require `--repo`, `file_history` dedupes `closed_issues`, `what_closed` reports the item kind, `search` pages with a `hit_key` tiebreak, `sync` booleans are strictly typed, and failed lock/thread acquisition rolls the sync job back. - Round-3: the generic tools/call fault path no longer re-raises and kills the session, external-join and stale-refresh failures roll back or self-contain so single-flight never wedges, README notes the pre-v5 constraints on `what-closed`/`file-history`, and regression tests cover both fault-containment fixes (283 tests OK). Written for commit a07b7ce8c9899a50c53511c53a86f48d4853a2f8. Summary will update on new commits. ## Post-publication review (swarm-pr-review + swarm-pr-feedback) A 14-lane swarm review (6 base + 8 micro-lane families, 3 reviewer shards, critic challenge) verified 15 finding clusters; all are closed on this branch (commits fae2ff1, 209a03e, a07b7ce; closure ledger in `.zcode/pr-review/15-83a6e46/`): - **Bounds** on the serialized server: page/cursor/depth/numbers ceilings (`related` depth <= 5 with strict bad_request; page <= 500; cursor <= 10k; pr_overlap 2..64 numbers); `open_items` pages in SQL. - **The per-call `db` tool argument was REMOVED** (supersedes the earlier recorded decision that it wins over the server pin): a model-reachable path was a filesystem oracle and an arbitrary mkdir/DB-creation primitive (a `#` in it even made a *read* create a file via sqlite URI fragment truncation). The database is operator-pinned (`--db` / `ZAXBYGRAPH_DB`) only. - **Protocol containment**: a deeply nested JSON frame no longer kills the server (RecursionError caught at both parse sites); any unexpected tools/call fault answers as the envelope runtime error (session survives — regression-tested by corrupting the FTS tables mid-session). - **Typed arguments**: `max_body_chars` and sync `force`/`include_patches` strictly validated (the string "false" no longer forces a full pull). - **Query semantics**: `file_history.closed_issues` deduplicated across provenance; the three product queries require `--repo` (number-keyed no-filter scans collapsed distinct same-numbered items across repos); `what_closed` reports the item `kind`; `file_history` carries `index_stale`. - **Registry robustness**: Thread.start/acquire failures roll back (no permanent single-flight wedge); external joins leave no phantom entries (regression-tested: a second sync STARTS after an external lock frees). - **Search paging**: a full page always offers a cursor; `hit_key` tiebreak makes ranking a total order. - **Docs/test truth**: SKILL/README writer-claim, resolution-pin, routing and pre-v5 qualifications fixed; FB1 disjoint+union cursor oracle; FB6 tempfile + pinned cp1252 regime; registry tables validated against parser and dispatch table. Suite 283 OK; all 7 frozen acceptance checks GREEN at head; CI green. Known disclosed boundaries are in the module docstring and the trace artifacts.

C7 (read-only guard stack) GREEN-GREEN. - Impacted suite: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` -> **Ran 270 tests — OK** (baseline 250 at 426966e; +5 MCP protocol tests, +1 product-query test, +4 mapping guardrail tests, +10 review-feedback tests in the new `tests/test_mcp_feedback.py`). - Lint/type/build/security checks: none configured in this repo (stdlib-only; the suite is the gate); read-only escape-hatch guards pinned by C7 + the existing QueryTests band; PAT sweep over the diff clean; pyproject has zero install dependencies. - Deferred-work scan: `scan-deferred.sh` -> clean. ## Regression Protection - `tests/test_mcp.py` (frozen pre-implementation by an independent check-author; byte-identical through three review rounds — checkpoint-verified): protocol, resolution (real git worktrees + roots), structured errors + no-create, background refresh via an injected blocking runner, schema-resource deep equality. - `tests/test_mcp_feedback.py` (new, review-round findings): cursor paging on the capped list tools, sql runtime errors as envelope errors, the authorizer layer driven through the tool, stale-sql refresh parity, pipelined requests surviving the roots handshake, server-pin resolution both directions, pr_overlap dedupe, and a subprocess stdin-decoding FIDELITY oracle (U+4E01 sentinel round-trip; proven RED on the pre-fix tree by execution in three revert contexts). - `tests/test_mcp_registry.py` (new, defect-class guardrail). - Test drift review: frozen files untouched (checkpoint byte-hash proof at every gate); all other test changes additive; no stale tests, zero skips. ## External Checkpoint Anchor - Receipt published before implementation (human-confirmed; local validation cannot attest publication/timing): `issue-tracer-checkpoint-v1 slug=7-mcp-typed-agent-surface manifest=542aecbac20c6ab68e9f72f957ce3c4862203eb8 semantics=d89ee2f0c44514a46cc5be034e6c05c65da4931f tree=88ee198aa082476968a0576fe4d50496dcc3f59d` - External artifact location: https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/issues/7#issuecomment-5991227934 (verified live at the final gate) - Independent verification: `repro-check.sh verify-anchor --slug 7-mcp-typed-agent-surface --receipt ''` -> PASS (exit 0, re-verified by the implementation reviewer and the final critic) - Local copy/provenance: `02-reproduction.md` discovery copy — explicitly non-authoritative ## Acceptance Criteria -> Evidence | Acceptance criterion (from intake) | Evidence (command + output, or test name) | |---|---| | AC1: initialize + tools/list list the 11 typed tools with JSON input schemas | Check C1 (`tests.test_mcp.McpProtocolTests.test_initialize_and_tools_list`) — PASS at head, ERROR at base for the frozen signature; live-smoked by the final critic | | AC2: worktree resolves the same slug-keyed DB; roots beat cwd | Check C2 (`tests.test_mcp.McpResolutionTests.test_worktree_and_roots_resolve_same_db`) — PASS; real `git worktree add` harness, `db_files_under(worktree)` stays empty | | AC3: no-corpus / invalid SQL -> isError true + envelope error, nothing created | Check C3 (`tests.test_mcp.McpErrorTests.test_no_corpus_and_bad_sql_are_structured_errors`) — PASS; no DB file, no directory, session survives | | AC4: pr_overlap / file_history / what_closed as tools AND CLI commands | Check C4 (`tests.test_query.ProductQueryTests.test_pr_overlap_file_history_what_closed`) — PASS; shapes seeded through the real sync pipeline (closing_ref provenance); CLI envelopes parsed from stdout | | AC5: stale read answers now, one locked background sync, refreshing true | Check C5 (`tests.test_mcp.McpFreshnessTests.test_stale_read_answers_now_and_refreshes_in_background`) — PASS; runner called exactly once with (str(db_path), repo); second read starts nothing; sql shares the contract (test_mcp_feedback) | | AC6: zaxbygraph://schema equals the schema CLI command | Check C6 (`tests.test_mcp.McpResourceTests.test_schema_resource_matches_cli`) — PASS (deep equality on the same DB) | | AC7: implementation choice recorded (stdlib JSON-RPC; 900s default) | NON-EXECUTABLE (PRODUCT_DECISION) — recorded in 01 Ambiguities + 05 Selected Fix: hand-written stdlib server per the AGENTS.md "No runtime dependencies" standing invariant (the SDK-extra candidate is rejected in the plan's Candidate table); 900s default shipped as `--stale-seconds`/`ZAXBYGRAPH_MCP_STALE_SECONDS`. Maintainer veto path: this bullet — say the word and the SDK-extra candidate is re-opened in a follow-up. | | AC8: the sql tool applies the same read-only guards as the CLI | Check C7 PRESERVING (`repro/c7.sh`, the three existing guard tests) — GREEN-GREEN; the tool routes through `assert_read_sql` + `connect_readonly_query`; authorizer denial exercised through the tool (test_mcp_feedback) | ## Invariant Audit Per AGENTS.md (the repo's invariant doc), each invariant touched or not: - No runtime dependencies: not touched — pyproject has no `dependencies` key; the MCP server is hand-written stdlib JSON-RPC (this was the AC7 decision's whole basis). - No GitHub PAT anywhere: not touched — grep over the diff clean; sync threads use the same `gh`-based sources as the CLI. - Every edge confidence=EXTRACTED / node types: not touched — no sync-path or schema change; `what_closed` reads the existing v5 edges with their `source` provenance (closes reserved for timeline/closing_ref; the new src_type constraint sharpens it). - sql read-only escape hatch (two independent layers): touched and preserved — the MCP sql tool REUSES `assert_read_sql` + `connect_readonly_query` rather than reimplementing (C7 GREEN-GREEN; authorizer denial exercised through the tool); row limits still clamped (`_clamp_limit` via `_int_arg`), results still fetched incrementally. - Item-scoped child-row replacement / edge ownership: not touched — no write-path change. - Closes vs closes_keyword vocabulary: not touched — `what_closed` reports `closes`/`closed_by_commit` edges with their provenance, matching the docs' usage. - Windows first-class: touched with evidence — the server pins stdin/stdout/stderr to UTF-8 (a piped stdin on a cp1252 locale would silently mojibake frames — oracle-tested), paths via urlparse+url2pathname (3.11/3.12-safe), lock reuse proven cross-platform; CI matrix covers windows+ubuntu × 3.11/3.12. - SQLite floor: not touched — no new SQLite features. ## Risk and Rollback - Risk level: low-medium — first threading code in the package (confined to mcp_server.py: atomic registry + the proven whole-run lock, contained exceptions, same-host dead-PID takeover as the recovery story), and a new public interface (guarded by the frozen checks and the mapping guardrail). Three below-threshold, disclosed nits are carried (get_item max_body_chars wrong-type reaches a -32603 frame; sync's force accepts truthy non-bool; FB6 leaves gitignored -wal/-shm sidecars). - Rollback: revert the three commits (single feature + two review-fix commits); no schema or data migration involved. - Residual risk: an MCP client that never answers the roots request stalls that call (spec-conformant clients answer, with an error at worst) — disclosed in the module docstring. ## Waivers (or none) none ## Merge status Awaiting explicit user approval; not merged. PR head: 83a6e46ef21b225bcfdf894a83498c9568d04cde ## Issue Closure Closes #7 ## Verification ladder (trace: .agents/issue-traces/7-mcp-typed-agent-surface) - Plan critic (MiniMax-M3, fresh context): Round 1 NEEDS_REVISION (14 revisions — sql rows positional per frozen C3, single-flight mechanism, resource contract, serverInfo, arg names, hints, no-dir edge, guardrail mcp exclusion, version pair, SKILL contract, cursors wiring, concurrency, pins, mapping-table rung) -> Round 2 APPROVE -> Rounds 3-4 rebind rechecks APPROVE at the shipped head. - Implementation review (swarm-reviewer, fresh context, execution-probed): Round 1 NEEDS_REVISION (five confirmed defects: dead cursors on capped list tools; sql runtime errors escaping as JSON-RPC -32603 through a dead except; stale sql reads bypassing AC5 refresh; pipelined requests dropped during the roots handshake; stdin not UTF-8-pinned) -> Round 2 NEEDS_REVISION (all five upheld-fixed; the new stdin test's oracle OVERTURNED as vacuous) -> Round 3 APPROVE (FB6 fidelity oracle; RED-on-revert independently reproduced in three revert contexts; both carried nits closed; frozen files byte-identical; 270 OK). - Final critic (swarm-critic, fresh context): APPROVE — ten mandated checks executed independently, including a live end-to-end MCP session over real pipes against the repo's real corpus, the anchor receipt fetched live from the issue, zero AMEND rows in the manifest, AC1-AC8 all CLOSED, no deferral/scope-out/unwired/waiver. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds `zaxbygraph mcp`, a typed stdio MCP server with 11 tools that adapts the existing query layer — no new query logic, credentials, or dependencies. It closes issue #7: agents get a typed surface that resolves the repo without the process cwd, plus the three proven hand-written queries productized on both MCP and CLI surfaces. **New Features** - Tools `graph_status`, `search`, `get_item`, `related`, `path`, `pr_overlap`, `file_history`, `what_closed`, `open_items`, `sql`, `sync` answer with the same JSON envelope as the CLI (`{ok, db, repo, freshness, data, truncated}` plus `error{code, message, hint}`), with `isError` on failures; `zaxbygraph://schema` serves the same DDL/notes as the `schema` command. - Repo resolution is explicit `repo` argument, then MCP roots, then the server cwd's git origin — the same slug-keyed store the CLI uses, so worktrees share one graph and reads never create files or directories. - Stale reads answer immediately and start exactly one locked background sync (`freshness.refreshing: true`); the `sync` tool never blocks and returns a job id. - The `sql` tool reuses both read-only guard layers (`assert_read_sql` + `connect_readonly_query` with default-deny authorizer). - The three proven hand-written queries are productized as CLI commands (`overlap`, `file-history`, `what-closed`) in addition to MCP tools. - List tools take `limit`, set `truncated`, and emit `data.next_cursor`; `get_item` takes `max_body_chars`. - README and bundled skill document the MCP surface and prefer it when configured; version bumped to 0.4.0. **Review Hardening** - The database is no longer a tool argument — it is operator-pinned via `--db`/`ZAXBYGRAPH_DB`, since a `#` in a path could let reads create files through sqlite URI parsing. - Server-side bounds cap page/cursor/depth and `pr_overlap`'s number count; malformed frames, sqlite open faults, and bad argument types answer as structured errors instead of killing the session. - The product queries now require `--repo`, `file_history` dedupes `closed_issues`, `what_closed` reports the item kind, `search` pages with a `hit_key` tiebreak, `sync` booleans are strictly typed, and failed lock/thread acquisition rolls the sync job back. - Round-3: the generic tools/call fault path no longer re-raises and kills the session, external-join and stale-refresh failures roll back or self-contain so single-flight never wedges, README notes the pre-v5 constraints on `what-closed`/`file-history`, and regression tests cover both fault-containment fixes (283 tests OK). Written for commit a07b7ce8c9899a50c53511c53a86f48d4853a2f8. Summary will update on new commits. ## Post-publication review (swarm-pr-review + swarm-pr-feedback) A 14-lane swarm review (6 base + 8 micro-lane families, 3 reviewer shards, critic challenge) verified 15 finding clusters; all are closed on this branch (commits fae2ff1, 209a03e, a07b7ce; closure ledger in `.zcode/pr-review/15-83a6e46/`): - **Bounds** on the serialized server: page/cursor/depth/numbers ceilings (`related` depth <= 5 with strict bad_request; page <= 500; cursor <= 10k; pr_overlap 2..64 numbers); `open_items` pages in SQL. - **The per-call `db` tool argument was REMOVED** (supersedes the earlier recorded decision that it wins over the server pin): a model-reachable path was a filesystem oracle and an arbitrary mkdir/DB-creation primitive (a `#` in it even made a *read* create a file via sqlite URI fragment truncation). The database is operator-pinned (`--db` / `ZAXBYGRAPH_DB`) only. - **Protocol containment**: a deeply nested JSON frame no longer kills the server (RecursionError caught at both parse sites); any unexpected tools/call fault answers as the envelope runtime error (session survives — regression-tested by corrupting the FTS tables mid-session). - **Typed arguments**: `max_body_chars` and sync `force`/`include_patches` strictly validated (the string "false" no longer forces a full pull). - **Query semantics**: `file_history.closed_issues` deduplicated across provenance; the three product queries require `--repo` (number-keyed no-filter scans collapsed distinct same-numbered items across repos); `what_closed` reports the item `kind`; `file_history` carries `index_stale`. - **Registry robustness**: Thread.start/acquire failures roll back (no permanent single-flight wedge); external joins leave no phantom entries (regression-tested: a second sync STARTS after an external lock frees). - **Search paging**: a full page always offers a cursor; `hit_key` tiebreak makes ranking a total order. - **Docs/test truth**: SKILL/README writer-claim, resolution-pin, routing and pre-v5 qualifications fixed; FB1 disjoint+union cursor oracle; FB6 tempfile + pinned cp1252 regime; registry tables validated against parser and dispatch table. Suite 283 OK; all 7 frozen acceptance checks GREEN at head; CI green. Known disclosed boundaries are in the module docstring and the trace artifacts.

_Generated from a post-merge tooling audit in a ZaxbyHub/ragappv3 session (PR #883 / issue #708 closeout retrospective). Every claim below was re-checked against commit `b5a67ac189f10392801fe1ad3e050ecebc3a2ca2` (repo HEAD at filing) on 2026-10-12, running the installed CLI (`zaxbygraph 0.4.0`, `python -m zaxbygraph` from the repo root). One issue = one PR. Local artifacts referenced below (session scratch captures) are not in this repository; the quoted excerpts are from this repository at the anchor commit and grep clean there._

## Summary

After this PR, `--format json` output is **merge-safe**: a consumer that captures a successful read with `stderr` merged into `stdout` (the common `2>&1` idiom) still gets exactly one strict-parseable JSON document. Today the one stderr identity line interleaves into the buffered JSON at a nondeterministic position and the parse fails. Text-mode output is unchanged: it keeps its single stderr identity line.

## Problem (claims to verify)

1. **The stderr identity line exists by design and is documented — the split contract is stdout=JSON, stderr=identity.** `src/zaxbygraph/cli.py:137-152` ([permalink](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b5a67ac189f10392801fe1ad3e050ecebc3a2ca2/src/zaxbygraph/cli.py#L137-L152)):

   ```py
   def _identity_line(
       conn: sqlite3.Connection | None, slug: str | None, db_path: Path | None
   ) -> str | None:
       """The one stderr identity line every successful read prints (AC7).
   ```

   and `README.md:453` states "writes exactly one identity line to stderr". `tests/test_cli_envelope.py:495` (`FormatTests::test_stderr_identity_line`) pins it. **VERIFIED** (grepped at the anchor commit; live probe: `zaxbygraph sql "SELECT 1 AS a" --format json 1>/dev/null 2>err` → `err` holds exactly `# db=... repo=... items=... synced=... complete=yes`, stdout strict-parses as the envelope).

2. **When a consumer merges the streams, the identity line corrupts the JSON at a nondeterministic position.** A live session run of `zaxbygraph open --format json 2>&1 | python -c "import json,sys; json.load(sys.stdin)"` failed with `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 779 column 22`, while the same command with `2>/dev/null` strict-parses clean (the `# db=` line is a single unbuffered stderr write against block-buffered JSON stdout, so it lands wherever the buffers interleave). The corruption is deterministic in **outcome** (always raises) and nondeterministic only in **position** — it cannot be consumed correctly without stream surgery. **VERIFIED** (reproduced at 0.4.0 this session; `python -m zaxbygraph open --format json 2>/dev/null` → strict `json.load` OK).

   *CORRECTED during review: an earlier pass of this issue claimed the identity line lands on stdout ("preamble before the JSON"). Re-probing at the anchor commit disproved that — stdout is pure JSON; the line is on stderr. The stale claim came from an older-version consumer note; preserved here per the living-record rule. The defect is not the channel choice, it is that machine mode emits the line at all in a way that breaks the most common capture idiom.*

3. **The envelope already carries everything the identity line repeats.** `{"ok", "db", "repo", "freshness{synced_at, age_s, complete}", "data", "truncated"}` (probed: `sql`, `open`, `status` all return it; `tests/test_cli_envelope.py:174` `test_every_command_returns_envelope` pins the shape). Suppressing the line under `--format json` therefore loses no information. **VERIFIED** (probe + test read at the anchor commit).

4. **Prior-art reconciliation.** The stderr identity line was introduced as AC7 of a prior contract ("The one stderr identity line every successful read prints (AC7)", `cli.py:142`) and is pinned by `test_stderr_identity_line`. This issue **extends** that contract — scoping the line to text mode — rather than duplicating it; the pinned test's json-mode expectation must be updated with the fix (see Files). The README's machine-mode guidance (`README.md:135`, "prefer `json` for anything parsed"; `jsonl` note "identity is on the stderr line") documents the channel but does not warn against merging streams, and `skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md`'s Output-shapes section does not mention the identity line at all — which is how agent consumers arrive unprepared. **VERIFIED** (grepped at the anchor commit).

## Scope

- In: suppress the stderr identity line when `--format json` (or `--format jsonl` / `--format compact` — any machine format) is active; keep the text-mode identity line exactly as today; update the pinned test and the two doc surfaces; add the merged-capture regression check.
- Out: envelope shape changes; error-path stderr echoes (`error: MESSAGE`, which fires only on failures and is documented); `sync` output shape; the compact/jsonl payload semantics.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: WHEN a successful read command runs with a machine output format, THE SYSTEM SHALL emit no non-JSON lines on stdout or stderr, so combined stdout+stderr strict-parses as one JSON document.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_cli_json_machine_mode.py::test_json_merged_capture_strict_parses -q`
  - expect: `JSONDecodeError`
  - files: `tests/test_cli_json_machine_mode.py` (new), `src/zaxbygraph/cli.py`
  - why: VERIFIED red at base — a merged capture (`stderr=subprocess.STDOUT`) of `open --format json` raises `JSONDecodeError` (identity line at a nondeterministic byte position inside the buffered envelope), while the stderr-discarded capture parses. The check spawns the CLI against a fixture DB (tests/fixtures.py family — no live gh), merges streams at the subprocess level, and asserts `json.loads` succeeds.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN a successful read command runs in text mode, THE SYSTEM SHALL write exactly one identity line to stderr.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_cli_json_machine_mode.py::test_text_mode_keeps_stderr_identity_line -q`
  - expect: `1 passed`
  - files: `tests/test_cli_json_machine_mode.py` (new)
  - why: green at base and must stay green — the fix scopes suppression to machine formats only; this pins the AC7 contract's text-mode half independently of `tests/test_cli_envelope.py::FormatTests::test_stderr_identity_line`, which the fix must amend.
- [ ] AC3: THE SYSTEM SHALL carry `db`, `repo`, and `freshness` in every successful machine-format envelope.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_cli_envelope.py::EnvelopeTests::test_every_command_returns_envelope -q`
  - expect: `1 passed`
  - files: `tests/test_cli_envelope.py`
  - why: green at base and must stay green — suppression of the stderr line loses nothing only because the envelope already carries the identity fields (prior-art check reused as the driver, not duplicated).
- [ ] AC4: THE SYSTEM SHALL document the machine-mode silence rule and the capture hazard on both doc surfaces.
  - class: NON-EXECUTABLE(DOCS_ONLY)
  - argv: named substitute evidence — rendered diff review of `README.md` (the `--format` table row at :135 and the identity-line note at :453) and `skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md` (Output-shapes section), confirming both state: machine formats emit identity fields inside the envelope only; text mode prints the stderr identity line; consumers must not merge streams when parsing, and pre-0.4 builds printed the line on stdout so legacy `strip-before-first-{` recipes are vestigial.
  - expect: reviewer confirms the two surfaces carry the rule and the version note.
  - files: `README.md`, `skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md`
  - why: docs-only; the executable contract is AC1-AC3. This closes the gap that produced a wrong first-pass claim on this very issue (see the CORRECTED note).
item.title: Machine-mode output: make --format json merge-safe (stderr identity line corrupts 2>&1 captures)

_Generated from the ZaxbyHub/opencode-swarm #3316 session (PR #3419, merged ed0dd10d8) retrospective on 2026-10-23, cross-checked against an independent adjudication. Every claim was re-verified on 2026-10-24 against origin/main `bc736f2dd171824faa4486ea6d160df515489300`: the executed SQL ran against a production cache built by the installed CLI (editable install at this lineage, synced 2026-10-22), and the source excerpts below were read at the anchor commit and grep clean there. The cache belongs to another repository and is not in this repository; the query text and results are restated inline. One issue = one PR._

## Summary

After this PR, the `edges` table holds at most one row per `(repo, dst_type, dst_id, src_type, src_id, rel)`: the two independent `closes` extraction sources (the item's `closingIssuesReferences` and the timeline `closed` event, issue #6) merge their provenance instead of each inserting an edge, existing caches gain a migration/re-sync path, and read-side consumers stop double-counting.

## Problem (claims to verify)

1. **VERIFIED (executed SQL against a production cache on 2026-10-23): duplicate `closes` rows exist for at least six PR→issue pairs.** Over the `edges` table of a `zaxbyhub/opencode-swarm` cache:
   ```sql
   SELECT dst_id, src_id, rel, COUNT(*) AS n
   FROM edges WHERE repo='zaxbyhub/opencode-swarm' AND rel='closes'
   GROUP BY dst_id, src_id, rel HAVING n > 1 LIMIT 5
   ```
   returns `(2826, 2834)`, `(2867, 2874)`, `(2906, 3195)`, `(2907, 3207)`, `(2908, 3284)` — each with `n = 2` — and `(3315, 3400)` shows the same on inspection: two `closes` rows whose `evidence` differs, `'closingIssuesReferences'` and `'timeline closed event 2026-10-21T09:31:27Z'`. Any join or count over edges double-counts these pairs (a session query literally printed the same `#3400 closes #3315` row twice).

2. **VERIFIED (source read at the anchor): both `closes` sources emit edges independently, and `edges` carries no uniqueness constraint.** Extraction for item-derived links includes `"closes"` alongside `"closes_keyword"`:
   https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/bc736f2dd171824faa4486ea6d160df515489300/src/zaxbygraph/extract.py#L204-L206
   and the timeline extractor (#6) adds its own:
   https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/bc736f2dd171824faa4486ea6d160df515489300/src/zaxbygraph/extract.py#L221-L228
   (`"closed": "timeline closed event"` with `source='timeline'`). `schema.sql` declares `UNIQUE` constraints for `items (repo, number)` and `comments (repo, kind, github_id)` — none for `edges`.

3. **INFERENCE: the interaction, not either source alone, produces the duplicates.** Each extractor is individually correct; nothing merges a `closes(src=item)` with a `closes(src=timeline)` for the same pair, and the "replace edges for that number on ingest" invariant governs per-item re-ingest, not cross-source collapse.

**Prior-art reconciliation:** #6 (shipped, `426966e`) *added* the timeline source with provenance — the duplicate is its unmanaged interaction with the item source, not a regression of #6 itself. Epic #8 root cause 2 ("failures look like success") is the adjacent program; this is a concrete data-integrity defect with its own fix shape and does not need the epic's DB-location work. #17 is the output merge-safety layer — a different layer; the duplicates are visible even in perfectly parsed JSON.

## Scope

In:
- Exactly one `closes` edge per `(repo, dst, src)` pair, with the two provenances merged (e.g. evidence list or a preference order), enforced by a `UNIQUE` constraint or equivalent ingest-time collapse in `store.py`/`sync.py`.
- A path that heals existing caches (re-sync of affected items or a one-shot migration) — the AGENTS contract already re-ingests per item, so the collapse must run there.
- A regression spec that ingests a fixture item carrying **both** sources and asserts one edge.

Out:
- The stderr/stdout output split and JSON merge-safety (#17).
- Epic #8's DB-location, typed-surface, and completeness work.
- Any change to `closes_keyword` vs `closes` as distinct relations (they stay distinct).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: WHEN an item is ingested that yields both an item-source `closes` edge (from `closingIssuesReferences`) and a timeline `closes` edge (from a `closed` timeline event) for the same `(dst, src)`, THE SYSTEM SHALL store exactly one `closes` row for that pair, carrying both provenances.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest tests.test_closes_edge_uniqueness -v`
  - expect: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tests.test_closes_edge_uniqueness'`
  - files: `tests/test_closes_edge_uniqueness.py` (new; fixture item + timeline event through the extraction/store path, assert single edge and merged evidence; plus a second case asserting pre-seeded duplicates collapse on re-ingest)
  - why: the collapse does not exist at base — the spec asserts an invariant the current code violates, so it cannot run red today.
- [ ] AC2: THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the existing edge tests green.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m unittest tests.test_edges -v`
  - expect: green at base and head
  - files: `tests/test_edges.py`
  - why: the uniqueness change must not alter any other edge behaviour (AGENTS invariants: EXTRACTED-only confidence, owned-edge deletion, rollups).

## Design (non-binding)

1. Ingest-time collapse at the store boundary: before insert, delete/merge any existing same-`(repo,dst_type,dst_id,src_type,src_id,rel)` row (mirroring the owned-edge replace invariant), unioning `evidence` into a bounded list or keeping the higher-priority source with the other recorded in evidence.
2. `schema.sql` gains `UNIQUE (repo, dst_type, dst_id, src_type, src_id, rel)` on `edges` (or an `INSERT OR REPLACE` equivalent) so old caches heal on their next per-item re-ingest without a standalone migration tool.

## Files to change

`src/zaxbygraph/schema.sql`, `src/zaxbygraph/store.py` (or `sync.py` edge write path), `tests/test_closes_edge_uniqueness.py` (new).

## Definition of done

AC1-AC2 proven; a re-sync of a duplicate-bearing production cache verified to collapse existing pairs (evidence from the reporter's cache available on request); AGENTS edge invariants re-read and confirmed unchanged.
