item.body:
Closes #17
Closes #19

(A post-publication swarm-pr-review + cubic feedback round hardened this PR: `merge_evidence` now hard-truncates instead of ever returning NULL, protects the arriving stream's marker and the closing_ref string at the 512-char cap, and bounds the first-insert path; docs truth fixes in schema.sql's header, the `zaxbygraph schema` notes, emit_result's docstring, and README/SKILL.md's capture-hazard wording; test pins added for every command surface's stderr silence, the untouched v5 candidate, jsonl rows-only shape, and non-closes two-rows invariant.)

(Collated into one PR per the maintainer's explicit session instruction to collate the issues that can ship together; the fixes are layer-disjoint — #17 output layer, #19 ingest layer — with zero file overlap, and were trace-worked together under `.agents/issue-traces/17-19-machine-output-closes-uniqueness/`.)

## Summary

Two core-contract correctness fixes, verified end to end by the issue-tracer protocol (frozen RED/GREEN acceptance checks, independent reviewer, final critic):

- **#17 — machine-format output is merge-safe.** `--format json|compact|jsonl` no longer print the stderr identity line; a merged `2>&1` capture of a successful read strict-parses as JSON. Text mode is byte-identical to before and keeps its one identity line. `json`/`compact` carry the identity fields in the envelope (`db`, `repo`, `freshness`), which they always did; **`jsonl` list payloads print rows only — no envelope — so that surface carries no identity fields at all; use `json` or `compact` when you need them.** Legacy `strip-before-first-{` recipes are vestigial (pre-0.5 builds printed the line in machine mode too).
- **#19 — `closes` edges collapse to one row per pair.** The two GitHub-reported streams — `closingIssuesReferences` (`source='closing_ref'`) and the timeline `closed` event (`source='timeline'`) — corroborate ONE closure fact and now merge instead of each inserting. The `closing_ref` source survives (structured declaration over the event stream) and `evidence` carries both provenance strings. A same-source refresh unions evidence instead of replacing, so re-ingesting one stream can never drop the other stream's provenance. Schema v6 collapses stored duplicates and installs a partial UNIQUE index (`ux_edges_closes_pair`) that makes the invariant physical.

## Root Cause

#17: `emit_result` (src/zaxbygraph/cli.py, the single output owner) printed the identity line after rendering for every format (cli.py:280-283 pre-fix); stderr is unbuffered and stdout block-buffered under a pipe, so the line interleaved into merged captures at a buffer-dependent offset and strict parsing always failed. #19: the `edges` UNIQUE key deliberately includes `source` (two provenance streams are two facts), nothing merged the `closes` streams across sources, and both sources are delete-exempt on re-ingest — so duplicates accumulated and existing caches could never self-heal. Reproduced live: merged capture raised `JSONDecodeError`; a production v5 store held duplicate pairs (14→6, 15→7) and `what-closed 6` printed PR 14 twice.

## Fix

- `src/zaxbygraph/cli.py`: the identity-line print is gated on the resolved format being `text` (covers all 17 `emit_result` call sites, computed and caller-supplied lines). Failure-path `error:` echo unchanged.
- `src/zaxbygraph/extract.py`: `merge_evidence(*parts)` — distinct-part union, first-seen order, `"; "`-joined, 512-char cap dropping newest parts first (the two provenance strings survive truncation), NULL-safe, idempotent.
- `src/zaxbygraph/store.py`: `insert_edge` for `rel='closes'` looks up ANY existing row for the pair; different source → merge into the survivor (`closing_ref` preferred); same source → union evidence (never replace). All other relations keep today's exact semantics.
- `src/zaxbygraph/db.py`: migration v6 (`migrate_v5_to_v6`) collapses stored duplicate pairs and creates `ux_edges_closes_pair ... WHERE rel='closes'` — created by the MIGRATION only, not schema.sql, because `init_schema` runs `executescript(schema.sql)` before the chain and a UNIQUE index there would fail against a v5 store's not-yet-collapsed duplicates (fresh DBs get the index when the forward chain runs from user_version 0). `CURRENT_USER_VERSION` 5→6.
- `src/zaxbygraph/schema.sql`: comment documenting why the v6 index is migration-created.
- Docs: README.md + skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md (machine-mode silence rule, capture hazard, jsonl-list identity truth), docs/schema.md (v6, index, merge semantics, true healing triggers — sync / `doctor --consolidate` / MCP sync; reads never migrate), AGENTS.md (the closes exception to the provenance-key invariant).

**Healing/migration:** existing v5 caches heal on their next writable open — a `sync`, `doctor --consolidate`, or MCP-triggered sync. Read commands never migrate, so an unmigrated cache still shows duplicates to read-only consumers until then (documented in docs/schema.md). **Rollback note:** reverting this PR strands stores already migrated to user_version 6 (forward-only policy, unchanged from prior schema bumps).

## Recurrence Prevention (defect class)

- Defect class (a): success-path stderr writes break the machine-mode output contract. (b): two extraction streams independently insert the same link fact without a cross-source collapse.
- Sweep result: 8 counted units across 5 predicates, all dispositioned (2 FIX = the defect sites themselves; rest FALSE_POSITIVE with stated disqualifiers / OUT_OF_CLASS with named boundary). Census: only `closes` is a multi-source relation; all 20 hand-seeding edge test sites audited (none trips the index — suite green is the executed proof).
- Guardrail: schema-constraint rung for (b) — the partial UNIQUE index makes any bypassing writer fail loudly (demonstrated: `test_partial_index_fires_on_bypassing_writers` errors at base, passes at head). Regression-family rung for (a) — the merged-capture subprocess family (C1 + 5 extension tests), demonstrated RED at base / GREEN at head, mutant-killing verified (gate revert kills C1; a jsonl-reprinting partial fix is killed by the extension module).

## Tests

- Regression: `python -m unittest tests.test_closes_edge_uniqueness tests.test_cli_json_machine_mode tests.test_cli_machine_formats_extended -v` -> PASS (was FAIL/absent at base)
- Impacted suite: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` -> **Ran 309 tests — OK** (baseline 283 OK at f4c8065)
- Frozen acceptance checks (disposable-worktree base legs at f4c8065793b4d16364c2a2f7fa21cfb6b46e2533): C1 DISCRIMINATING RED→GREEN; C5 NEW-SURFACE absence→GREEN; C2/C3/C6 PRESERVING GREEN→GREEN — all PASS at shipped head 0ad68c5d11b19f064310b240a2d09d9a66be665c
- Mutation discipline: gate revert kills C1; store-merge revert kills C5 via the index; migration revert kills C5 via `5 != 6`; jsonl-reprint mutant killed by the extension module — all restore green
- Lint/type/build/security: none configured (stdlib-only; the suite is the gate); no new dependencies; no secrets in the diff
- Deferred-work scan: `scan-deferred.sh` -> clean

## Regression Protection

- New: tests/test_cli_json_machine_mode.py (frozen C1/C2), tests/test_closes_edge_uniqueness.py (frozen C5, incl. the v5→v6 healing seam), tests/test_cli_machine_formats_extended.py (jsonl/compact/default), SamePairTwoStreamsTests rewrite (one-row contract, degraded re-ingest, both orders, index-fires, what_closed consumer), MigrateV5ToV6Tests, DoctorConsolidateV6CollapseTests, merge_evidence units, doc-content pins (tests/test_docs.py).
- Boundary/adversarial: NULL evidence, cap truncation keeps first-seen, both ingest orders, post-merge single-stream re-ingest, pre-v5 no-op, index fires on bypassing writers, Windows paths (replay wrappers are cygpath-aware).
- Test drift review: the two json-mode identity pins and SamePairTwoStreamsTests encoded the OLD contracts; each was replaced with a strictly stronger pin (machine-mode silence + text-mode AC7 parity; one-row merge contract) — the two flips are the sanctioned checkpoint AMEND rows 6 (C5 CHECK_WRONG) and 7 (C3 AC_CHANGED_BY_USER), reviewer-approved with archived pre-edit legs, so nothing was weakened.

## External Checkpoint Anchor

- Receipt published before implementation (v1), superseded pre-implementation after the sanctioned C5 CHECK_WRONG amendment (v2), and re-anchored post-implementation under the reviewer-authorized amendment wave (v3, then v4 bound to the shipped head's tree). Final binding literal:
  `issue-tracer-checkpoint-v1 slug=17-19-machine-output-closes-uniqueness manifest=26f49c43187dcca398f0a91850badff19be85b74 semantics=f7a3d197d48fa6380794f5e7b2796d7d97fceff1 tree=bb3f71cd1d1194b09ebba504317a44552b339e46`
- External artifact location: comments on #17 and #19 (v1: issuecomment-6369409342 / 6369409962; v2: 6369640234 / 6369640640; v3: 6373328494 / 6373329494; v4: 6373858529 / 6373859148)
- Independent verification: `repro-check.sh verify-anchor --slug 17-19-machine-output-closes-uniqueness --receipt '<v4 literal>'` -> PASS (re-run by the implementation reviewer and the final critic)
- Local copy: `.agents/issue-traces/17-19-machine-output-closes-uniqueness/02-reproduction.md` (discovery copy, explicitly non-authoritative)

## Acceptance Criteria -> Evidence

| Acceptance criterion (from intake) | Evidence (command + output, or test name) |
|---|---|
| AC1 machine formats emit no non-JSON bytes (merged capture strict-parses) | C1 frozen check RED→GREEN (`repro/C1.{base,head}.log`) + tests/test_cli_machine_formats_extended.py (5 tests) |
| AC2 text mode keeps exactly one stderr identity line | C2 frozen check GREEN/GREEN + TextIdentityTests + the flipped envelope pin's text-mode leg |
| AC3 db/repo/freshness in every machine envelope | C3 frozen check GREEN/GREEN (test_every_command_returns_envelope) + machine-mode envelope asserts |
| AC4 machine-mode silence + capture hazard documented on both surfaces | NON-EXECUTABLE(DOCS_ONLY): rendered README.md/SKILL.md diff + tests/test_docs.py::MachineModeSilenceDocTests; rationale: AC4's class is frozen in the anchored acceptance table (moving it would move the semantics digest), so the record carries cheap string pins + this line (plan-critic binding directive 2) |
| AC5 one closes row per pair, both provenances; existing caches heal | C5 frozen check absence→GREEN + SamePairTwoStreamsTests + MigrateV5ToV6Tests + DoctorConsolidateV6CollapseTests + what_closed consumer test + index-fires probe |
| AC6 existing edge tests stay green | C6 frozen check GREEN/GREEN (40 tests at head vs 36 at base) + full suite 309 OK |

## Invariant Audit

(AGENTS.md, verified by two independent gates + the final critic; each with executed or source evidence)

- Every edge `confidence='EXTRACTED'`: untouched — the merge UPDATE never touches the column; INSERT literal unchanged (store.py).
- Node types unchanged; closes endpoints stay `item`; commit endpoints unchanged.
- Evidence is a payload, never identity: the 7-column UNIQUE key is untouched; the closes exception (both streams = one fact, evidence merged) is now documented in AGENTS.md itself.
- Actor rollups, mentions/closes rollup, per-payload suppression: untouched (query.py/extract.py unchanged in those paths).
- Cross-repo handling: untouched.
- `closes_keyword` vs `closes` distinction: preserved — keyword regexes still never write `closes`; docs re-affirm it.
- Owned-edge deletion with append-only exemption: unchanged (store.py:82-91); the merged row's survivor source is always exempt (`closing_ref`/`timeline`), so re-ingest can never retract a GitHub-reported link.
- Watermark verbatim/inclusive, per-item BEGIN IMMEDIATE, idempotent ingest: untouched (sync.py not in the diff).
- Read-only `sql` escape hatch: untouched (zero diff in the authorizer/query-guard paths).
- Windows-first portability: replay wrappers cygpath-aware; suite green on this Windows box; CI matrix (Windows+Linux, 3.11/3.12) runs the same unittest suite.
- SQLite floor: unchanged at 3.35.0 (partial indexes are 3.8.0+, well under).

## Considered, not filed

| Item | Reason | Re-evaluation trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `emit_result` still computes the identity line in machine mode then discards it (two wasted queries per machine read) | Cosmetic perf nit (implementation-review Round 2 record); fails the necessity gate (no correctness consequence) | If a profile ever shows read-command overhead matters |
| `; ` delimiter lets payload text (e.g. an unchecked `created_at`) alias or forge evidence-PAYLOAD parts | Pre-existing evidence-string pattern (payload text was always concatenated); impact confined to the display payload — the `source` column and row identity are unaffected; fails necessity-gate proportionality for an escaping redesign | If evidence parts ever become machine-parsed rather than displayed |
| `index_stale` does not flag a pre-v6 store (reads show duplicates until the next writable open) | Documented healing boundary (reads never migrate); adding v6 detection is an enhancement, not a defect | If a consumer reports acting on un-healed duplicate rows |
| `churn` jsonl rows carry no repo column; `source` names the survivor stream only | Both are pre-existing shapes or documented survivor semantics (jsonl identity caveat; closing_ref-preference recorded in the trace) | If multi-repo jsonl attribution or per-stream provenance queries become a need |
| Test-hardenings: no subprocess timeouts in test harnesses, env-var scrubbing, whitespace-normalization notice, evidence-order canonicality across heal-vs-ingest paths | Improvement-tier (no defect; deterministic today); recorded per the follow-up covenant | Batch them if a follow-up hardening PR is opened |
| PR body said "18 emit_result call sites"; the real count is 17 (18 included the definition) | Corrected in this body | n/a |
| jsonl list payloads carry no identity fields (by design under AC1's silence mandate) | Disclosed behavior, documented on README + SKILL + pinned by tests — not a defect | If consumers request identity on jsonl lists (would be an envelope-shape design change, new issue) |

## Waivers (or none)

None. Every Full-Resolution Contract clause is satisfied with evidence in the trace; both checkpoint AMENDs went through the sanctioned reviewer-approved path.

## Merge status

AWAITING_USER_APPROVAL

item.body:
_Tracking issue. Generated from the SOTA review and bundling plan (`docs/plans/sota-and-bundling.md` rev 7, `docs/plans/remote-and-multi-user.md`, branch `claude/upbeat-fermi-2fqehy`). The plan was reviewed by two independent critic passes and reconciled against two other models' plans (GLM 5.3, Mimo v2.6 Pro) and two comparable tools (gitcrawl, ghcrawl). Every child issue was re-checked against origin/main b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5 on 2026-10-25 (baseline: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → `Ran 310 tests ... OK`). Every DISCRIMINATING expectation was observed with an executed base-leg probe, and every PRESERVING check was run green at base. One child issue = one PR._

## Purpose
zaxbygraph already records **what happened** faithfully. This program makes it answer two more questions: **what matters now**, and **what belongs together**. Agents can then find the most important open issues and bundle 2–3 to fix together, using evidence the tool computes rather than ad-hoc SQL. It also:
- fixes a quadratic cold sync;
- fixes four read paths that give wrong or partial answers;
- brings the MCP surface up to current spec;
- adds a verified git-snapshot path for remote and multi-user use.

The derived read tier is maintainer-approved and codified in `AGENTS.md` on the plan branch: it scores and groups at query time, never persists, and labels its output a heuristic.

## How to work this
- Work each workstream's PRs in slot order. Different workstreams run in parallel once their `Depends on` edges have merged.
- Dependency kinds:
  - `Depends on`: must merge first.
  - `Schema after`: the migration lane.
  - `Gated on`: a maintainer decision or external evidence.
- Every PR body says `Closes #<child>` and carries a `## Closure evidence` section with each AC's argv and result.
- **argv convention:** every AC uses `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p <file> -k <test> -b`. Its absence signature is `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5). The two documented forms both fail at base on `from fixtures import`: `python -m pytest <file> -q` (CONTRIBUTING:139) and `python -m unittest tests.<module>` (used by #1–#7). C-01 repairs them.

## Workstreams
| Id | Workstream | PRs | Tiers (S/M/L) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Ingest at scale and the evidence schema | 6 | 0/3/3 |
| B | Derived read tier: export, similarity, triage and bundling | 3 | 0/1/2 |
| C | Read truth and environment | 1 | 0/1/0 |
| D | Agent surface (MCP) | 2 | 0/2/0 |
| E | Remote and multi-user use | 1 | 0/1/0 |

### Workstream A: Ingest at scale and the evidence schema (6 PRs, critical path)
| Slot | Issue | Title | Tier | Depends on | Schema after | Gated on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A-01 | #22 | Cold sync scales linearly and graph reads stop scanning every edge | M | — | — | — |
| A-02 | #23 | Sync survives schema drift, records section completeness, refreshes exact items, and writes a replayable sidecar | L | A-01 | — | — |
| A-03 | #24 | Demand, ownership and dependency signals become queryable columns; review text and changed paths become searchable | L | A-02 | — (v7, lane head) | — |
| A-04 | #25 | Edited and deleted issue text stays answerable as evidence | M | A-02, A-03 | A-03 (v8) | — |
| A-05 | #26 | Issues link to the files, errors and PRs their text names | M | A-04 | A-04 (v9) | — |
| A-06 | #27 | Blocked-by, parent, duplicate, reopen, open-linked-PR and commit-message links come from GitHub | L | A-02, A-05 | A-05 (v10) | — |

### Workstream B: Derived read tier (3 PRs)
| Slot | Issue | Title | Tier | Depends on | Schema after | Gated on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B-01 | #28 | A deterministic, hash-stamped corpus export | M | A-02, A-04 | — | — |
| B-02 | #29 | `similar`/`explain`/`coupling`, measured against GitHub's own ground truth | L | A-01, A-05, A-06, B-01 | — | — |
| B-03 | #30 | `triage`, `bundle` and `brief` for the most important workable issues | L | B-02, A-03, A-06 | — | B-03 AC9 |

### Workstream C: Read truth and environment (1 PR, parallel-safe)
| Slot | Issue | Title | Tier | Depends on | Schema after | Gated on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C-01 | #31 | Read answers stay truthful on REST-only stores, old SQLite, proxy remotes and every documented check command | M | — | — | — |

### Workstream D: Agent surface (2 PRs)
| Slot | Issue | Title | Tier | Depends on | Schema after | Gated on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D-01 | #32 | Typed MCP results, read-only hints, triage/bundle tools, 2025-11-25 | M | B-03 | — | D-01 AC7 |
| D-02 | #33 | Stateless 2026-07-28 protocol without Roots | M | D-01 | — | — |

### Workstream E: Remote and multi-user use (1 PR)
| Slot | Issue | Title | Tier | Depends on | Schema after | Gated on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E-01 | #34 | Warm start from a verified git snapshot | M | B-01, C-01 | — | E-01 AC6 (external evidence) |

**Critical path:** A-01 → A-02 → A-03 → A-04 → A-05 → A-06 → B-02 → B-03 → D-01 → D-02. C-01 can merge at any time. B-01 can start once A-04 merges, and E-01 once B-01 and C-01 have merged.

## Hotspot files (hard: one open PR at a time)
| File | PRs |
|---|---|
| `src/zaxbygraph/store.py` | A-01, A-02, A-03, A-04, A-05, A-06 |
| `src/zaxbygraph/sync.py` | A-01, A-02, A-06 |
| `src/zaxbygraph/db.py` / `schema.sql` | A-01 (index only), A-03, A-04, A-05, A-06 (the migration lane) |
| `src/zaxbygraph/mcp_server.py` | D-01, D-02 |

## Shared files (soft: rebase before merge)
| File | PRs |
|---|---|
| `src/zaxbygraph/query.py` | A-01, A-03, A-04, A-05, A-06, B-03, C-01, E-01 |
| `src/zaxbygraph/cli.py` | A-02, A-04, B-01, B-02, B-03, C-01, E-01 |
| `src/zaxbygraph/graphql.py` | A-02, A-03, A-06 |
| `README.md` / `docs/schema.md` / `skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md` | most PRs |

## Schema-after lane
Every migration lands in this order:
1. **A-01:** adds the `items(repo, title)` index through `schema.sql`, with no `user_version` bump. A non-unique index needs no migration; `idx_items_repo_merge` is the precedent.
2. **A-03 → v7:** payload columns, `assignees`, `issue_field_values`, comment `author_association`, `reviews_fts`, FTS path text.
3. **A-04 → v8:** `revisions`.
4. **A-05 → v9:** `item_path_refs`, `item_signatures`.
5. **A-06 → v10:** `item_events`, `pr_commits`.

## Maintainer decisions
Each item below is a NON-EXECUTABLE criterion, and the PR cannot close until it is recorded on the issue. The first two are maintainer decisions; the last two need external or review evidence.
- **B-03 AC9 (PRODUCT_DECISION):** WHEN default triage weights and the label-weight map format are chosen THE SYSTEM SHALL ship them documented and echoed in every payload.
- **D-01 AC7 (PRODUCT_DECISION):** WHEN distribution is decided THE SYSTEM SHALL be published to PyPI and listed in the MCP Registry, or the maintainer SHALL record a decline.
- **E-01 AC6 (EXTERNAL_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE), not a maintainer decision:** a recorded push to `refs/zaxbygraph/snapshot` settles the default snapshot location; the fallback is a branch.
- **E-01 AC7 (DOCS_ONLY):** reviewer approval of the remote-use README section.

## Coverage accounting
Every plan finding maps to exactly one slot.

|---|---|
| T1 actor-edge DELETE scans every edge (§2.1) | A-01 |
| T2 per-item `recount` (§2.1) | A-01 |

| `item`/`related`/`what-closed` O(E) reads; `PRAGMA optimize` (§2.2, §13 B8) | A-01 |
| GraphQL field error aborts sync; validation vs runtime errors (§2.5, §13 B7) | A-02 |
| GraphQL query in argv (§2.8) | A-02 |
| Section completeness never reaches ingest (§13 B12) | A-02 |
| `sync --numbers` without moving the watermark (§11 G1, §13 B3/B9) | A-02 |
| Sidecar not deduplicable or replayable; README:152 advice (§13 B2) | A-02 |
| Listing payload signals unmodeled (§2.4) | A-03 |
| Issue fields (GA 2026-07-02) unmodeled (§2.4) | A-03 |
| Comment `author_association` missing (§2.8) | A-03 |
| COALESCE for source-specific columns | A-03 |
| Review bodies not searchable (§10 R4) | A-03 |
| Changed paths not searchable (§11 G4) | A-03 |
| Coverage reporting, including DB size (§11 G9, §10.2) | A-03 |
| Edit history and tombstones (§12, §13 B1/B4/B5) | A-04 |
| Open issues have no file linkage (§2.3) | A-05 |
| Error signatures (§4 A3) | A-05 |
| Branch-name linkage (§4 A3) | A-05 |
| Reference positions; single-digit `#N` noise (§11 G5) | A-05 |
| Dependencies, parents, duplicates (§2.5, §4 A2) | A-06 |
| Reopen events (§4 A2) | A-06 |
| Open linked PRs from GitHub (§4 A2) | A-06 |
| PR commit-message references (§11 G3) | A-06 |
| `duplicate_keyword` stream (§10.2) | A-06 |
| Corpus export with determinism and an orphan-edge trailer (§12.3, §13 B6) | B-01 |
| No relatedness primitive (§1) | B-02 |

| Anchor guard (§5.5) | B-02 |
| Hub penalty (§13.4) | B-02 |

| Git-delivered verified snapshots (remote plan §3) | E-01 |

## Considered, not filed (RECORD)
| Item | Reason | Gate test failed | Re-evaluation trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fetch GitHub `userContentEdits` (`sync --edit-history`) | The schema documents `diff` as "a summary of the changes"; reconstruction is unproven. | 1 (verified) | A real payload shows full prior text is reconstructible. |
| `export-corpus --as-of` | Edges carry no timestamp, so the result would be a half-snapshot; B-02's evaluation snapshot owns time-correctness. | 2 | Edges gain timestamps. |
| Public time filters on `similar` (`--open-at` etc.) | No user beyond the evaluation; kept internal to B-02. | 3 | An agent workflow needs them. |
| Batch `item N [N…]` | `bundle --briefs` covers the use. | 2 | A measured agent-overhead problem. |
| Label→file priors | Minimum support of 3 rarely fires on small corpora. | 3 | B-02's evaluation shows anchor signals are insufficient. |
| Local embeddings (`[semantic]` extra) | A runtime dependency is a design change (AGENTS). | 3 | B-02's evaluation shows lexical plus structural recall below its floor. |
| Persisted clusters and local maintainer overrides (gitcrawl governance) | Conflicts with the never-persist rule for the derived tier; GitHub assignment is the shared claim. | 2 | — |
| Continue-on-error per-item failure ledger | It would advance the single watermark past a failed item and lose it. | 2 | — |
| `derived.db` sidecar, rank fusion, "sibling-heat" | Persistence conflict; rank fusion is not a symmetric magnitude; sibling-heat is self-reinforcing. | 2 | — |

item.body:
_Remediation issue. Generated from the SOTA review and bundling plan (`docs/plans/sota-and-bundling.md` rev 7 and `docs/plans/remote-and-multi-user.md` on branch `claude/upbeat-fermi-2fqehy`; plan reviewed by two independent critic passes). Every claim below was re-checked against origin/main b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5 on 2026-10-25 by source trace and/or an executed probe (baseline: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → `Ran 310 tests ... OK`). One issue = one PR. Tracking: #21._

## Summary
After this PR, ingesting one item costs about the same at 100 items as at 100,000. Today each item's ingest pays three costs that grow with corpus size, so a cold sync of a large repository is quadratic. After this PR, `item`, `related` and `what-closed` also read only the edges they return instead of every edge in the repo.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **The actor-edge DELETE scans every edge in the repo on every item ingest.** [VERIFIED by `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on a fresh v6 DB: `SEARCH edges USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_edges_1 (repo=?)`. The same predicate without `rel IN (...)`, or as a SELECT, plans on `idx_edges_dst`. Splitting it into `rel = 'authored'` equality deletes plans identically, so that is NOT a fix (independent critic, reproduced).]
   [store.py#L89-L92](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/store.py#L89-L92)
   ```py
       conn.execute(
           "DELETE FROM edges WHERE repo = ? AND dst_type = 'item' AND dst_id = ? "
           "AND rel IN ('authored', 'commented', 'reviewed')",
           (repo, nid),
   ```
2. **The title lookups read every item row, `raw_json` included, on every ingest:** one for revert PRs, two in the reverse revert pass. [VERIFIED by `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`: `SEARCH items USING INDEX idx_items_repo_merge (repo=?)`, which is non-covering.]
   [store.py#L363-L368](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/store.py#L363-L368)
   ```py
       def title_lookup(title: str) -> list[int]:
           rows = conn.execute(
               "SELECT number FROM items WHERE repo = ? AND title = ? AND number != ?",
               (repo, title, number),
           ).fetchall()
           return [int(r[0]) for r in rows]
   ```
   [store.py#L403-L407](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/store.py#L403-L407)
   ```py
           for variant in revert_title_variants(title):
               for row in conn.execute(
                   "SELECT number FROM items WHERE repo = ? AND title = ? AND number != ?",
                   (repo, variant, number),
               ).fetchall():
   ```
3. **`recount` runs three full COUNTs inside every item's transaction.** [VERIFIED by probe: 5 `recount` calls for a 5-item sync.]
   [store.py#L631-L632](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/store.py#L631-L632)
   ```py
       bump_watermark(conn, repo, list_raw.get("updated_at"))
       recount(conn, repo)
   ```
4. **Measured effect.** [VERIFIED twice, independently. The synthetic corpus had about 22–24 edges per item. Per-batch time grows linearly with corpus size:
   - this session: 12.3 → 32.0 → 51.4 → 69.1 s per 2,000 items (cProfile at 4k items: `delete_owned_edges` 11.7 ms/call, `recount` 3.6 ms);
   - critic: 4.98 → 21.82 s per 1,000 items, flattening to 2.23 → 2.36 s only with all three fixes applied.]
5. **The `item` and `related` edge query plans as a full repo-edge scan.** `related` runs it once per BFS frontier node. [VERIFIED: `SEARCH edges USING INDEX idx_edges_dst (repo=?)`.]
   [query.py#L331-L336](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L331-L336)
   ```py
           for x in conn.execute(
               f"SELECT src_type, src_id, rel, dst_type, dst_id, confidence, evidence{source_col} "
               "FROM edges WHERE repo = ? AND ("
               "(src_type = 'item' AND src_id = ?) OR (dst_type = 'item' AND dst_id = ?)"
               ")",
               (r, str(n), str(n)),
   ```
6. **`what_closed` PR rows scan every `closes` row,** and `path_between` loads every repo edge into Python on each call. [VERIFIED: `SEARCH edges USING COVERING INDEX ux_edges_closes_pair (repo=? AND src_type=?)`; source trace below.]
   [query.py#L894-L900](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L894-L900)
   ```py
       if repo:
           pr_rows = conn.execute(
               f"SELECT src_id, evidence{source_col} FROM edges "
               "WHERE repo = ? AND src_type = 'item' AND rel = 'closes' "
               "AND dst_type = 'item' AND dst_id = ?",
               (repo, str(number)),
           ).fetchall()
   ```
   [query.py#L503-L506](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L503-L506)
   ```py
       rows = conn.execute(
           "SELECT src_type, src_id, rel, dst_type, dst_id FROM edges WHERE repo = ?",
           (repo,),
       ).fetchall()
   ```
7. **Prior art: the fix needs no migration.** A non-unique `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` in `schema.sql` reaches every store on its next write-open, because `init_schema` runs the script on every open. `idx_items_repo_merge` already does exactly this. [VERIFIED: [schema.sql#L50](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/schema.sql#L50), [db.py#L614](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/db.py#L614).]

> **argv convention note.** CONTRIBUTING:139 names `python -m pytest <file> -q`, and issues #1–#7 used `python -m unittest tests.<module>...`; both fail at base with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fixtures'` for the 23 test modules that `from fixtures import` (VERIFIED: `python -m pytest tests/test_store.py -q` → collection error; `python -m unittest tests.test_store` → ImportError). Every argv here therefore uses the form that works at base, `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p <file> -k <test> -b`, whose absence signature is `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5). [Workstream C] PR 1 of 1 repairs the documented forms.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN `store.delete_owned_edges` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL plan its actor-edge DELETE on `idx_edges_dst (repo=? AND dst_type=? AND dst_id=?)`, independent of `ANALYZE` statistics.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_ingest_scale.py" -k test_actor_delete_plan_uses_dst_index -b`
  - expect: FAIL: the plan text is `SEARCH edges USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_edges_1 (repo=?)` (probe-observed at base).
  - files: tests/test_ingest_scale.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 1; the check reads the plan from a fresh, never-analyzed DB.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN the revert-title lookups run THE SYSTEM SHALL plan them on an `items(repo, title)` index.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_ingest_scale.py" -k test_title_lookup_plan_uses_title_index -b`
  - expect: FAIL: the plan text is `SEARCH items USING INDEX idx_items_repo_merge (repo=?)`.
  - files: tests/test_ingest_scale.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 2.
- [ ] AC3: WHEN N items are ingested by one `sync_repo` run THE SYSTEM SHALL execute the corpus-wide `recount` O(1) times per listing page (or derive counts at read time), never once per item.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_ingest_scale.py" -k test_recount_not_per_item -b`
  - expect: FAIL: `recount` is called 5 times for a 5-item sync (probe-observed).
  - files: tests/test_ingest_scale.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 3.
- [ ] AC4: WHEN items 2,001 and 4,001 are ingested into synthetic corpora of 2,000 and 4,000 items THE SYSTEM SHALL execute a per-item VDBE step count (`conn.set_progress_handler`) at 4k that is within 1.25× of the count at 2k.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_ingest_scale.py" -k test_per_item_cost_is_flat -b`
  - expect: FAIL: the step ratio is about 2× (cost tracks edge count).
  - files: tests/test_ingest_scale.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 4. Deterministic: step counts, not wall clock.
- [ ] AC5: WHEN `item`, `related`, or `what-closed` reads the edges for one item THE SYSTEM SHALL plan each lookup as indexed equality searches (a `UNION ALL` of the src and dst lookups), never `(repo=?)` alone.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_ingest_scale.py" -k test_item_edge_reads_are_indexed -b`
  - expect: FAIL: the plans are `idx_edges_dst (repo=?)` and `ux_edges_closes_pair (repo=? AND src_type=?)`.
  - files: tests/test_ingest_scale.py
  - why: RED at base per claims 5–6.
- [ ] AC6: WHEN `sync_repo` finishes a run THE SYSTEM SHALL run `PRAGMA optimize` on the write connection.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_ingest_scale.py" -k test_sync_runs_pragma_optimize -b`
  - expect: FAIL: no `optimize` statement is traced (`conn.set_trace_callback`).
  - files: tests/test_ingest_scale.py
  - why: RED at base: `sync_repo` issues no optimize (source trace, `sync.py:317-646`).
- [ ] AC7: WHEN a v6 store is opened for writing after this PR THE SYSTEM SHALL gain the title index without a `user_version` bump, and the migration chain's idempotence SHALL hold.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_migrations.py" -k test_init_schema_is_idempotent -b`
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_migrations.py
  - why: GREEN at base; the index must ride `schema.sql`, not a migration.
- [ ] AC8: WHEN a full sync is followed by an incremental one THE SYSTEM SHALL keep today's inclusive-watermark semantics.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_sync.py" -k test_full_then_incremental_since -b`
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_sync.py
  - why: GREEN at base.
- [ ] AC9: WHEN a destination item is re-ingested THE SYSTEM SHALL keep inbound mentions from other items.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_store.py" -k test_inbound_mention_survives_destination_upsert -b`
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_store.py
  - why: GREEN at base; the rewritten deletes must not widen ownership.
- [ ] AC10: WHEN closes rows were pre-seeded as duplicates THE SYSTEM SHALL still collapse them on re-ingest.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_closes_edge_uniqueness.py" -k test_preseeded_duplicates_collapse_on_reingest -b`
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_closes_edge_uniqueness.py
  - why: GREEN at base.

## Scope
**In:** `INDEXED BY idx_edges_dst` on the actor DELETE; an `items(repo, title)` index in `schema.sql`; per-item `recount` removed (counts recomputed per page and at finish, or derived at read time); indexed `UNION ALL` edge reads in `item`/`related`/`what_closed`; `PRAGMA optimize` at the end of `sync_repo`.
**Out:** `path_between`'s whole-graph BFS (it stays O(E) per call; [Workstream B] PR 2 of 3 builds its own bounded adjacency and does not call it per pair); any schema-version bump.

## Sequence
[Workstream A] Ingest at scale and the evidence schema: #22 -> #23 -> #24 -> #25 -> #26 -> #27 (this issue is A-01). Workstream A owns the schema lane: each PR's migration lands in slot order.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: none
- Schema after: none (no `user_version` change)
- Gated on: none

## Files expected to change
`src/zaxbygraph/store.py` (hotspot), `src/zaxbygraph/schema.sql`, `src/zaxbygraph/sync.py` (hotspot), `src/zaxbygraph/query.py`, new `tests/test_ingest_scale.py`.

## Constraints and invariants
- The one-item-one-transaction watermark rule is unchanged.
- `status` counts must stay truthful at every committed boundary.
- Plans must not depend on `sqlite_stat1`, because read connections are `mode=ro` and cannot write it.
- The SQLite floor (3.35) is unchanged.

## Definition of done
All ACs pass on the Windows and Linux CI legs. The PR body says `Closes #<n>` and carries `## Closure evidence` with each AC's argv and result, plus one before/after batch-timing table on a synthetic 8k-item corpus.

Issue-tracer trace `23-sync-schema-drift-plumbing`: the red checkpoint for this PR work is frozen. Checks C1-C7 live in `tests/test_sync_plumbing.py` (authored in a separate fresh context), C8-C10 pin existing PRESERVING tests. Amended via the sanctioned CHECK_WRONG path: pages now derive from the already-captured call list (identical filter), C2-C7 re-frozen onto the amended bytes, each with a fresh pinned-base RED/GREEN replay (C2/C3/C5/C6 base RED -> head GREEN; C1/C4/C7 base ERROR -> head GREEN), amendment approved by the plan critic. ```

## Superseding checkpoint receipt v3 (C9/C10 blob reconciliation)

The frozen file tests/test_sync.py carries a sibling test (test_jsonl_writes_events_in_dir) pinning the pre-bundle sidecar record that this issue replaces; the shipped tree updates that sibling assertion to the item_bundle record. C9/C10 semantics are unchanged; the file blob was reconciled via CHECK_WRONG amend rows with fresh pinned-base GREEN/GREEN replays (verdict PASS both). Also superseding v2: same semantics digest, updated manifest + freeze tree.

```
issue-tracer-checkpoint-v1 slug=23-sync-schema-drift-plumbing manifest=c5e20233c098b3dd0e746d06170bee1779384c0d semantics=4c93884f51cf0bfb56c286152d7ddab76c65fbdb tree=8aa7e46f478710ff40d798cd3438329c36405e5e
```

PR published: https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/pull/37 — "feat: sync survives schema drift, records section completeness, refreshes exact items, writes a replayable sidecar" (head 309caff, base main).

**What changed**
- The GraphQL page query travels on stdin (`gh api graphql --input -`); no argv element carries query text, so Windows' command-line limit can never truncate a query again.
- A cached capability probe (one introspection per host+gh version, persisted in `meta`) omits each field the host's schema lacks — per field — and records every omission in `fetch_log`. Schema drift can no longer abort a sync; a per-field runtime error (e.g. FORBIDDEN on one section) drops only that section for the affected items.
- `ingest_item` now receives a per-section `children_complete` map (False for REST-fallback, cap-truncated, and 404-path sections).
- `sync --numbers N,M` re-ingests exactly those items through the bulk children path with the watermark, full-sync state, and freshness stamps untouched.
- `sync --jsonl` writes one replayable `item_bundle` record per item (deduplicable by `(number, item.updated_at)`), and `JsonlReplaySource` (`tests/replay.py`) replays recorded sidecars row-for-row — recorded deletions included.

**How to use**
No CLI changes beyond the new flag: `zaxbygraph sync --numbers 12,34` for a targeted refresh. Sidecar consumers move from the legacy per-payload records (and their `(resource, payload.id)` key) to `item_bundle` keyed `(number, item.updated_at)` — README documents both.

**Migration**
No migration required (no schema change; `meta` rows from the probe cache are inert on older code). Sidecar consumers that parsed per-child records need the one-line key change above.

**Verification**
348 tests OK locally; the 10 frozen acceptance checks replay RED→GREEN/GREEN→GREEN at a pinned base; 7/7 mutation probes kill; scan-deferred clean. Gate ladder: plan critic APPROVE (4 rounds), implementation reviewer APPROVE (3 rounds, incl. a real block-lead-granularity catch), final critic APPROVE. Checkpoint receipts (v1 + two superseding after sanctioned CHECK_WRONG amends) are on this issue. The trace lives in `.agents/issue-traces/23-sync-schema-drift-plumbing/`.

_Remediation issue. Generated from the SOTA review and bundling plan (`docs/plans/sota-and-bundling.md` rev 7 and `docs/plans/remote-and-multi-user.md` on branch `claude/upbeat-fermi-2fqehy`; plan reviewed by two independent critic passes). Every claim below was re-checked against origin/main b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5 on 2026-10-25 by source trace and/or an executed probe (baseline: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → `Ran 310 tests ... OK`). One issue = one PR. Tracking: #21._

## Summary
After this PR:
- **Schema drift cannot take down the sync.** Adding a GraphQL field can no longer abort every sync on hosts or tokens that lack it. A cached capability probe builds the query from the fields that exist. A per-field runtime error drops only that section and logs it.
- **The GraphQL query travels on stdin,** not argv.
- **Ingest knows which child sections were fetched complete,** which the observed-revision work in #25 needs.
- **`sync --numbers N,...` refreshes exact items without moving the watermark.**
- **The `--jsonl` sidecar becomes a replayable per-item record.** CI can then replay a recorded real corpus through the real ingest path.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **Any GraphQL error other than NOT_FOUND aborts the whole page query, and with it the sync.** [VERIFIED by probe: a `FORBIDDEN` error payload makes `_graphql` raise `GitHubError("Resource not accessible")`.] Two different failure shapes exist:
   - a field missing from the schema is a *validation* error that rejects the whole query, so only a probe can prevent it;
   - a runtime per-field error (FORBIDDEN, partial `data`) can be dropped per section.
   [graphql.py#L357-L366](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/graphql.py#L357-L366)
   ```py
               hard = [
                   e
                   for e in (errors if isinstance(errors, list) else [])
                   if isinstance(e, dict)
                   and str(e.get("type", "")).upper() != "NOT_FOUND"
                   and "Could not resolve to an issue" not in str(e.get("message", ""))
                   and "Could not resolve to a pullRequest" not in str(e.get("message", ""))
               ]
               if hard or not isinstance(data.get("data"), dict):
                   raise self._with_rate_budget(GitHubError(message, status=status))
   ```
2. **The query is passed in argv,** and chunk size is clamped to stay under the Windows command-line limit. Every added field shrinks chunks and adds calls. [VERIFIED. `gh api --help` (gh 2.89.0) documents `--input -` for a stdin request body.]
   [graphql.py#L304](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/graphql.py#L304)
   ```py
           cmd = [self.gh_bin, "api", "graphql", "-f", f"query={query}"]
   ```
3. **Ingest never learns whether a child section was complete.** `*_incomplete` flags are resolved by REST fallback before ingest, and `timeline` is always a list. [VERIFIED: [sync.py#L166-L182](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/sync.py#L166-L182), [sync.py#L206](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/sync.py#L206).]
4. **`ingest_item` always bumps the watermark,** so a targeted refresh of a recently updated item would skip every item updated between the old watermark and it. [VERIFIED by probe: one `ingest_item` call with `updated_at` ahead of `issues_since` advanced the watermark to that item's timestamp.] There is no `sync --numbers`: `zaxbygraph sync --numbers 1` exits 2 with `unrecognized arguments: --numbers 1`.
   [store.py#L631](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/store.py#L631)
   ```py
       bump_watermark(conn, repo, list_raw.get("updated_at"))
   ```

   [VERIFIED by probe through `PageShapedBulkSource`: `issue_comment` has `number` absent; `pr_file` has `number` absent and `id=None`.]
   [sync.py#L539-L549](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/sync.py#L539-L549)
   ```py
                           _write_jsonl(jsonl_handle, "item", list_raw)
                           if pull_raw:

                           for rec in issue_comments:
                               _write_jsonl(jsonl_handle, "issue_comment", rec)
                           for rec in review_comments:
                               _write_jsonl(jsonl_handle, "review_comment", rec)
                           for rec in reviews:
                               _write_jsonl(jsonl_handle, "review", rec)
                           for rec in files:
                               _write_jsonl(jsonl_handle, "pr_file", rec)
   ```
6. **No test source can replay a recorded sidecar through bulk ingest.** `FakeGitHubSource` has no `fetch_children`, and timeline events have no REST fallback. [VERIFIED: [fixtures.py#L134-L222](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/tests/fixtures.py#L134-L222), [sync.py#L201-L205](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/sync.py#L201-L205).]

_Remediation issue. Generated from the SOTA review and bundling plan (`docs/plans/sota-and-bundling.md` rev 7 and `docs/plans/remote-and-multi-user.md` on branch `claude/upbeat-fermi-2fqehy`; plan reviewed by two independent critic passes). Every claim below was re-checked against origin/main b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5 on 2026-10-25 by source trace and/or an executed probe (baseline: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → `Ran 310 tests ... OK`). One issue = one PR. Tracking: #21._

## Summary
After this PR (migration v7), an agent can rank and gate work from stored data without parsing `raw_json`:

- reactions
- comment count
- author association
- milestone
- issue type
- sub-issue progress
- open and total blocked-by and blocking counts
- assignees
- issue field values
- comment author association

Two search gaps also close: text that appears only in review bodies becomes searchable, and a PR can be found by searching for a path it touched. `status` gains a `coverage` block, so "absent upstream" is distinguishable from "not fetched".

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **The data is already stored but unmodeled.** No column, child table or edge exists for any of these signals, and `raw_json` holds the merged listing and pull payload. [VERIFIED: [schema.sql#L15-L44](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/schema.sql#L15-L44), [store.py#L587-L610](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/store.py#L587-L610).]
2. **The live REST listing carries every field.** Issue rows carry `assignees`, `author_association`, `milestone`, `reactions`, `type`, `sub_issues_summary`, `issue_dependencies_summary` (`blocked_by`, `blocking`, `total_blocked_by`, `total_blocking`), and `issue_field_values`. PR rows lack the two summaries. [VERIFIED live, twice, with `gh api repos/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/issues?state=all` (gh 2.89.0).] Checks bind to recorded fixtures, never to a live call (CONTRIBUTING repo notes).
3. **Review-only text is unsearchable.** [VERIFIED by probe: a token present only in a review body → `search` `total_matches: 0`. Search unions `items_fts` and `comments_fts` only: [query.py#L112-L135](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L112-L135).]
4. **A PR cannot be found by a path it touched.** [VERIFIED by probe: `search "zz_unique_path"` → 0 for a PR touching `src/zz_unique_path.py`.]
5. **Upserts replace the whole row,** so a column that only one source supplies would be nulled by a re-ingest from the other source. [VERIFIED: [store.py#L161-L180](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/store.py#L161-L180).]
6. **JSON1 cannot be relied on for the backfill.** It is only built in from SQLite 3.38, and the floor is 3.35. [VERIFIED: [db.py#L21](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/db.py#L21).]

> **argv convention note.** CONTRIBUTING:139 names `python -m pytest <file> -q`, and issues #1–#7 used `python -m unittest tests.<module>...`; both fail at base with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fixtures'` for the 23 test modules that `from fixtures import` (VERIFIED: `python -m pytest tests/test_store.py -q` → collection error; `python -m unittest tests.test_store` → ImportError). Every argv here therefore uses the form that works at base, `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p <file> -k <test> -b`, whose absence signature is `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5). [Workstream C] PR 1 of 1 repairs the documented forms.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN an issue whose listing payload carries reactions, assignees, milestone, type, sub-issue and dependency summaries is ingested THE SYSTEM SHALL expose each as a typed `items` column or child row (`assignees`, `issue_field_values`), with open and total dependency counts kept distinct.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_payload_signals.py" -k test_listing_fields_become_columns -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_payload_signals.py
  - why: There are no columns at base.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN a v6 store is migrated to v7 THE SYSTEM SHALL backfill those columns from stored `raw_json` using Python `json`, with no SQLite JSON functions and no GitHub calls; keys absent from old payloads stay NULL.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_payload_signals.py" -k test_v7_backfill_from_raw_json -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_payload_signals.py
  - why: There is no v7 at base.
- [ ] AC3: WHEN a REST re-ingest follows a GraphQL ingest THE SYSTEM SHALL keep source-specific column values (COALESCE on absent) rather than nulling them.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_payload_signals.py" -k test_source_specific_columns_survive_rest_reingest -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_payload_signals.py
  - why: Claim 5; the columns do not exist at base.
- [ ] AC4: WHEN a term appears only in a review body THE SYSTEM SHALL return the owning item from `search`, merged like comment hits.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_payload_signals.py" -k test_review_only_text_is_searchable -b`
  - expect: FAIL: `total_matches` is 0 (probe-observed).
  - files: tests/test_payload_signals.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 3.
- [ ] AC5: WHEN a search term matches a path segment of a file a PR touched THE SYSTEM SHALL return that PR, with path text weighted below title and body.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_payload_signals.py" -k test_changed_path_is_searchable -b`
  - expect: FAIL: `total_matches` is 0 (probe-observed).
  - files: tests/test_payload_signals.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 4.
- [ ] AC6: WHEN `status` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL include `coverage`: counts of `fetch_log` truncation notes by kind, capability-dropped fields, rows with NULL v7 columns, and the store's size in bytes.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_payload_signals.py" -k test_status_reports_coverage -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_payload_signals.py
  - why: There is no coverage block at base.
- [ ] AC7: WHEN GraphQL comment nodes are fetched and the probe reports `authorAssociation` THE SYSTEM SHALL store comment `author_association` (REST supplies it natively).
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_payload_signals.py" -k test_comment_author_association -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_payload_signals.py
  - why: There is no column at base; the GraphQL selection lacks it ([graphql.py#L57-L69](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/graphql.py#L57-L69)).
- [ ] AC8: WHEN fresh and migrated stores are compared THE SYSTEM SHALL tokenize identically.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_search.py" -k test_fresh_db_and_migrated_db_share_tokenizer -b`
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_search.py
  - why: GREEN at base; the FTS rebuild must keep parity.
- [ ] AC9: WHEN `init_schema` re-runs THE SYSTEM SHALL be idempotent.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_migrations.py" -k test_init_schema_is_idempotent -b`
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_migrations.py
  - why: GREEN at base.

## Scope
**In:** migration v7: the columns, `assignees`, `issue_field_values`, comment `author_association`, `reviews_fts` (external content plus triggers), an FTS path-text column, `status.coverage`; the COALESCE rule; the `docs/schema.md` and `schema_notes.py` rows.
**Out:** link relations (#27); revisions (#25).

## Sequence
[Workstream A] Ingest at scale and the evidence schema: #22 -> #23 -> #24 -> #25 -> #26 -> #27 (this issue is A-03). Workstream A owns the schema lane: each PR's migration lands in slot order.

**What changed**

2. **Re-ingest deletes every comment and review before reinserting the current set,** so an upstream deletion leaves no trace. [VERIFIED:]
   [store.py#L63-L67](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/store.py#L63-L67)
   ```py

       conn.execute("DELETE FROM labels WHERE repo = ? AND number = ?", (repo, number))
       conn.execute("DELETE FROM comments WHERE repo = ? AND number = ?", (repo, number))
       conn.execute("DELETE FROM reviews WHERE repo = ? AND number = ?", (repo, number))
   ```

  - class: NEW-SURFACE

  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.

- [ ] AC5: WHEN `item N --as-of T` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL return each entity's version whose `[valid_from, valid_to)` contains T, and report `as_of_basis`.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_revisions.py" -k test_item_as_of -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.

OK`). One issue = one PR. Tracking: #21._

## Summary
After this PR (migration v9), each item keeps four kinds of mechanically extracted references from its text:
- **File paths.** Raw path strings mentioned in bodies, comments and reviews: stack frames, `blob/` URLs and backticked paths.
- **Error signatures.** Exception class names, masked error lines and frame function names.
- **Branch-name links.** A link to the issue a PR's branch name points at (`branch_ref`).
- **Reference positions.** The position of every `#N` reference.

Paths are stored raw and resolved against the known file vocabulary at **read** time. That keeps them independent of sync order: an issue ingested before the PR that adds `src/x.py` still resolves later.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **Items link to files only through PR files.** `touches` is emitted only from PR files, so an open issue reaches no file. [VERIFIED:]
   [extract.py#L173-L179](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/extract.py#L173-L179)
   ```py
   def edges_from_files(number: int, files: Iterable[dict]) -> list[tuple]:
       edges: list[tuple] = []
       for rec in files:
           path = rec.get("filename") or rec.get("path")
           if path:
               edges.append(("item", str(number), "touches", "file", str(path), "pulls.files", "payload"))
       return edges
   ```
2. **Every `#N` is treated alike, prose digits included.** [VERIFIED by probe: `parse_mentioned_numbers("Repro: step #2 then click")` → `[2]`.] The position is not recorded, so a reader cannot weight title and lead references above incidental ones.
   [extract.py#L67-L71](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/extract.py#L67-L71)
   ```py
       for match in re.finditer(rf"(?i){re.escape(repo)}#(\d+)\b", local):
           nums.add(int(match.group(1)))
       for match in re.finditer(r"(?<[A-Za-z0-9._-])#(\d+)\b", local):
           nums.add(int(match.group(1)))
       return nums
   ```
3. **`head_ref` is stored, but no edge derives from branch names.** [VERIFIED: `upsert_item_row` stores `head_ref` ([store.py#L201-L202](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/store.py#L201-L202)); `RELATIONS` has no branch relation ([extract.py#L253-L269](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/extract.py#L253-L269)).]

**Design note (binding).** Path *resolution* must not happen at ingest, because the vocabulary grows as later PRs ingest. Resolving at ingest would make edges depend on sync order, or require rewrites outside the owning item's transaction.

> **argv convention note.** CONTRIBUTING:139 names `python -m pytest <file> -q`, and issues #1–#7 used `python -m unittest tests.<module>...`; both fail at base with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fixtures'` for the 23 test modules that `from fixtures import` (VERIFIED: `python -m pytest tests/test_store.py -q` → collection error; `python -m unittest tests.test_store` → ImportError). Every argv here therefore uses the form that works at base, `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p <file> -k <test> -b`, whose absence signature is `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5). [Workstream C] PR 1 of 1 repairs the documented forms.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC2: WHEN a foreign-repo `blob/` URL appears THE SYSTEM SHALL store no path ref for it.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE

  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.

  - class: NEW-SURFACE

OK`). One issue = one PR. Tracking: #21._

## Summary
After this PR (migration v10), sync records these links from the fields GitHub itself reports:
- **dependencies** (`blocked_by`)
- **sub-issue parents** (`child_of`)
- **duplicates** (`duplicate_of`)
- **reopen events**
- **open PRs that reference an issue**
- **PR commit messages** (`fixes #N` in a commit becomes a `closes_keyword` edge with commit provenance)

A keyword `duplicate_keyword` stream gives REST-only corpora partial duplicate coverage.

Link edges use a new presence-gated `source='link'` stream:
- they are replaced only when the section was fetched **complete**;
- a degraded re-ingest never retracts them;
- an overflowed connection is union-only.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **Issue nodes select only `databaseId`, comments and the timeline.** [VERIFIED:]
   [graphql.py#L170-L174](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/graphql.py#L170-L174)
   ```py
   _ISSUE_FIELDS = f"""
   databaseId
   {_ISSUE_COMMENT_NODES}
   {_TIMELINE_NODES}
   """
   ```
2. **The timeline captures two event types only.** [VERIFIED: [graphql.py#L141](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/graphql.py#L141), [graphql.py#L280](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/graphql.py#L280).]
3. **The official GraphQL schema exposes every field this PR needs.** [VERIFIED twice, independently, against `github/docs` `src/graphql/data/fpt/schema.docs.graphql`:]
   - `Issue.blockedBy`, `parent`, `issueType`, `duplicateOf`;
   - `closedByPullRequestsReferences(first, includeClosedPrs, excludeUserLinked, orderByState)`;
   - `PullRequest.commits`;
   - `Commit.messageHeadline`/`messageBody`;
   - `REOPENED_EVENT`.

   `stateReason(enableDuplicate:)` is marked for removal and must not be requested.
4. **Payload-sourced outbound edges are deleted on every re-ingest and only rebuilt from the payload in hand.** A degraded re-ingest would therefore silently drop link facts if they used `source='payload'`. [VERIFIED:]
   [store.py#L84-L88](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/store.py#L84-L88)
   ```py
       conn.execute(
           "DELETE FROM edges WHERE repo = ? AND src_type = 'item' AND src_id = ? "
           "AND source NOT IN ('timeline', 'closing_ref')",
           (repo, nid),
       )
   ```

> **argv convention note.** CONTRIBUTING:139 names `python -m pytest <file> -q`, and issues #1–#7 used `python -m unittest tests.<module>...`; both fail at base with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fixtures'` for the 23 test modules that `from fixtures import` (VERIFIED: `python -m pytest tests/test_store.py -q` → collection error; `python -m unittest tests.test_store` → ImportError). - [ ] AC3: WHEN `parent` and `duplicateOf` are fetched THE SYSTEM SHALL write `child_of` and `duplicate_of` link edges from the owner's side, cross-repo endpoints repo-qualified.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_link_stream.py" -k test_parent_and_duplicate_edges -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_link_stream.py

- [ ] AC4: WHEN `closedByPullRequestsReferences(includeClosedPrs: false)` is fetched THE SYSTEM SHALL record the issue's open linked PRs from GitHub's own report.

## PR opened: #42 — feat: export-corpus writes a deterministic, hash-stamped corpus snapshot

**What changed.** `zaxbygraph export-corpus` writes a deterministic, hash-stamped JSONL snapshot of one store (`zaxbygraph.corpus.v1`): a manifest line (counts, `corpus_sha256`, store completeness, an unhashed `provenance` block), one canonical-JSON line per item (each with a `content_hash`) and per release, an optional `revisions` line (`--include revisions`), and an `orphan_edges` trailer. Two exports of one store are byte-identical; a no-op sync leaves `corpus_sha256` unchanged (the hash domain is stored content — canonical `sort_keys` JSON — and excludes the SQLite-assigned `comments.pk`/`edges.id`/`revisions.id` and sync provenance that every no-op sync rewrites); Windows and Linux produce the same hash (binary `\n` writes; a pinned golden constant is asserted on both CI legs); a replayed `--jsonl` sidecar exports the same hash as the original store. Every edge is emitted exactly once (src item → dst item for actor/commit/foreign sources → `orphan_edges` trailer). All reads run under one `BEGIN DEFERRED` snapshot, released before the destination copy, so a concurrent sync cannot split the corpus.

**How to use it.**
```
zaxbygraph export-corpus [--out F] [--include raw,patches,revisions] [--require-complete]
```
No `--out` → the snapshot goes to stdout as bytes. Guarded refusals: `repo_required` (`--repo ''`), `out_is_database` (realpath+samefile vs the db and `-wal`/`-shm`), `store_too_old` (schema < v10), `bad_include`, `incomplete_store` (with `--require-complete`). Contains GitHub user content verbatim — treat the artifact accordingly.

**Migration.** No migration required — new command, no schema change, no store writes. Stores below schema v10 need one regular `sync` run to migrate first.

**Verification.** 7 frozen acceptance checks (C1–C6 RED→GREEN against the frozen base, C7 GREEN→GREEN), 16-test module, full suite 488 tests OK, three independent gate contexts re-ran the evidence at the shipped head 8a33a7b. The first line is a manifest, followed by one line per item and one per release. Each item carries a sha256 `content_hash`, and the manifest carries a `corpus_sha256` over content only.

Two exports of one database are byte-identical, and a sync that fetched nothing new leaves `corpus_sha256` unchanged. Bundles, evaluation runs and git snapshots can therefore cite the exact corpus they used.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **No snapshot artifact exists.** The `--jsonl` sidecar is an append-only fetch log, which README itself says "may duplicate lines". [VERIFIED:]
   [sync.py#L297-L302](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/sync.py#L297-L302)
   ```py
   def _write_jsonl(handle: TextIO | None, resource: str, payload: object) -> None:
       if handle is None:
           return
       handle.write(json.dumps({"resource": resource, "payload": payload}, ensure_ascii=False))
       handle.write("\n")
       handle.flush()
   ```
2. **A sync that fetches nothing new still rewrites row ids.** It re-ingests the inclusive boundary item, which deletes and reinserts its comments and edges and changes `comments.pk`/`edges.id`. A naive dump would therefore change after such a sync. [VERIFIED: [store.py#L63-L67](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/store.py#L63-L67), [store.py#L84-L93](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/store.py#L84-L93); inclusive watermark per AGENTS.]
3. **`closes` evidence depends on ingest order.** Evidence merges first-seen-first, so the hash domain must be defined over stored content, not ingest order. [VERIFIED: [store.py#L109-L137](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/store.py#L109-L137).]

> **argv convention note.** CONTRIBUTING:139 names `python -m pytest <file> -q`, and issues #1–#7 used `python -m unittest tests.<module>...`; both fail at base with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fixtures'` for the 23 test modules that `from fixtures import` (VERIFIED: `python -m pytest tests/test_store.py -q` → collection error; `python -m unittest tests.test_store` → ImportError). Every argv here therefore uses the form that works at base, `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p <file> -k <test> -b`, whose absence signature is `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5). [Workstream C] PR 1 of 1 repairs the documented forms.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN `export-corpus --out F` runs twice on one store THE SYSTEM SHALL write byte-identical files (UTF-8, `\n`, `sort_keys` canonical JSON).
  - class: NEW-SURFACE

  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_export_corpus.py
  - why: There is no command at base.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN a sync that fetches nothing new runs between two exports THE SYSTEM SHALL produce equal `corpus_sha256`. The hashed domain excludes `comments.pk`, `edges.id`, `revisions.id`, `fetch_log` and sync timestamps, which go in an unhashed `provenance` block.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE

  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.

- [ ] AC3: WHEN edges are exported THE SYSTEM SHALL emit every edge exactly once: under its `src` item, under its `dst` item when `src` is an actor or a foreign `owner/repo#N`, or in an `orphan_edges` trailer when neither endpoint item is stored.

OK`). One issue = one PR. Tracking: #21._

## Summary
After this PR, the derived read tier answers which items are related and why:
- **`similar N`** returns related items with per-signal evidence. The signals are lexical, title, error signature, direct files, analog files, co-change, structural and context.
- **`explain A B`** shows the full breakdown for one pair.
- **`coupling PATH`** reports which files change together.

Everything is computed at query time on a `mode=ro` connection, temp objects only, and marked `derived: true` (AGENTS).

**`zaxbygraph eval similar|localize|bundle`** measures retrieval quality against ground truth already in the graph:
- `duplicate_of` pairs;
- files touched by a merged fix PR;
- issue sets that one PR closed.

The evaluation runs on a leakage-controlled, time-split snapshot. A recorded real corpus is replayed in CI, and score floors are asserted on it.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **`related` is edge incidence only.** It returns edges where the item is an endpoint, so two issues sharing files, labels or vocabulary are never connected. [VERIFIED:]
   [query.py#L366-L370](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L366-L370)
   ```py
                   f"SELECT {edge_columns} "
                   "FROM edges WHERE repo = ? AND ("
                   "(src_type = 'item' AND src_id = ?) OR (dst_type = 'item' AND dst_id = ?)"
                   ")",
                   (repo, nid, nid),
   ```
2. **No similarity, co-change or evaluation code exists in `src/`.** [VERIFIED by grep over `src/zaxbygraph/` for `similar`, `coupling`, `eval`: no command or function.]
3. **Temp objects work on `mode=ro` read connections.** A temp `fts5vocab` table can therefore supply term statistics without writing the store. _Remediation issue. Generated from the SOTA review and bundling plan (`docs/plans/sota-and-bundling.md` rev 7 and `docs/plans/remote-and-multi-user.md` on branch `claude/upbeat-fermi-2fqehy`; plan reviewed by two independent critic passes). OK`). One issue = one PR. Tracking: #21._

## Summary
After this PR:

**`triage`** ranks workable open issues with a transparent heuristic that shows every input:
- **demand:** reactions, participants, comments, inbound duplicates and mentions;
- **leverage:** items it blocks, sub-issue gap, milestone due date;
- **risk:** reopen count, hotspot and revert history of its files, and a regression flag;
- **explicit:** issue type, label weights and issue-field values.

Each excluded issue states why: blocked, assigned, has an open linked PR, or locked.

**`bundle`** proposes 2–3-issue bundles **for one agent to work in sequence**. Each bundle carries:
- per-pair rationale and its file set (direct, linked and analog);
- the tests that historically co-changed with those files;
- open-PR collisions and dependency order;
- a risk summary and a `why_not_bigger` explanation;
- a stable `bundle_id`.

By default, bundles shown together never share files.

**`brief N`** returns a token-budgeted work packet. GitHub-authored text is marked untrusted. CI and review state appear only under `--live`, read live and never stored.

The bundled skill also gains the recipe for picking and bundling work.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **`open` cannot rank anything.** It returns no labels, assignees, linkage or demand signals, sorts only by recency, and the CLI passes no limit. [VERIFIED: `zaxbygraph open --limit 5` → exit 2 `unrecognized arguments: --limit 5`.]
   [query.py#L429-L437](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L429-L437)
   ```py
   def open_items(
       conn: sqlite3.Connection,
       repo: str | None = None,
       limit: int | None = None,
       offset: int = 0,
   ) -> list[dict]:
       repo = _fold_repo(repo)
       sql = """
           SELECT repo, number, kind, title, author, updated_at, html_url
   ```
2. **`churn` counts unmerged PRs,** so it is not a hotspot signal. [VERIFIED by probe: a closed, unmerged PR (`merged_at` NULL) is counted in `churn`.]
   [query.py#L415-L419](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L415-L419)
   ```py
       sql = """
           SELECT path, COUNT(*) AS prs,
                  SUM(additions) AS additions, SUM(deletions) AS deletions
           FROM pr_files
       """
   ```
3. **No ranking, bundling or work-packet command exists.** [VERIFIED by grep over `src/zaxbygraph/`.]

**Evidence-based constraints** (each source retrieved and confirmed this session):
- CooperBench (arXiv 2601.13295) finds about 30% lower success when agents split coupled work, so a bundle is for **one** agent.
- AgenticFlict (2604.03551) finds 27.67% of 107K agent PRs conflict, and Co-Coder (2606.00953) gains from cohesion-aware partitioning with hub isolation, so **cross-bundle file disjointness is the default**.
- ChainSWE (2607.02606) finds per-bug success falls up to 70% along dependent chains, so **the size cap is 3, with dependency order kept**.

> **argv convention note.** CONTRIBUTING:139 names `python -m pytest <file> -q`, and issues #1–#7 used `python -m unittest tests.<module>...`; both fail at base with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fixtures'` for the 23 test modules that `from fixtures import` (VERIFIED: `python -m pytest tests/test_store.py -q` → collection error; `python -m unittest tests.test_store` → ImportError). [Workstream C] PR 1 of 1 repairs the documented forms.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN `triage` runs on a fixture THE SYSTEM SHALL order open issues exactly by the documented formula over the echoed weights, and return every raw feature and gate reason; before #27 lands, A06-dependent features are `null` with `requires`.

  - why: There is no command at base.

  - class: NEW-SURFACE

  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.

  - class: NEW-SURFACE

  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.

- [ ] AC4: WHEN a bundle is returned THE SYSTEM SHALL include the per-pair rationale, a direct/linked/analog file split, historically co-changed tests (config globs), open-PR collisions, the in-pool `blocked_by` order, the risk summary, `why_not_bigger`, and `bundle_id` = sha1 of the sorted members plus the config hash.

  - class: DISCRIMINATING

**Out:** MCP tools (#32).

OK`). One issue = one PR. Tracking: #21._

## Summary
After this PR:
- **Closure reads.** `file-history` and `what-closed` report keyword-derived closures (as a separate `keyword_closes` field, never merged into GitHub-reported `closes`), so a REST-only store stops answering "closed nothing".
- **Environment checks on reads.** Read paths enforce the SQLite floor and probe for FTS5 with a clear message.
- **Proxy remotes resolve.** Remote and cloud sessions whose origin is a loopback git proxy resolve the repo, with the same normalization rule zmem uses.
- **Bounded reads.** `item` can cap comments, and CLI reads can bound staleness with `--max-age`.
- **CI and docs.** CI covers the Python versions people actually run, the skill carries a version stamp tested against the CLI, and the documented check commands work.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **Keyword closures are invisible to `file-history` and `what-closed`.** [VERIFIED by probe: on a REST-sourced store where PR #2 says `Fixes #1`, the only edge is `closes_keyword` (`source=keyword`), `file_history` returns `closed_issues: []` and `what_closed(1)` returns `prs: []`.]

   ```py
               closes = conn.execute(
                   f"SELECT dst_id{source_col} FROM edges "
                   "WHERE repo = ? AND src_type = 'item' AND src_id = ? "
                   "AND rel = 'closes' AND dst_type = 'item'",
                   (repo, str(n)),
               ).fetchall()
   ```

   [db.py#L35-L37](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/db.py#L35-L37)
   ```py
   def connect(db_path: Path) -> sqlite3.Connection:
       assert_sqlite_supported()

   ```

   ```py
       info = _parse_remote_info(proc.stdout)
   ```

   [ci.yml#L18](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L18)
   ```yaml
           python-version: ["3.11", "3.12"]
   ```
6. **The documented check commands fail at base.** Both `python -m pytest <file> -q` (CONTRIBUTING:139) and `python -m unittest tests.<module>` fail to import 23 test modules (`No module named 'fixtures'`). [VERIFIED by running both.] The skill has no version stamp (VERIFIED by grep), while `zaxbygraph --version` reports `0.4.0`.

## Summary
After this PR:
- **`snapshot publish`** pushes a verified store snapshot as a single-commit orphan. It runs under the sync lock, takes a `Connection.backup()` copy, vacuums it, gzips it, splits it under 100 MB and writes a manifest of hashes.
- **Where the snapshot lives.** Either a non-`heads` ref in the repo itself, so access matches the repo's, or a private store repo. `gh` stays the only credential.
- **`snapshot pull`** verifies every hash, runs `quick_check`, refuses a newer schema, and never replaces a newer local store. It records snapshot provenance, and `--verify-sample N` optionally re-fetches N random items to compare `content_hash`.
- **After the pull**, a normal incremental `sync` fetches only the delta.
- **One writer, many readers.** One machine or one scheduled Action using `GITHUB_TOKEN` (not a PAT) publishes. Everyone else only pulls.

item.title: [Workstream E] PR 1 of 1: A traveling laptop, cloud session or teammate starts warm from a verified git snapshot

item.body:
Closes #22
PR head: 0edd79399b0e07859b640a33dc16810f8c1e0448

## Summary

Cold sync no longer scales quadratically. Per-item ingest sheds its three corpus-sized costs: the actor-edge DELETE pins `INDEXED BY idx_edges_dst` (the `rel IN (...)` term flipped the planner to the repo-only unique-index scan), revert-title lookups seek on a new additive `items(repo, title)` index, and `recount` moves out of the per-item transaction to sync finish. `item` and `related` edge reads become a multiplicity-preserving `UNION ALL` of two full-key seeks (the dst arm excludes src-arm rows, so self-incident edges keep their exact original multiplicity); `what_closed`'s closes lookup pins `INDEXED BY idx_edges_dst`. `sync_repo` runs `PRAGMA optimize` at finish (advisory planner maintenance; nothing depends on sqlite_stat1). What changed in this PR This PR fixes a quadratic cold-sync cost and eliminates full-edge-table scans in graph reads for this stdlib-only Python CLI. Graph reads (`item`, `related`) switch from an `OR` predicate to a multiplicity-preserving `UNION ALL` of two indexed equality seeks, and `what_closed` pins `INDEXED BY idx_edges_dst`. `sync_repo` also issues advisory `PRAGMA optimize` at finish.
