*Provenance: generated from the swarm-pr-review + swarm-pr-feedback closeout of PR #35 (post-publication review of issue #22's implementation). Every claim below was re-checked against origin/main at commit 93201e5025c3bf51255ed7ab725c5ceb703d3cb2 (PR #35's squash merge) on 2026-10-25 by source read and grep. One issue = one PR. Improvement items filed with the maintainer's in-session approval (2026-10-25: "file a detailed issue on the repo using the contributing.md guidance" — the covenant's ASK/approval path, CONTRIBUTING.md:112/132). Probe evidence cited from the PR #35 review lanes lives partly in out-of-repo artifacts (the issue-tracer trace at `.agents/issue-traces/22-cold-sync-scale-indexed-reads/`, git-excluded) and is quoted inline where load-bearing. Background: #22, #35, epic #21.*

## Summary

After this PR, the frozen acceptance checks introduced by #22 assert the SQL the code actually executes (C2 and C6 join C1's runtime-capture discipline), the acceptance corpus costs about 4x less wall time on every CI leg with identical RED/GREEN discrimination, and AGENTS.md's agent contract names the count-freshness boundary that `status` consumers currently discover only in `docs/schema.md`.

## Problem (claims to verify)

1. **Claim 1 — VERIFIED (source read at the anchor commit; mutant probe executed during the PR #35 review):** C2 asserts a hand-copied SQL literal, not the statement the code executes.
   [tests/test_ingest_scale.py#L309-L311](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/93201e5025c3bf51255ed7ab725c5ceb703d3cb2/tests/test_ingest_scale.py#L309-L311)

   ```py
               "EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT number FROM items "
               "WHERE repo = ? AND title = ? AND number != ?",
               (REPO, "some title", 1),
   ```

   A mutant rewriting the shipped lookup (`store.title_lookup`) to an unindexable `LOWER(title) = LOWER(?)` predicate leaves C2 GREEN; only C4's runtime ratio catches it (probed 1.948 during review). Prior-art reconciliation: C1 was amended in 2e2bfc2 to exactly this runtime-capture form (its round-3 amendment rejected the copied-literal pattern); C2 predates that amendment and was left in the old shape. Cubic's query.py:299 note and the review's UR-4 finding (per-node `PRAGMA table_info`) are already fixed in 0edd793 and are not re-raised here.

2. **Claim 2 — VERIFIED (source read at the anchor commit):** C6 asserts presence, not position, of `PRAGMA optimize`.
   [tests/test_ingest_scale.py#L699](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/93201e5025c3bf51255ed7ab725c5ceb703d3cb2/tests/test_ingest_scale.py#L699)

   ```py
               any("pragma optimize" in s for s in normalized),
   ```

   A mutant issuing the statement at the start of `sync_repo` passes C6 while defeating the change's purpose (the shipped placement is after the finish commit, [src/zaxbygraph/sync.py#L613](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/93201e5025c3bf51255ed7ab725c5ceb703d3cb2/src/zaxbygraph/sync.py#L613), best-effort per 0edd793). Position is the load-bearing property the review confirmed: the statement is advisory and must never precede or gate the data path.

3. **Claim 3 — VERIFIED (probes executed on the review; numbers implementer-reported and consistent with the shipped check):** the C4 acceptance corpus is fsync-bound and oversized for its discrimination.
   [tests/test_ingest_scale.py#L53-L54](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/93201e5025c3bf51255ed7ab725c5ceb703d3cb2/tests/test_ingest_scale.py#L53-L54)

   ```py
   CORPUS_SMALL = 2000
   CORPUS_LARGE = 4000
   ```

   The whole-run leg is ~93% commit-fsync (23.3s -> 1.51s with `synchronous=OFF` on the review probe) and adds ~97s of suite wall across the 4 CI legs. Probed at 1k/2k: the pin-reverted mutant still FAILS (item-txn ratio 1.961, whole-run 1.8377) while head stays flat (1.0000/1.0006) — same RED/GREEN separation, ~4x less work.

4. **Claim 4 — VERIFIED (absence grep at the anchor commit):** AGENTS.md is silent on count freshness, while `status` counts are now finish-time snapshots. Absence evidence: the invariant sections beginning at line 27 carry no count-freshness clause (grep for "count" over the invariants finds nothing).
   [docs/schema.md#L315](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/93201e5025c3bf51255ed7ab725c5ceb703d3cb2/docs/schema.md#L315)

   ```py
   The three counts are recomputed when a sync run finishes (and by
   ```

   `docs/schema.md` and `schema_notes.py` document the boundary (count-refresh points: sync finish, `doctor --consolidate`, migrations; identity-line vs `where` divergence), but an agent reading AGENTS.md alone treats `status.item_count` as corpus truth. Prior-art reconciliation: this extends #22's disclosed trade (finish-only recount), not a new behavior.

## Scope

**In:** the C2 and C6 check amendments to runtime/position-capture forms (one checkpoint AMEND, reason `CHECK_WRONG`, with fresh RED/GREEN replays of all six discriminating checks, re-anchored receipt, and amendment approval per the trace contract); C4's `CORPUS_SMALL`/`CORPUS_LARGE` moved to 1000/2000 in the same AMEND; one count-freshness bullet in AGENTS.md's invariants.
**Out:** every other row of PR #35's "Considered, not filed" table (they stay closed under their recorded re-evaluate triggers): `PRAGMA optimize` for doctor/migrations (deferred — the probed scan shape is the historic OR query, no longer shipped), the `what_closed` repo=None branch (dead code; delete/reconcile when query.py is next touched), reviews_fts (cut by the plan critic), the C4 conn-leak nit (rides a future AMEND only if one is already happening for other reasons).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: WHEN the strengthened C2 runs against a store whose items table carries the title index, THE SYSTEM SHALL pass while asserting the EXPLAIN plan of the revert-title statement captured at runtime from a real ingest (connection trace), not a copied literal.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_ingest_scale.py -q -k test_title_lookup_plan_uses_title_index`
  - expect: OK at both ends (the check is a strengthening, not a defect fix); discrimination is demonstrated by the recorded mutant probe — a `LOWER(title)` rewrite of the shipped lookup turns the strengthened check RED while the copied-literal form stays GREEN (probe of record in the PR #35 review, test-infrastructure lane)
  - files: tests/test_ingest_scale.py
  - why: GREEN at base and head today under the copied-literal form; the amendment buys discrimination against runtime query drift, which the current form cannot see
- [ ] AC2: WHEN sync_repo runs, THE SYSTEM SHALL issue `PRAGMA optimize` on the write connection after the finish transaction's COMMIT statement, asserted positionally in the traced statement order.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_ingest_scale.py -q -k test_sync_runs_pragma_optimize`
  - expect: OK at both ends; discrimination demonstrated by the recorded mutant probe — a variant issuing the statement at the start of sync_repo turns the strengthened check RED while the presence-only form stays GREEN
  - files: tests/test_ingest_scale.py
  - why: GREEN at base and head today under the presence-only form; the amendment pins the placement the shipped design depends on (best-effort maintenance after the durable commit)
- [ ] AC3: WHEN C4's cost check runs with `CORPUS_SMALL = 1000` and `CORPUS_LARGE = 2000`, THE SYSTEM SHALL keep both ratios within their 1.25x threshold at head and RED under the pin-reverted mutant.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_ingest_scale.py -q -k test_per_item_cost_is_flat`
  - expect: OK at both ends at both corpus sizes; discrimination evidence of record — pin-reverted mutant ratios 1.961 (item-txn) and 1.8377 (whole-run) at 1k/2k vs head 1.0000/1.0006
  - files: tests/test_ingest_scale.py
  - why: GREEN at base and head at the current 2k/4k sizes; the shrink is a pure cost reduction with probed-equal discrimination (~97s suite wall saved across the CI matrix)
- [ ] AC4: THE SYSTEM SHALL state the count-freshness boundary in AGENTS.md's invariants, naming that `sync_state` counts are finish-time snapshots exact after every completed run and may lag after an interrupted run, cross-referencing docs/schema.md.
  - class: NON-EXECUTABLE(DOCS_ONLY)
  - substitute evidence (review artifact): the AGENTS.md diff adding the invariant bullet, cross-referenced against docs/schema.md's "recomputed when a sync run finishes" paragraph (grep-verified at the anchor commit)
  - substitute evidence (verification): the merged PR's diff view showing the new AGENTS.md bullet
  - files: AGENTS.md
  - why: docs-only; the executable surface (schema_notes.py notes, docs/schema.md) already landed in 0edd793

## Design

1. C2 amendment: mirror C1's round-3 pattern — capture the runtime revert-title SELECT via `conn.set_trace_callback` during a real `sync_repo` ingest, EXPLAIN the captured statement on a stats-cleared fresh connection (C1's established oracle), assert an index seek binding `title=?`.
2. C6 amendment: assert the traced statement order — the finish transaction's COMMIT appears, and the first `pragma optimize` occurrence appears after it.
3. C4 corpus constants: `CORPUS_SMALL = 1000`, `CORPUS_LARGE = 2000` (one-line change; the probed separation holds).
4. All three land as ONE checkpoint AMEND batch (reason `CHECK_WRONG` per pair, fresh base+head replays of all six discriminating checks, re-anchored receipt published to this issue, amendment approved by the implementation reviewer) — never three separate refreezes.
5. AGENTS.md: one bullet under "Correctness of ingest" (or "Integrity of the data") stating the boundary, cross-referencing docs/schema.md; wording mirrors schema_notes.py.

## Files to change

`tests/test_ingest_scale.py` (C2, C6, corpus constants — checkpoint-anchored, AMEND required), `AGENTS.md` (one bullet), the trace's `repro/checkpoint.manifest` + re-anchored receipt (git-excluded).

```

python -m unittest discover -s tests -b
bash .agents/issue-traces/22-cold-sync-scale-indexed-reads/repro/replay-all.sh   # TMPDIR=/e/ZCode/tmp on this host
```

## Dependencies

Depends on: none (post-merge work on main; base = 93201e5025c3bf51255ed7ab725c5ceb703d3cb2).
Gated on: maintainer go-ahead recorded (in-session approval, see preamble).
Blocks: nothing.

## Constraints and invariants

- The checkpoint AMEND path is mandatory: editing the frozen file without AMEND rows + fresh replays + a re-anchored, republished receipt is an anti-tampering violation.
- Plans asserted must stay stats-independent (C1's fresh-connection oracle pattern) — real stores are stats-bearing after their first sync, and the stats-regime remains uncovered by design (PR #35's Considered-not-filed row).
- Windows is first-class: the suite and the amended checks must stay green on the Windows CI legs.
- No schema, no `user_version` change, no new runtime dependencies.

## Definition of done

All four ACs pass on the Windows and Linux CI legs; the amended checks' discrimination evidence (mutant probes) is quoted in the PR body; the trace's replay is 10/10 PASS at the final head with all identities rebound; the PR body says `Closes #<this issue>` and carries the fresh anchor receipt.

item.body:
Closes #23

## Summary

The sync path could be taken down by one hostile payload, and the store could not tell
complete answers from partial ones. This PR adds the two foundations and two plumbing channels
the issue specified (Workstream A-02 of epic #21):

- **Schema drift cannot abort a sync.** The GraphQL page query now travels on stdin
  (`gh api graphql --input -`, JSON body) — no argv element carries query text, so Windows'
  CreateProcessW limit can never truncate a query again and the `_MAX_QUERY_CHARS` clamp stops
  being argv-motivated (chunks return to the 40-alias page cap). A cached capability probe
  (one introspection per host+gh-version, persisted in `meta`) omits **each** field the host's
  schema lacks — per field, not per block — and records every omission in `fetch_log`. Probe
  failure fails open (full field set, one fetch_log row).
- **A per-field runtime error drops only that section.** Errors whose `path` scopes them to one
  item alias's section (`["repository", "i2", "comments"]`) are removed from the hard-error set;
  the errored key is deleted from that item's node so the established absent-section REST
  fallback answers it, and the drop is logged. Validation errors (data null) stay fatal.
- **Masked-null sections fall back.** `_children_from_node`'s five section gates now test
  nullness, not key presence — a permission-masked field returns null WITH the key, which used
  to present as complete-and-empty and skip the REST fallback.
- **Ingest learns section completeness.** `ingest_item` receives a per-section
  `children_complete` map (False for REST-fallback sections, cap-truncated sections, and the
  whole 404 path); sync records one fetch_log note per item with its incomplete sections. The
  map is not persisted (#25's scope).
- **`sync --numbers N,M` refreshes exact items** through the bulk children path. The watermark
  never moves (`advance_watermark=False` through ingest and the gone path), no full sync starts
  or completes (a never-full store stays marked pending, so a numbers-only corpus reads
  incomplete), the deletion oracle never runs, freshness stamps are untouched, and the targeted
  finalizer clears `last_error` + rate columns only. Item shells come from
  `get_issues(numbers)` — the same REST endpoint family as the listing, so issue-list `id` /
  `updated_at` / `pull_request` identity is preserved verbatim; a source without it falls back
  to an unfiltered listing filtered per page (explicitly requested items older than the
  watermark are still found).
- **The `--jsonl` sidecar becomes a replayable per-item record.** One `item_bundle` per ingested
  item carries `number`, `item`, `pull` (number-stamped when the payload lacked it), every child
  section, the timeline, and a `gone`/`gone_status` pair for recorded deletions — deduplicable
  by `(number, item.updated_at)`. `JsonlReplaySource` (`tests/replay.py`) replays a recorded
  sidecar row-for-row through the real ingest path, routing gone bundles through the same
  first-sighting 404/410 ingest-and-mark handler as a live error so `state`, `state_reason`, and
  `raw_json` reproduce byte-identically; duplicate lines (append-mode resume) dedup last-wins.

One issue = one PR: #24/#25/#26/#27 (the rest of Workstream A) and #36 are deliberately not
bundled. Bundling was checked against the graph before starting: #23's connected items are its
closed dependency #22 (delivered by PR #35, in this base), the epic, and siblings the issue's
Out-list excludes.

## Root cause

One shared architectural cause (`04-root-cause.md` in the trace): the GraphQL integration grew
per-feature (NOT_FOUND tolerance, argv chunk clamping, `*_incomplete` flags, a per-payload
sidecar) without a capability model of the schema or a transport independent of process argv,
and the ingest boundary took only section lists — so "these comments are complete" was
information the store never had, and one oversized or hostile payload aborted everything.

## Recurrence prevention (defect class)

- Defect class: one hostile or unexpected payload (GraphQL error, absent schema field, oversized
  argv, unattributed record, masked-null section) takes down or silently corrupts the whole sync
  because a single failure/transport/attribution mechanism serves every section.
- Sweep: 18 raise sites dispositioned (FIXED 1, SAFE-FAIL-CLOSED 12, DISPOSITIONED 2, SAFE
  recorder 1 — table in the trace's `08a-recurrence-sweep.md`); argv-built GraphQL payloads: 0
  remain; sidecar writers without an owning key: 0 remain (release records are corpus-level by
  nature); presence-only node guards: 0 remain; unconditional watermark writes: 0 remain (both
  sites gated).
- Guardrail: the per-field omission + section-error classifier + null-aware guards, pinned by
  frozen C1/C2 and supplementary tests, demonstrated biting: mutation M1/M2 (guard reverted)
  kill the checks, and a masked-null node falls back instead of storing complete-empty
  (`NullSectionGuardTests`).

## Tests

- Frozen acceptance checks (authored arm's-length, frozen pre-implementation, replayed at a
  pinned base): `bash .agents/issue-traces/23-sync-schema-drift-plumbing/repro/replay-all.sh`
  → **10/10 PASS** (C2/C3/C5/C6 base RED → head GREEN; C1/C4/C7 base ERROR → head GREEN;
  C8-C10 GREEN/GREEN).
- Full suite: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → **Ran 348 tests … OK** (319 at base
  + 7 frozen + 22 supplementary).

## Summary

The sync path could be taken down by one hostile payload, and the store could not tell
complete answers from partial ones. This PR adds the two foundations and two plumbing channels
the issue specified (Workstream A-02 of epic #21):

- **Schema drift cannot abort a sync.** The GraphQL page query now travels on stdin
  (`gh api graphql --input -`, JSON body) — no argv element carries query text, so Windows'
  CreateProcessW limit can never truncate a query again and the `_MAX_QUERY_CHARS` clamp stops
  being argv-motivated (chunks return to the 40-alias page cap). A cached capability probe
  (one introspection per host+gh-version, persisted in `meta`) omits **each** field the host's
  schema lacks — per field, not per block — and records every omission in `fetch_log`. Probe
  failure fails open (full field set, one fetch_log row).
- **A per-field runtime error drops only that section.** Errors whose `path` scopes them to one
  item alias's section (`["repository", "i2", "comments"]`) are removed from the hard-error set;
  the errored key is deleted from that item's node so the established absent-section REST
  fallback answers it, and the drop is logged. Validation errors (data null) stay fatal.
- **Masked-null sections fall back.** `_children_from_node`'s five section gates now test
  nullness, not key presence — a permission-masked field returns null WITH the key, which used
  to present as complete-and-empty and skip the REST fallback.
- **Ingest learns section completeness.** `ingest_item` receives a per-section
  `children_complete` map (False for REST-fallback sections, cap-truncated sections, and the
  whole 404 path); sync records one fetch_log note per item with its incomplete sections. The
  map is not persisted (#25's scope).
- **`sync --numbers N,M` refreshes exact items** through the bulk children path. The watermark
  never moves (`advance_watermark=False` through ingest and the gone path), no full sync starts
  or completes (a never-full store stays marked pending, so a numbers-only corpus reads
  incomplete), the deletion oracle never runs, freshness stamps are untouched, and the targeted
  finalizer clears `last_error` + rate columns only. Item shells come from
  `get_issues(numbers)` — the same REST endpoint family as the listing, so issue-list `id` /
  `updated_at` / `pull_request` identity is preserved verbatim; a source without it falls back
  to an unfiltered listing filtered per page (explicitly requested items older than the
  watermark are still found).
- **The `--jsonl` sidecar becomes a replayable per-item record.** One `item_bundle` per ingested
  item carries `number`, `item`, `pull` (number-stamped when the payload lacked it), every child
  section, the timeline, and a `gone`/`gone_status` pair for recorded deletions — deduplicable
  by `(number, item.updated_at)`. `JsonlReplaySource` (`tests/replay.py`) replays a recorded
  sidecar row-for-row through the real ingest path, routing gone bundles through the same
  first-sighting 404/410 ingest-and-mark handler as a live error so `state`, `state_reason`, and
  `raw_json` reproduce byte-identically; duplicate lines (append-mode resume) dedup last-wins.

One issue = one PR: #24/#25/#26/#27 (the rest of Workstream A) and #36 are deliberately not
bundled. Bundling was checked against the graph before starting: #23's connected items are its
closed dependency #22 (delivered by PR #35, in this base), the epic, and siblings the issue's
Out-list excludes.

## Root cause

One shared architectural cause (`04-root-cause.md` in the trace): the GraphQL integration grew
per-feature (NOT_FOUND tolerance, argv chunk clamping, `*_incomplete` flags, a per-payload
sidecar) without a capability model of the schema or a transport independent of process argv,
and the ingest boundary took only section lists — so "these comments are complete" was
information the store never had, and one oversized or hostile payload aborted everything.

## Recurrence prevention (defect class)

- Defect class: one hostile or unexpected payload (GraphQL error, absent schema field, oversized
  argv, unattributed record, masked-null section) takes down or silently corrupts the whole sync
  because a single failure/transport/attribution mechanism serves every section.
- Sweep: 18 raise sites dispositioned (FIXED 1, SAFE-FAIL-CLOSED 12, DISPOSITIONED 2, SAFE
  recorder 1 — table in the trace's `08a-recurrence-sweep.md`); argv-built GraphQL payloads: 0
  remain; sidecar writers without an owning key: 0 remain (release records are corpus-level by
  nature); presence-only node guards: 0 remain; unconditional watermark writes: 0 remain (both
  sites gated).
- Guardrail: the per-field omission + section-error classifier + null-aware guards, pinned by
  frozen C1/C2 and supplementary tests, demonstrated biting: mutation M1/M2 (guard reverted)
  kill the checks, and a masked-null node falls back instead of storing complete-empty

item.body:
Closes #24

## Summary

Migration v7 makes the demand/ownership/dependency signals GitHub already ships in listing payloads queryable from stored columns (reactions, milestone, issue type, sub-issue progress, open and total blocked-by/blocking counts, author association, comment count, assignees, custom field values, merged_by), closes two search gaps (review bodies via `reviews_fts`; PR touched paths via an `items_fts.paths_text` column weighted below title/body), and gives `status` a `coverage` block that distinguishes "absent upstream" from "not fetched". A Python-`json` backfill populates the new columns from stored `raw_json` on migration; cross-source re-ingests preserve sibling-source values via source-owned ABSENT-merge; pre-v7 stores degrade cleanly on every read path.

## Root Cause

Six verified gaps (issue body claims re-executed at HEAD before implementation): the demand/ownership/dependency signals GitHub already ships in the listing payload (reactions, milestone, type, sub-issue progress, blocked-by/blocking open+total counts, author association, assignees, custom field values) lived only inside `items.raw_json` (`schema.sql:15-44` had no columns; `store.py` extracted nothing); review bodies were stored (`store.insert_reviews`) but indexed by no FTS table, and `query._SEARCH_MERGED` (`query.py:112-135`) unioned only `items_fts` + `comments_fts`, so review-only text was unsearchable; `pr_files.path` was stored and B-tree-indexed but outside FTS, so a PR was unfindable by a touched path; `upsert_item_row`'s two `ON CONFLICT` clauses assigned every column `= excluded.<col>` wholesale, so a re-ingest from one source nulled a sibling source's values (reproduced: a listing-only re-ingest wiped `merge_commit`); the GraphQL mapper emitted `merged_at`/`merge_commit_sha`/`merged_by` unconditionally — a capability-masked selection was indistinguishable from an explicit null; and `status` returned only `repos[]`/`counts[]`, unable to distinguish "absent upstream" from "not fetched".

## Fix

Migration v7 (`user_version` 6→7), one migration slot per the epic #21 lane:

- `items` gains 13 columns: 10 listing-owned payload signals + `merged_by` (pull-owned) + derived `comment_count`/`paths_text` (NOT NULL, recomputed from stored child rows each ingest); `comments` gains `author_association`; new item-scoped child tables `assignees` and `issue_field_values` (replaced with the other children on re-ingest; adopted by `doctor --consolidate`).
- Source-owned ABSENT-merge: listing-owned signals extract from `list_raw` only, the pull trio (`merged_by`, `merge_commit`, `merged_at`) from `pull_raw` only — `pull_raw=None` emits ABSENT so even a listing carrying pull-named keys preserves the stored trio; a key present with explicit JSON null clears; an absent key preserves. The migration backfills all of it from stored `raw_json` in Python `json` (no SQLite JSON1: the supported floor is 3.35) and fully rebuilds `items_fts` (4 columns) and `reviews_fts` (new) — creation alone never indexes rows a v6 store already holds.
- Search: `reviews_fts` merges review-only hits into the owning item like comment hits (`src=2` under the same `hit_key` GROUP BY); `items_fts.paths_text` makes a PR findable by a touched path at bm25 weight 0.5 (strictly below title 10 / body 1 / labels 3). Pre-v7 stores degrade to the legacy arms with `index_stale: true` (reads never migrate).
- `status` gains `coverage`: `truncation_notes` by `fetch_log.resource`, `dropped_fields` (capability `omitted <field>` notes), `null_v7_rows` (null on pre-v7 stores), `store_bytes`.
- GraphQL: `authorAssociation` joins both comment node selections, probe-gated per comment type (IssueComment / PullRequestReviewComment introspection added to the #23 probe); a strip records `authorAssociation` in `omitted_fields` so `coverage.dropped_fields` sees it; the mapper emits all four absence-critical keys (`authorAssociation`, `mergedBy`, `mergedAt`, `mergeCommit`) only when the node carries them — a masked selection can no longer masquerade as an explicit-null clearing. Comment `author_association` survives probe-degraded re-ingest via per-kind pre-replacement snapshots.
- Schema-version literals in four test files derive from `CURRENT_USER_VERSION`/`SCHEMA_VERSION` (eradicates the version-literal class).

## Recurrence Prevention (defect class)

## Summary

Migration v7 makes the demand/ownership/dependency signals GitHub already ships in listing payloads queryable from stored columns (reactions, milestone, issue type, sub-issue progress, open and total blocked-by/blocking counts, author association, comment count, assignees, custom field values, merged_by), closes two search gaps (review bodies via `reviews_fts`; PR touched paths via an `items_fts.paths_text` column weighted below title/body), and gives `status` a `coverage` block that distinguishes "absent upstream" from "not fetched". A Python-`json` backfill populates the new columns from stored `raw_json` on migration; cross-source re-ingests preserve sibling-source values via source-owned ABSENT-merge; pre-v7 stores degrade cleanly on every read path.

## Root Cause

Six verified gaps (issue body claims re-executed at HEAD before implementation): the demand/ownership/dependency signals GitHub already ships in the listing payload (reactions, milestone, type, sub-issue progress, blocked-by/blocking open+total counts, author association, assignees, custom field values) lived only inside `items.raw_json` (`schema.sql:15-44` had no columns; `store.py` extracted nothing); review bodies were stored (`store.insert_reviews`) but indexed by no FTS table, and `query._SEARCH_MERGED` (`query.py:112-135`) unioned only `items_fts` + `comments_fts`, so review-only text was unsearchable; `pr_files.path` was stored and B-tree-indexed but outside FTS, so a PR was unfindable by a touched path; `upsert_item_row`'s two `ON CONFLICT` clauses assigned every column `= excluded.<col>` wholesale, so a re-ingest from one source nulled a sibling source's values (reproduced: a listing-only re-ingest wiped `merge_commit`); the GraphQL mapper emitted `merged_at`/`merge_commit_sha`/`merged_by` unconditionally — a capability-masked selection was indistinguishable from an explicit null; and `status` returned only `repos[]`/`counts[]`, unable to distinguish "absent upstream" from "not fetched".

## Fix

Migration v7 (`user_version` 6→7), one migration slot per the epic #21 lane:

- `items` gains 13 columns: 10 listing-owned payload signals + `merged_by` (pull-owned) + derived `comment_count`/`paths_text` (NOT NULL, recomputed from stored child rows each ingest); `comments` gains `author_association`; new item-scoped child tables `assignees` and `issue_field_values` (replaced with the other children on re-ingest; adopted by `doctor --consolidate`).
- Source-owned ABSENT-merge: listing-owned signals extract from `list_raw` only, the pull trio (`merged_by`, `merge_commit`, `merged_at`) from `pull_raw` only — `pull_raw=None` emits ABSENT so even a listing carrying pull-named keys preserves the stored trio; a key present with explicit JSON null clears; an absent key preserves. The migration backfills all of it from stored `raw_json` in Python `json` (no SQLite JSON1: the supported floor is 3.35) and fully rebuilds `items_fts` (4 columns) and `reviews_fts` (new) — creation alone never indexes rows a v6 store already holds.
- Search: `reviews_fts` merges review-only hits into the owning item like comment hits (`src=2` under the same `hit_key` GROUP BY); `items_fts.paths_text` makes a PR findable by a touched path at bm25 weight 0.5 (strictly below title 10 / body 1 / labels 3). Pre-v7 stores degrade to the legacy arms with `index_stale: true` (reads never migrate).
- `status` gains `coverage`: `truncation_notes` by `fetch_log.resource`, `dropped_fields` (capability `omitted <field>` notes), `null_v7_rows` (null on pre-v7 stores), `store_bytes`.
- GraphQL: `authorAssociation` joins both comment node selections, probe-gated per comment type (IssueComment / PullRequestReviewComment introspection added to the #23 probe); a strip records `authorAssociation` in `omitted_fields` so `coverage.dropped_fields` sees it; the mapper emits all four absence-critical keys (`authorAssociation`, `mergedBy`, `mergedAt`, `mergeCommit`) only when the node carries them — a masked selection can no longer masquerade as an explicit-null clearing. Comment `author_association` survives probe-degraded re-ingest via per-kind pre-replacement snapshots.
- Schema-version literals in four test files derive from `CURRENT_USER_VERSION`/`SCHEMA_VERSION` (eradicates the version-literal class).

## Summary

Migration v8 gives the store evidence history: the prior version of every item title/body, comment and review body is kept whenever re-ingest replaces it, comments/reviews that vanish from a fetch whose section was complete are tombstoned, and `item N --history` / `item N --as-of T` answer what the text said at GitHub time T. Plain `item` output is byte-identical to the pre-v8 shape. This is Workstream A slot A-04 of 6 (epic #21); it consumes the `children_complete` map #23 shipped for exactly this purpose.

## Root Cause

The store was a current-state projection: `upsert_item_row` overwrites `title`/`body` in both ON CONFLICT arms (`store.py:260-297` at base) and `replace_item_children` deletes every comment/review row before reinserting the payload set (`store.py:68-77` at base), so displaced text was unrecoverable and upstream deletions left no trace; no query surface exposed prior text (`item` had no history flags). The store's own contract is faithfulness-as-evidence (AGENTS.md), which current-state-only text contradicts for edited/deleted content — the gap #25 designates for remediation.

## Fix

- **Schema v8** (`schema.sql`, `db.py`): additive `revisions` table (sequence id, owning item, entity, identity, origin `edit`/`deleted`, the exact displaced `content`, GitHub-time `valid_from`/`valid_to`) + `idx_revisions_item`; `SCHEMA_VERSION`/`CURRENT_USER_VERSION`/`MIGRATIONS` move to 8; idempotent `migrate_v7_to_v8`; no backfill (prior text was never stored).
- **Write rules** (`store.py`): `snapshot_revision_state` reads the stored item row (same dual identity as the upsert) and canonical child maps before replacement; `write_revisions` appends pre-images inside `ingest_item`'s one transaction only when content differs (NULL-aware; title compared with the same `or ""` coercion the column stores). Tombstones fire only when the section's `children_complete` flag `is True`, keyed by the production sections (`issue_comments`/`review_comments`/`reviews`). Rows are never updated or deleted by the ingest path.
- **Read surface** (`query.py`, `cli.py`): `item --history` (standard item envelope + `revisions`) and `item --as-of T` (strict `[valid_from, valid_to)` containment, highest-id-wins on overlap, live validity from the full revision sequence, `as_of_basis` disclosing every window rule, `absent_entities` for no-version-at-T) with coded errors for bad/combined flags. `--as-of` omits `edges`/`index_stale` (edges carry no recorded history; rationale in the docstring and README). The no-flag path adds no keys.
- **Compatibility** (`sync.py`, `tests/replay.py`, `doctor.py`): the item_bundle sidecar records the exact `children_complete` map; `_resolve_children` applies a present recorded map verbatim and leaves absent-key live responses unchanged; `JsonlReplaySource` fails pre-v8 bundles closed (injected all-False) so replay never fabricates deletion evidence, yields one version per number per page with page-scoped bundle identity, collapses only adjacent exact duplicates, and `get_issues` registers the targeted cursor. Consolidation adopts `revisions` with fresh ids in sequence order. v7 feature gates pin slot 7 (`_V7_USER_VERSION`), v8 gates pin `_V8_USER_VERSION` — never `CURRENT_USER_VERSION` — so stores behind the build keep their own features.
- **Coverage** (`query.py`): `status.coverage.revision_rows`/`revision_bytes` (UTF-8 bytes via `LENGTH(CAST(content AS BLOB))`; NULL pre-v8, honest 0 on an empty v8 store, repo-scoped).

## Recurrence Prevention (defect class)

- Defect class: a current-state projection silently discards displaced text at an ingest/copy boundary.
- Sweep result: 114 raw predicate hits across 5 executed greps (all `DELETE FROM` in store.py/doctor.py; 54 `excluded.` overwrite arms; version-gate sites; sidecar writer/reader/resolver consumption; text-bearing replaced surfaces), dispositioned one-to-one in `08a-recurrence-sweep.md` (trace) — 21 disposition units: 6 FIXED in this PR, 15 OUT with rationale.
- Guardrail: `AppendOnlyGuardTests.test_no_update_or_delete_targets_revisions` (grep-level: no UPDATE/DELETE may target `revisions` outside doctor's sanctioned copy) — demonstrated GREEN on the fix, RED on an injected `UPDATE revisions` mutant, GREEN again after revert.

## Tests

- Regression checks (frozen at the red checkpoint, certified post-commit): 8/8 PASS — C1-C6 base legs `exit=5 ERROR` matching `NO TESTS RAN` at base 548c07a, head legs GREEN at 92113644; C7/C8 GREEN/GREEN. New tests: `tests/test_revisions.py` (28 tests: write rules, NULL/empty transitions, tombstone gates incl. 1/"true" impostors, as-of windows/boundaries/overlap/gap/mixed-offset, CLI errors, replay fidelity incl. per-version children and gone-metadata dedup, three-way resolver contract, targeted refresh, append-only guard) + 3 migration tests (`tests/test_migrations.py`).
- Impacted suite: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` -> **424 tests OK** (385 at base; +28 revisions, +3 migrations, +8 feedback-round pins).
- Deferred-work scan: clean (no deferred-work markers on added lines).
- **Revision growth under resync:** from an empty store, a 5-observation recorded fixture (3 items, one body edit, one comment deletion) writes 2 revisions; an **incremental** resync of the same fixture re-ingests only the newest observation and grows `revisions` by exactly **0** (the equality guard makes steady-state growth track real edit volume, not sync volume). A **`--force`** replay re-derives the whole recorded trajectory — every historical observation re-displaces the stored text, so growth equals the trajectory length by design (final state is idempotent; replay from an empty store reproduces the same rows deterministically, pinned by test).

## Regression Protection

- 6 NEW-SURFACE frozen checks (one per AC1-AC6) + 2 PRESERVING checks (AC7/AC8 run unmodified against `tests/test_store.py`).
- Adversarial cases pinned: truthy gate impostors (`1`, `"true"`), duplicate payload rows, mixed comment kinds sharing a GitHub id, byte-identical nonconsecutive A→B→A, distinct same-timestamp observations, gone bundles differing only in deletion metadata, legacy sidecars fail closed, naive/malformed `--as-of`.
- AC6 golden fixture committed (`tests/revisions_item_golden.expected.json`), captured at base and provenance-verified by the final critic (regenerated from base code in a disposable worktree, byte-equal modulo the temp db path); never regenerated at head.
- Drift review: no pre-existing test weakened or deleted; `tests/fixtures.py` untouched; `tests/replay.py`'s contract change is the in-scope replay-fidelity work with its own round-trip tests.

## External Checkpoint Anchor

- Receipt published before implementation (human-confirmed; local validation cannot attest publication/timing): `issue-tracer-checkpoint-v1 slug=25-item-revisions-as-of manifest=b867c7b72b2c63a6f113071383038b00b6f48e38 semantics=32d40d4bae1c904a1ac999cac84f95a9b6f601bd tree=78a288a2ab5a46ab7dfa1534a55f56cc25007ead`
- External artifact location: https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/issues/25#issuecomment-6431189291
- Independent verification: `repro-check.sh verify-anchor --slug 25-item-revisions-as-of --receipt '<published literal>'` -> PASS (re-run by the implementation reviewer and the final critic, both at the final head)
- Local copy/provenance: `.agents/issue-traces/25-item-revisions-as-of/repro/anchor-v1.txt` (discovery copy, non-authoritative)

## Acceptance Criteria -> Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 body edit stores one revision with GitHub-time windows | C1 `test_body_edit_writes_pre_image` (frozen check, ERROR→GREEN) |
| AC2 A→B→A records two revisions, no sync wedge | C2 `test_revert_a_b_a_does_not_wedge` (ERROR→GREEN; the critic-reproduced wedge regression, authored first) |
| AC3 unchanged re-ingest writes no revision | C3 `test_unchanged_reingest_is_noop` (ERROR→GREEN) + force-resync growth = 0 (above) |
| AC4 tombstone iff the section's `children_complete` flag is True | C4 `test_tombstones_only_on_complete_sections` (ERROR→GREEN; production keys, impostor flags pinned) |
| AC5 `item N --as-of T` returns the version whose window contains T + `as_of_basis` | C5 `test_item_as_of` (ERROR→GREEN; boundaries, overlap, gap, first-sighted, mixed-offset) |
| AC6 plain `item N` byte-identical to the pre-PR shape | C6 `test_plain_item_unchanged` (ERROR→GREEN; base golden fixture) |
| AC7 re-ingest keeps inbound mentions (PRESERVING) | C7 `test_inbound_mention_survives_destination_upsert` (GREEN/GREEN, unmodified) |
| AC8 double upsert does not raise (PRESERVING) | C8 `test_upsert_idempotent` (GREEN/GREEN, unmodified) |

## Invariant Audit

Per AGENTS.md (zaxbygraph agent contracts):

- Every edge is `confidence='EXTRACTED'` — not touched: no new edge stream; `revisions` is a table, not edges (grep: no edges writes in the diff).
- Node types are actor/item/label/file/commit — not touched: revisions reference items by (repo, number); no new node type.
- Evidence is a payload, never part of an edge's identity — not touched: edge tables and `insert_edge` untouched by the diff.
- Actor commented/reviewed collapse; comment roll-up — not touched: `delete_owned_edges`/`rebuild_edges` semantics unchanged (AC7 GREEN).
- Cross-repo keyword/timeline rules — not touched: extraction unchanged.
- `closes` vs `closes_keyword` provenance — not touched.
- `items.id`/watermark from the issues-list payload — not touched: `upsert_item_row` untouched; watermark behavior pinned by the targeted-refresh test (revisions captured, watermark unchanged).
- One BEGIN IMMEDIATE per item incl. watermark — honored: revision writes join `ingest_item`'s caller-owned transaction; a sabotaged revision write aborts item + watermark together (pinned by `test_revision_failure_aborts_item_and_watermark`).
- Ingest is idempotent — strengthened: unchanged re-ingest writes nothing (AC3, C8 still GREEN).
- Storage faults reported, not swallowed — honored: the transaction test shows a failing revision write propagates.
- Item-scoped children replaced; owned edges deleted with the timeline/closing_ref exemption — not touched: replacement semantics unchanged (documented boundary pinned).
- Read-only `sql` escape hatch — not touched: `revisions` is a plain table; the final critic's live spot-check 3 queried it through the guarded surface.
- SQLite floor (3.35) — not touched: no JSON1, no new pragma; version constants moved in the same commit as the migration that requires them.
- Windows first-class — honored: the suite runs on the CI matrix (3.11/3.12); no platform-conditional code added; the frozen legs pin CPython 3.14 only for the absence signature (test-runner behavior, not product code).


## Post-publication review

A swarm-pr-review run (10 lanes, 11/11 risk families attested) verified 12 findings — 2 critic-survived HIGH (a plan-promised consolidation test that was missing, and the inaccurate force-resync figure above) — plus 7 MEDIUM and 3 LOW; all 12 are fixed in this PR's head (8 new test pins; window guard; as-of read fixes; coded errors for empty/overflow `--as-of`; docs truthfulness sweep). 9 candidates were rejected with executed disproofs; the full disposition ledger is in the run artifacts. One finding was escalated to the independent critic for a product-decision input and is now **filed as Priority: #40** — consolidation adopting a history-less candidate (e.g. a pre-v8 legacy DB) deletes the store's unrecoverable revision evidence for that slug with nothing to replace it. The critic rejected accept-by-design (the candidate is auto-selected on watermark freshness, the CLI recommends the command as cleanup, no surface discloses revision coverage, and a pre-v8 candidate's empty table is a schema artifact rather than an observation) and recommends **per-item preservation** (replace an item's history only when the candidate has rows for it) with a doctor-payload disclosure line; a `--replace-revisions` opt-in is the fallback if pure replace polarity is preferred.

## Risk and Rollback

- Risk level: medium (schema migration), mitigated: additive-only migration, no data rewrite, no backfill, floor unchanged; replay/consolidation/legacy-gate compatibility wired and tested; plain read surface byte-identical (frozen golden).
- Rollback: revert the commit; v8 databases keep working on pre-revert builds only if the revert also reverts the version check — the practical rollback is reverting the merge before dependent slots (A-05/A-06) land; the `revisions` table can be dropped harmlessly.
- Residual risk: none known; the documented incomplete-then-complete evidence boundary above is the one known limitation, deliberate and pinned.

## Waivers (or none)

none

## Merge status

Awaiting explicit user approval; not merged.

*Provenance: post-publication swarm-pr-review and independent-critic round of PR #39.* Generated from that round (issue #25, schema v8 revisions), at the maintainer's direction to obtain independent-critic input on an ASK item. Every claim below was re-verified against origin/main at commit d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c on 2026-10-27 by source read and executed probes (baseline: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → `Ran 424 tests ... OK`). One issue = one PR. Review artifacts referenced below live in the git-excluded `.zcode/pr-review/pr39-20261027/` and are quoted inline where load-bearing._

## Summary

After this PR, `doctor --consolidate` can no longer destroy revision evidence the adopted candidate never observed: adoption replaces an item's stored revision history only when the candidate holds revision rows for that item, every consolidation reports what it did to the slug's history, and the docs stop implying that history is carried through when it is deleted. The empty case (a pre-v8 candidate) falls out as the special case: nothing is deleted.

## Problem (claims to verify)

1. **`consolidate()` deletes the slug's revision rows unconditionally, before the copy.** [`VERIFIED`: source read at d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c; executed probe: adopting a zero-revision candidate into a store holding 2 revision rows for the slug leaves 0.] The adoption transaction deletes every `_COPY_TABLES` row for the slug, `revisions` included, then inserts the candidate's rows:

   [doctor.py#L201-L202](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c/src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py#L201-L202)
   ```py
       for table, autoinc_pk in _COPY_TABLES:
           dst.execute(f"DELETE FROM {table} WHERE repo = ?", (repo_l,))
   ```
   (VERIFIED at d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c: source read.)

   `_COPY_TABLES` gained `("revisions", "id")` in PR #39 (doctor.py#L49-L61).

2. **A candidate's empty `revisions` table is a schema artifact, not an observation, so its emptiness licenses nothing.** [`VERIFIED`: source read.] `migrate_v7_to_v8` creates the table empty and can never backfill:

   [db.py#L871](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c/src/zaxbygraph/db.py#L871)
   ```py
    _FTS_PORTER_STATEMENTS). No backfill is possible: prior text was never
   ```
   (VERIFIED at d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c: source read.)

   For every other adopted table the worst case of replace-the-slug is re-sync cost (GitHub regenerates the data). `revisions` is the one asymmetric table: it exists precisely because GitHub no longer serves displaced text, so the delete is a one-way door.

3. **The adopter never chooses the candidate, and no surface discloses the hazard.** [`VERIFIED`: source read.] `doctor()` auto-selects the winner by greatest `issues_since` among complete candidates ([doctor.py#L14-L18](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c/src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py#L14-L18) — a criterion with no correlation to revision coverage); the CLI recommends the exact command as cleanup (`run: zaxbygraph doctor --consolidate ...`); `inspect()`'s report carries `items/garbled/complete/issues_since` but no revision counts ([doctor.py#L126-L132](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c/src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py#L126-L132)); and the user's intent ("clean up my scattered DBs") says nothing about destroying recorded history. (VERIFIED at d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c: source read of doctor.py and cli.py.)

4. **The docs imply preservation where deletion happens.** [`VERIFIED`: source read.]

   [schema_notes.py#L51](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c/src/zaxbygraph/schema_notes.py#L51)
   ```py
        "id": "v8. Sequence order for one item's displaced-text history; assigned at insert and never updated. doctor --consolidate is the one sanctioned rewrite (fresh ids, per-item order preserved)",
   ```
   (VERIFIED at d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c: source read.)

   Nothing in docs/schema.md's revisions section or schema_notes.py tells a reader that adopting a history-less candidate erases their history.

5. **The only pin test codifies the disputed semantics, and no test covers the empty case.** [`VERIFIED`: source read + reviewer-executed mutant (dropping `("revisions", "id")` from `_COPY_TABLES` passes the full 424-test suite).] [tests/test_revisions.py#L1081-L1082](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c/tests/test_revisions.py#L1081-L1082) asserts `STALE-OLD`/`STALE-NEW` rows for number 1 are deleted by a candidate that holds no history for number 1 — precisely the semantics this issue proposes to change. The assertion must be reworked in the same PR.

**Prior-art reconciliation.** Replace-the-slug adoption predates this issue (issue #1's doctor); PR #39 extended it to `revisions` and added the ordered copy. This issue does not revert that extension — it narrows it per item so the extension stops destroying evidence the candidate cannot re-derive. The related recorded boundary in docs/schema.md ("an absence first seen degraded leaves nothing for a later complete fetch to tombstone") covers evidence the store never held; this issue covers evidence the store does hold and consolidation deletes. (VERIFIED at d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c: source read.)

**Product-decision framing (carried from the ASK).** The maintainer decision this issue settles is the default polarity: preserve-by-default (this issue's ACs) vs pure replace-the-slug. If pure replace is preferred, the defensible shape is an explicit opt-in (e.g. a `--replace-revisions` flag or a fail-closed refusal naming that flag) — never silent replacement; that variant is Out of scope here and the ACs would be re-cut on request.

## Scope

**In:** `consolidate()`'s revisions handling — a per-item guard inside the existing transaction (replace an item's revision history only when the candidate holds revision rows for that item; preserve the store's rows otherwise; fresh ids and `ORDER BY id` sequence preserved for adopted rows); a disclosure line in the doctor result payload (report preserved-vs-adopted revision counts); doc updates in docs/schema.md (revisions write-rules), schema_notes.py (`revisions.id`), and the `consolidate()` docstring.
**Out:** within-item history union/merging when the candidate has *shallower* history for an item it does cover (residual loss recorded as a named boundary in the docs update; priced extension later); store-vs-candidate freshness gating for adoption generally (separate finding — `consolidate()` compares candidates only, never the store); any new CLI flag; reverting the `revisions` adoption itself.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: WHEN `doctor --consolidate` adopts a candidate holding zero revision rows for the slug into a store holding revision rows for it, THE SYSTEM SHALL leave all stored revision rows for the slug in place.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_revisions.py" -k test_empty_candidate_keeps_stored_history -b
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_revisions.py
  - why: at base the adoption deletes the slug's revision rows unconditionally (doctor.py#L201-L203), so the new test cannot exist and pass until the guard lands.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN the candidate holds revision rows for some of the slug's items and none for others, THE SYSTEM SHALL replace only the revision history of items the candidate has rows for and preserve the rest.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_revisions.py" -k test_partial_candidate_replaces_only_observed_items -b
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_revisions.py
  - why: the same unconditional delete (doctor.py#L201-L203) removes preserved rows at base; an all-or-nothing guard would also fail this check (the cliff the per-item scope exists to close).
- [ ] AC3: WHEN a candidate's revision rows are adopted, THE SYSTEM SHALL assign them fresh ids in the candidate's per-item sequence order and SHALL NOT touch other repos' revision rows.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_revisions.py" -k test_consolidation_adopts_revisions_fresh_ids_in_order -b
  - expect: OK (green at base and head, after reworking the current assertion set for per-item scope — the number-1 "STALE" rows survive at head).
  - files: tests/test_revisions.py
  - why: regression floor for the adoption mechanics this issue narrows (fresh ids, `ORDER BY id` sequence, cross-repo isolation).
- [ ] AC4: WHEN consolidation retains stored revision rows the candidate had no history for, THE SYSTEM SHALL report the preserved count (and the adopted count) in the doctor result payload.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_doctor.py" -k test_adoption_reports_preserved_revision_counts -b
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_doctor.py, src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py
  - why: the doctor report envelope (doctor.py report assembly) carries no revision fields at base, so the disclosure surface cannot exist until the fix adds it.
- [ ] AC5: THE SYSTEM SHALL document, in docs/schema.md's revisions write-rules, schema_notes.py's `revisions.id` note, and the `consolidate()` docstring, that adoption preserves per-item revision history the candidate never observed and that within-item depth loss (a shallower candidate for an item it covers) remains a recorded boundary.
  - class: NON-EXECUTABLE(DOCS_ONLY)
  - substitute evidence: the PR's doc diff, reviewed at review time, showing each of the three surfaces names both the per-item preservation and the within-item depth-loss boundary
  - files: docs/schema.md, src/zaxbygraph/schema_notes.py, src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py
  - why: prose; substitute evidence is the doc diff reviewed at PR time, showing each of the three surfaces names both the per-item preservation and the within-item depth-loss boundary.
- [ ] AC6: WHEN the same candidate is consolidated twice, THE SYSTEM SHALL write no new revision rows and delete none after the first adoption.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_revisions.py -k test_consolidation_twice_is_row_neutral -b
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check does not exist at base (it extends the consolidation test's fixture at head).
  - files: tests/test_revisions.py
  - why: floor against a broken guard or dedupe (delete+copy must stay idempotent once preservation lands).

## argv convention

Every executable AC uses `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p <file> -k <test> -b`. Its absence signature is `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5), which is CPython ≥ 3.13 behavior — base legs pin `py -3.14` (the box/repo convention established in #25's trace; 3.11/3.12 exit 0 on zero matches). AC3/AC6 are green at both ends and pin the preserved mechanics.

## Definition of done

All ACs pass on both CI legs. The PR body states the disclosure the doctor payload now carries and the residual within-item depth-loss boundary. `## Closure evidence` is in the PR body.

item.body:
PR head: 1095476168e7f91eb27c0dc22aa6725c79c0e39e

Closes #26
Closes #27

Bundled per the maintainer's authorization ("I authorize more than one issue per PR as long as the PR remains reviewable and manageable"): both issues are Workstream A schema-lane slots (A-05 → A-06), share their file set and registry/docs surfaces, and #27 declares `Depends on: #26`. #40 was evaluated and deliberately NOT bundled (different subsystem — doctor/consolidation — and a Priority-severity fix deserving its own PR).

## Summary

Migration v9 (issue #26) and v10 (issue #27) make the store record the references an item's text already carries and the links GitHub itself reports:

- **v9 text-derived references**: `item_path_refs` (raw path strings — Python frames, `path:L:C` tokens, same-repo `blob/` URLs, backticked segments — with `origin` and a backticked flag) and `item_signatures` (exception + masked error line + frame function) are extracted from bodies, comments and reviews, replaced on re-ingest, and **backfilled from stored `raw_json`** so an incremental corpus is covered without a resync. Paths stay RAW — resolution against the file vocabulary is read-time (#29's lane), so rows never depend on sync order.
- **`branch_ref`**: a PR whose `head_ref` carries exactly ONE numeric token naming one stored *issue* links to it. A single token can never become ambiguous later, so no retraction path exists; an insert-only reverse pass closes the either-ingests-first order.
- **Reference positions**: `mentions`/`closes_keyword` evidence now carries the location (`title`, or `body@<offset>`, `comment:<id>@<offset>`, `review:<id>@<offset>`) via a same-length foreign-reference mask so offsets index the original text. Edge identity (the 7-column key) is untouched.
- **v10 GitHub-reported links**: `blockedBy`, sub-issue `parent`, `duplicateOf` and `closedByPullRequestsReferences(includeClosedPrs:false)` become `source='link'` edges (`blocked_by`, `child_of`, `duplicate_of`, `linked_pr`), replaced **per connection** only when that connection was fetched complete, union-only on overflow, never retracted by a degraded re-ingest (the delete-owned exemption gains `'link'`).
- **Commit messages**: `pr_commits` rows (complete-gated) are the canonical source for commit-message `closes_keyword` edges — re-derived from the RETAINED rows on every ingest, so a REST or overflowed re-ingest never retracts them; evidence names the commit sha; the `closes` relation stays reserved for GitHub-reported closures.
- **`duplicate_keyword`**: "duplicate of #N" text yields the keyword stream, never GitHub's `duplicate_of`.
- **Reopen events**: `REOPENED_EVENT` rides the timeline selection into `item_events` rows, replaced only when the timeline section was fetched complete; a plain-REST sync (presence `None`) touches nothing.
- **Capability probe v3**: cache key bump (stale v2 maps cannot know the new fields) plus `IssueTimelineItemsItemType` enum introspection — a host lacking `REOPENED_EVENT` degrades by omission instead of failing every page query.
- Compatibility: `doctor --consolidate` copies all four new tables; the `item_bundle` sidecar and replay carry the new sections with presence semantics; docs/schema.md and schema notes cover every new relation and table.


### Considered, not filed

Post-publication swarm-pr-review (6 base lanes + 7 micro families; 25 verified findings — 23 FIXED in a9b1b98, 2 REJECTED by execution) plus the gate ladder. Dispositions for everything NOT fixed:

| Item | Reason | Gate test failed | Re-evaluate when |
|---|---|---|---|
| branch digit-run heuristic can still emit a semantically false `branch_ref` for version-like branch names (`release/2026-fix` → issue 2026 if stored) | letter-adjacent runs now rejected (python3-support, v2), but a delimiter-adjacent year/slug remains shape-valid; tightening further (e.g. requiring an issue-style prefix) is a product call on the AC4 wording | fails gate 2 partially (false fact stored, but the evidence string names the head_ref so a reader can judge) and gate 3 (low-frequency) | a mis-resolved branch_ref misleads a real query, or AC4's pattern wording is tightened |
| Reverse `branch_ref` pass visits every stored PR per issue ingest — O(PRs × issues) row visits per sync | one-time-per-item cost behind a partial index, scale test green, and the alternative (SQL LIKE prefilter) re-derives candidates worse | fails gate 3 (perf, not correctness) | the 8k-corpus scale budget regresses, or a corpus with >10k PRs syncs slowly |
| v9 backfill materializes all items/comments/reviews via fetchall | one-shot migration memory spike on very large stores; idempotent and atomic per MIGRATIONS step | fails gate 3 | a store large enough that the one-time spike is operationally real |
| New tables (`item_path_refs`, `item_signatures`, `item_events`, `pr_commits`) have no query/CLI read surface | read-time resolution and scoring are #29's lane by plan; ABSORB notice posted on #29 with the new-evidence comment | fails gate 4 (tracked in #29) | #29 ships |
| `_strip_foreign` (pre-existing, base-inherited) retains a quadratic worst case on slash-free word runs | pre-existing behavior this PR did not touch; the new hot paths use the linear `_mask_foreign` instead | fails gate 4 (pre-existing, outside the new code) | profiled evidence ties it to a real sync stall |
| `test_title_evidence_parity`'s dict-level assertion message reads "relations or destinations diverge" on an evidence divergence | cosmetic wording; the per-key TITLE-EVIDENCE-PARITY loop reports correctly when reached | fails gate 2/3 | next time that test module is edited |

## Root Cause

The store derived evidence from exactly two text channels (`mentions`/`closes_keyword`) and two timeline streams (`closed`/`cross_referenced`), while four mechanically-derivable reference families in the same payloads were extracted by nothing and the GitHub-reported link connections were not selected at all. A new stream carried as `source='payload'` would have been destroyed by the next degraded re-ingest (`delete_owned_edges` exempted only `timeline`/`closing_ref`).

## Fix

Two additive migrations in workstream slot order (v9 → v10), exactly as the reviewed plan (`docs/plans` program, issue bodies) specifies. See Summary. Necessity and sufficiency are pinned by the frozen acceptance checks: each of the 15 maps to one mechanism, all 15 run RED/absent → GREEN at the shipped head, and 12 named revert-mutants are proven killed.

## Recurrence Prevention (defect class)

- Defect class: derived evidence drifting across source ownership, transport capability, completeness, replay, migration, and consolidation.
- Sweep result: 14 predicate hits, all dispositioned FIX (relation registration ×6, child-table registration ×4, serialized-contract round trips ×4); 0 left open.
- Guardrail: the relation-registry census now DRIVES every emitter (a new relation cannot ship unregistered), plus a structural drift test asserting every `(repo, number)`-keyed table in sqlite_master appears in `doctor._COPY_TABLES`. Demonstrated bites: MUT10 (cross-owner deletion), MUT11 (census unregistration), MUT12 (consolidation drop) each turn their guard RED.

## Tests

- Frozen acceptance checks (authored at arm's length, amended pre-implementation under CHECK_WRONG with an anchor chain v1→v3): 15/15 PASS at the shipped head (12 NEW-SURFACE ERROR→GREEN, 1 DISCRIMINATING RED→GREEN, 3 PRESERVING GREEN→GREEN).
- Full suite: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → **472 tests OK** (424 at base + 48 new across the ladder and the post-publication review round).
- Mutation probes: `repro/mutation_probes.py` → **12/12 KILLED**, tree clean (probe scripts live in the git-excluded trace directory by design; reproducible from the checked-in tests they pin).
- Deferred-work scan → clean.
- CI: windows + ubuntu × 3.11/3.12 (this PR's runs).

## Regression Protection

- The three pinned actor-collapse contracts (`test_last_write_wins`, `test_two_comments_one_commented_edge`, `test_review_collapse_keeps_last_state`) stayed UNCHANGED and green — `collapse_edges` merges evidence on `closes_keyword` collisions only; MUT8 (widened merge) kills them.
- Fresh-vs-migrated parity tests pin the backfill to live-extraction behavior (keyword edges, evidence strings, branch targets) on item, comment and review channels.
- Test drift review: two `test_revisions.py` recorded-map tests updated for the widened `_resolve_children` tuple (index shifts only); the probe-cache key helper bumped to v3; the fresh-born version assertion now derives from `CURRENT_USER_VERSION`.

## External Checkpoint Anchor

- Receipt published before implementation (human-confirmed; local validation cannot attest publication/timing): `issue-tracer-checkpoint-v1 slug=26-27-text-refs-and-link-stream manifest=faae56b98d6bb6869184b30769568965551753d9 semantics=4679317e873efb7b846f12b495328ddd76bf61b2 tree=b320548f6f5860df71e5f99725de27f3b4ff5f92`
- External artifact location: https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/issues/26#issuecomment-6451405669 (chain v1: comment 6450445573; v2: 6451163828 — semantics digest constant across all three)
- Independent verification: `repro-check.sh verify-anchor --slug 26-27-text-refs-and-link-stream --receipt '<published literal>'` -> PASS (re-verified by the implementation reviewer and the final critic)
- Local copy/provenance: `.agents/issue-traces/26-27-text-refs-and-link-stream/02-reproduction.md` (non-authoritative discovery copy)

## Acceptance Criteria -> Evidence

| Acceptance criterion (from intake) | Evidence (command + output, or test name) |
|---|---|
| 26-AC1 path refs with origin + backticked flag | C1 GREEN (`repro/C1.head.log`); `test_path_refs_extracted` |
| 26-AC2 foreign blob URL dropped | C2 GREEN; MUT6 kill |
| 26-AC3 exception + masked error_line | C3 GREEN; MUT5 kill |
| 26-AC4 branch_ref single-match discipline | C4 GREEN; MUT4 (first-token) + MUT10 (cross-owner deletion) kills |
| 26-AC5 reference position in evidence | C5 RED→GREEN; exact-offset pin; MUT1/MUT2 kills; migration parity via `test_backfill_parity_with_live_extraction` + `test_title_evidence_parity` |
| 27-AC1 blocked_by replaced when complete | C6 GREEN (`test_blocked_by_replaced_when_complete`) |
| 27-AC2 degraded re-ingest never retracts; overflow union-only | C7 GREEN; MUT3 kill |
| 27-AC3 child_of/duplicate_of, repo-qualified | C8 GREEN |
| 27-AC4 open linked PRs recorded | C9 GREEN (rel pinned to `linked_pr`) |
| 27-AC5 commit-message closes_keyword, never closes | C10 GREEN; MUT9 kill |
| 27-AC6 duplicate_keyword stream | C11 GREEN |
| 27-AC7 reopen events in item_events | C12 GREEN; MUT7 kill; `ReplayTimelinePresenceTests` |
| 26-AC6 + 27-AC8 registry classifies every relation | C13 GREEN; census drives every emitter; MUT11 kill |
| 26-AC7 + 27-AC8 docs table lists every relation | C14 GREEN (`docs/schema.md` relationships rows) |
| 27-AC9 closes collapse untouched | C15 GREEN; MUT8 kill |

## Invariant Audit

Against AGENTS.md (each verified at HEAD):

- Every edge `confidence='EXTRACTED'`: untouched — all new edges insert with `'EXTRACTED'`.
- Node types unchanged (actor/item/label/file/commit): all new edges are item→item; `branch_ref`/`blocked_by`/`child_of`/`duplicate_of`/`linked_pr`/`duplicate_keyword` endpoints are item numbers or repo-qualified ids (C8).
- Evidence is a payload, never part of identity: the 7-column key untouched (C5 pins one source-unfiltered row per pair); `closes` merge exception untouched (C15).
- `closes` reserved for GitHub-reported links, `closes_keyword` keyword-derived: commit messages emit `closes_keyword` with commit provenance, never `closes` (C10); AGENTS.md's delete-owned bullet updated to name the `link` stream and its per-connection replace-when-complete semantics.
- `closes_keyword`/`mentions` mutual exclusion within a payload: preserved live AND in the v9 backfill (round-1/2 review fixes + parity tests).
- Cross-repo keyword references dropped, never localized: same-length mask shared by every position-aware stream (C2, MUT6).
- Item-scoped children replaced on re-ingest: `item_path_refs`/`item_signatures` replace unconditionally; `item_events`/`pr_commits` are the documented completeness-gated exception (AGENTS.md note added).
- Watermark/ingest idempotence/one-transaction-per-item: untouched — all new writes run inside `ingest_item`'s caller-owned transaction; PKs make duplicate pagination idempotent.
- Read-only `sql` escape hatch: untouched.

## Risk and Rollback

PR head: 1095476168e7f91eb27c0dc22aa6725c79c0e39e

Closes #26
Closes #27

Bundled per the maintainer's authorization ("I authorize more than one issue per PR as long as the PR remains reviewable and manageable"): both issues are Workstream A schema-lane slots (A-05 → A-06), share their file set and registry/docs surfaces, and #27 declares `Depends on: #26`. #40 was evaluated and deliberately NOT bundled (different subsystem — doctor/consolidation — and a Priority-severity fix deserving its own PR).

## Summary

Migration v9 (issue #26) and v10 (issue #27) make the store record the references an item's text already carries and the links GitHub itself reports:

- **v9 text-derived references**: `item_path_refs` (raw path strings — Python frames, `path:L:C` tokens, same-repo `blob/` URLs, backticked segments — with `origin` and a backticked flag) and `item_signatures` (exception + masked error line + frame function) are extracted from bodies, comments and reviews, replaced on re-ingest, and **backfilled from stored `raw_json`** so an incremental corpus is covered without a resync. Paths stay RAW — resolution against the file vocabulary is read-time (#29's lane), so rows never depend on sync order.
- **`branch_ref`**: a PR whose `head_ref` carries exactly ONE numeric token naming one stored *issue* links to it. A single token can never become ambiguous later, so no retraction path exists; an insert-only reverse pass closes the either-ingests-first order.
- **Reference positions**: `mentions`/`closes_keyword` evidence now carries the location (`title`, or `body@<offset>`, `comment:<id>@<offset>`, `review:<id>@<offset>`) via a same-length foreign-reference mask so offsets index the original text. Edge identity (the 7-column key) is untouched.
- **v10 GitHub-reported links**: `blockedBy`, sub-issue `parent`, `duplicateOf` and `closedByPullRequestsReferences(includeClosedPrs:false)` become `source='link'` edges (`blocked_by`, `child_of`, `duplicate_of`, `linked_pr`), replaced **per connection** only when that connection was fetched complete, union-only on overflow, never retracted by a degraded re-ingest (the delete-owned exemption gains `'link'`).
- **Commit messages**: `pr_commits` rows (complete-gated) are the canonical source for commit-message `closes_keyword` edges — re-derived from the RETAINED rows on every ingest, so a REST or overflowed re-ingest never retracts them; evidence names the commit sha; the `closes` relation stays reserved for GitHub-reported closures.
- **`duplicate_keyword`**: "duplicate of #N" text yields the keyword stream, never GitHub's `duplicate_of`.
- **Reopen events**: `REOPENED_EVENT` rides the timeline selection into `item_events` rows, replaced only when the timeline section was fetched complete; a plain-REST sync (presence `None`) touches nothing.
- **Capability probe v3**: cache key bump (stale v2 maps cannot know the new fields) plus `IssueTimelineItemsItemType` enum introspection — a host lacking `REOPENED_EVENT` degrades by omission instead of failing every page query.
- Compatibility: `doctor --consolidate` copies all four new tables; the `item_bundle` sidecar and replay carry the new sections with presence semantics; docs/schema.md and schema notes cover every new relation and table.


### Considered, not filed

Post-publication swarm-pr-review (6 base lanes + 7 micro families; 25 verified findings — 23 FIXED in a9b1b98, 2 REJECTED by execution) plus the gate ladder. Dispositions for everything NOT fixed:

| Item | Reason | Gate test failed | Re-evaluate when |
|---|---|---|---|
| branch digit-run heuristic can still emit a semantically false `branch_ref` for version-like branch names (`release/2026-fix` → issue 2026 if stored) | letter-adjacent runs now rejected (python3-support, v2), but a delimiter-adjacent year/slug remains shape-valid; tightening further (e.g. requiring an issue-style prefix) is a product call on the AC4 wording | fails gate 2 partially (false fact stored, but the evidence string names the head_ref so a reader can judge) and gate 3 (low-frequency) | a mis-resolved branch_ref misleads a real query, or AC4's pattern wording is tightened |
| Reverse `branch_ref` pass visits every stored PR per issue ingest — O(PRs × issues) row visits per sync | one-time-per-item cost behind a partial index, scale test green, and the alternative (SQL LIKE prefilter) re-derives candidates worse | fails gate 3 (perf, not correctness) | the 8k-corpus scale budget regresses, or a corpus with >10k PRs syncs slowly |
| v9 backfill materializes all items/comments/reviews via fetchall | one-shot migration memory spike on very large stores; idempotent and atomic per MIGRATIONS step | fails gate 3 | a store large enough that the one-time spike is operationally real |
| New tables (`item_path_refs`, `item_signatures`, `item_events`, `pr_commits`) have no query/CLI read surface | read-time resolution and scoring are #29's lane by plan; ABSORB notice posted on #29 with the new-evidence comment | fails gate 4 (tracked in #29) | #29 ships |
| `_strip_foreign` (pre-existing, base-inherited) retains a quadratic worst case on slash-free word runs | pre-existing behavior this PR did not touch; the new hot paths use the linear `_mask_foreign` instead | fails gate 4 (pre-existing, outside the new code) | profiled evidence ties it to a real sync stall |
| `test_title_evidence_parity`'s dict-level assertion message reads "relations or destinations diverge" on an evidence divergence | cosmetic wording; the per-key TITLE-EVIDENCE-PARITY loop reports correctly when reached | fails gate 2/3 | next time that test module is edited |

The store derived evidence from exactly two text channels (`mentions`/`closes_keyword`) and two timeline streams (`closed`/`cross_referenced`), while four mechanically-derivable reference families in the same payloads were extracted by nothing and the GitHub-reported link connections were not selected at all.
