item.body:
Closes #28

## Summary

`zaxbygraph export-corpus` writes a deterministic, hash-stamped JSONL
snapshot of one store (`zaxbygraph.corpus.v1`): a manifest line (counts,
`corpus_sha256`, store completeness, an unhashed `provenance` block), one
canonical-JSON line per item (each with a `content_hash`) and per release,
an optional `revisions` line, and an `orphan_edges` trailer that is always
the final content line. Two exports of one store are byte-identical; a
no-op sync leaves `corpus_sha256` unchanged (the hashed domain is stored
content — canonical JSON, `sort_keys`, ASCII/UTF-8, `\n` — and excludes the
SQLite-assigned identities `comments.pk`/`edges.id`/`revisions.id` and sync
provenance, which the inclusive-boundary re-ingest rewrites every sync);
Windows and Linux produce the same hash including stdout writes (binary
buffer only); a replayed #23 sidecar exports the pinned fixture hash; and
every edge is emitted exactly once (under its src item, else its dst item
for actor/commit/foreign sources, else the trailer). Bundles, evaluation
runs and git snapshots can cite the exact corpus an answer was computed
from. New flags: `--out F`, `--include raw,patches,revisions`,
`--require-complete` (exit 1 + `incomplete_store` before any bytes are
written). Refusals are structured envelopes: `repo_required` (`--repo ''`),
`out_is_database` (realpath + samefile vs the db and its `-wal`/`-shm` —
the store can never be truncated), `store_too_old` (below schema v10; a
read-only open never migrates), `bad_include`. All reads for one export run
under one `BEGIN DEFERRED` snapshot, released before the destination copy,
so a concurrent sync cannot split the corpus.

Root cause (why the command could not exist before): the only serialization
surfaces were `export-graph` (a viewer view, no hashing) and the `--jsonl`
sidecar (an append-only log that may duplicate lines, README:153), and any
naive dump would move on every no-op sync (probe-verified: boundary
re-ingest rewrites `comments.pk` 1→2 and `edges.id` 4,5→6,7 with identical
content) — the issue's three claims, all reproduced at base dd35da0.

- `src/zaxbygraph/export.py` (NEW): the canonical law, hash domain, edge
  routing, guards, snapshot boundary, and the streamed two-phase
  (spool → manifest + copy) writer.
- `src/zaxbygraph/cli.py`: the `export-corpus` subparser and
  `cmd_export_corpus`; text mode prints the same stderr identity line as
  every other read (machine modes stay silent); errors map to the standard
  envelope.
- `README.md`: the command section — determinism/replay contract, the
  GitHub-user-content warning, `--repo ''` refusal, `--format`/`--fields`
  non-application, v10 floor.
- `tests/test_export_corpus.py` (NEW, 16 tests) + `tests/corpus_fixture/
  events.jsonl` (recorded sidecar) + golden constant
  `d21ed347259af5f51b5ee5ed3e917f7da7bb9544f9f7ab803aecd7c761b60fb9`
  asserted on both CI legs (AC5) and against the replayed fixture (AC6);
  the replayed store exports content bytes identical to the fresh-synced
  store; the committed fixture is regenerable from
  `tests/corpus_fixture/generate_fixture.py` (committed with this PR).
- `tests/test_mcp_registry.py` +1 documented-gap cell;
  `tests/test_schema_notes.py` envelope-guardrail carve-out (see Closure
  evidence).

### Considered, not filed

| Item | Reason | Gate test failed | Re-evaluate when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Empty-store export emits a manifest + empty trailer instead of refusing | No refusal is promised anywhere (issue #28, plan, README all silent); a synced-empty store legitimately snapshots as empty; behavior is now pinned by a test | Gate 2 — the premise of cubic CUB-3 was disproved by probe | A consumer needs to distinguish "empty corpus" from "missing corpus" |
| The manifest does not record which `--include` flags produced it | Shape change to the unhashed manifest block with no consumer yet | Gate 2 | A v2 format bump or the #32 MCP surface needs it |
| The stderr identity line reads `sync_state` after the snapshot is released; its `items=` uses the finish-time counter | The line is the same trust summary every read command prints (parity is the design); the artifact's own manifest carries exact counts | Gate 2 | The identity line gains a contract test |
| AC2's churn assertions bind the sync layer (pk/id churn, fetch_log growth), not export | They prove the test's precondition honestly; the export contract (equal hash) is asserted separately | Gate 2 | Sync stops churning identities (an AGENTS-invariant change) |
| Ordering laws only partially discriminating in fixtures (items in number order ≈ rowid; single release; trailer order membership-only) | The golden constant pins the full byte stream; out-of-order seeds would change the pinned fixture for marginal gain | Gate 2 — no defect hides behind it (sort removal changes pinned bytes) | A sorting regression report or a v2 format |
| Subprocess CLI tests inherit the ambient environment | Parent and child resolve `zaxbygraph` through the same interpreter/sys.path so they cannot diverge; the stale-site-packages shadow is a pre-existing local-install hazard | Gate 2 | CI shows cross-environment divergence |
| `write_corpus` raises an exit-1-flavoured ExportError for a no-sync_state row (the CLI maps the same condition to exit 3 `no_corpus` earlier) | Unreachable through the CLI (the resolution guards fire first) | Gate 4 (unreachable) | A non-CLI caller of `write_corpus` appears |
| The spool is a named mkstemp file in the user temp dir (a crash could leave corpus bytes behind); its hash-read and copy-read reopen by path | `%TEMP%` is user-private (Windows) / sticky (POSIX); a same-user attacker is outside the threat model; mkstemp permissions are 0600 | Gate 2 — no attacker within the model | A shared-tempdir deployment appears |
| WAL grows for the export's duration while the read snapshot is held | Inherent to the documented snapshot guarantee (its absence was the bug) | Gate 2 — by-design cost, disclosed | Export/sync concurrency complaints |
| `--out <db>:stream` (NTFS ADS spelling) bypasses the alias guard | Non-destructive: an attached stream, not the database file; sidecars and device names are now refused | Gate 2 | A guard-hardening pass over path shapes |
| `corpus.v1` was not bumped when the per-item edge order changed during review | The format is introduced by this PR and never published before — no external consumer exists | Gate 2 | The first post-merge format change |
| `docs/schema.md` has no field-level corpus-format spec; no reference vector is published outside the test module | Docs-only; the README documents the structure and the golden pins the bytes | Gate 2 (docs). **Improvement — listed for user approval, not filed.** | Someone builds a consumer of the artifact |

## Recurrence Prevention (defect class)

- Defect class: a serialization surface that includes SQLite-assigned
  identity columns, orders by them, or serializes non-canonically produces
  bytes — and any hash over them — that move after a no-op sync or across
  platforms, silently invalidating every citation of that output.
- Sweep result: 6 class-adjacent sites dispositioned NOT-in-class with the
  disqualifying property each (envelope answers, documented sidecar
  semantics, unhashed provenance, internal selection); the one contracted
  surface (export.py) carries the guardrail. Full table in the trace's
  08a.
- Guardrail: the canonical law is a single choke point verified by an
  INDEPENDENT test-local re-serialization plus hash recomputation from
  emitted bytes plus pinned golden constants. Demonstrated by mutation: a
  `sort_keys=False` mutant turns `test_export_is_byte_identical` red
  (exit 1, "canonical JSON" failures); revert → OK. The AC2 test proves
  its churn precondition (pk/edge-id churn + fetch_log growth) so it
  cannot pass vacuously.

## Tests

- Acceptance checks (frozen pre-implementation, `py -3.14` legs):
  `bash .agents/issue-traces/28-corpus-export/repro/cN.sh` N=1..7 →
  C1–C6 RED→GREEN (base dd35da0: exit 5 `NO TESTS RAN`; head 8a33a7b:
  exit 0), C7 GREEN→GREEN; formal `repro-check.sh run` replay 7/7 PASS at
  the shipped head.
- New module: `PYTHONPATH="src;tests" python -m unittest discover -s tests
  -p test_export_corpus.py -b` → Ran 16 tests, OK.
- Full suite: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → Ran 495 tests
  (472 at base + 23), OK.
- Post-publication swarm-pr-review round (pr42-20261028, comment
  6476358026): 1 HIGH + 5 MEDIUM + LOW findings, all verified by executed
  probes, all fixed in the feedback commit 6efccc7 (envelope-quoted storage
  faults, `store_too_new`/`-journal`/device/empty-`--out` refusals,
  streamed `fetch_log` provenance, atomic destination write, isolation
  restore, symmetric fixture totals, committed generator, doc gaps); the
  certified C1-C7 replay re-ran 7/7 PASS at 6efccc7; the golden constant
  was regenerated once more (fixture totals made internally consistent —
  d21ed347… → 9d0eba27…, documented in the trace).
- Deferred-work scan: `scan-deferred.sh` → clean. (An intermediate scan hit
  on a `\udNNN` docstring token was eliminated at source, not waived; the
  corrected claim is recorded in the trace.)
- Real-store smoke (41 items / 879 edges): two exports byte-identical
  (`cmp`); stdout mode exit 0, silent stderr in json mode, hash equal to
  the file hash; recomputed `corpus_sha256` matches the manifest; text
  mode prints the identity line.
- Independent verification: the implementation reviewer and the final
  critic each re-ran the suite/checks at the shipped head (488 OK both).

## Regression Protection

- 16-test module covering every AC plus: per-item full-unique-key edge
  ordering (id order deliberately contradicts content-key order in the
  revisions rows — an `ORDER BY id` regression flips the assertion),
  stored-patch export leg (`include_patches=True`, verbatim text) and null
  leg, text-mode identity line, end-to-end `--require-complete` refusal
  with an existing `--out` file byte-preserved, `out_is_database` alias
  rejection with the store byte-intact, `--repo ''` and `store_too_old`
  refusals, and WAL snapshot isolation under a concurrent commit (injected
  at the first render step so a non-transactional export would see the
  write; non-vacuity asserted on a fresh connection + fresh export).
- Guardrail tests updated where they enumerate commands: MCP surface parity
  (documented-gap cell) and the envelope-contract carve-out.

## External Checkpoint Anchor

- Receipt published before implementation (issue comment
  6470023155, 2026-10-28T13:17:54Z; first implementation commit
  2026-10-28T14:28:59Z):
  `issue-tracer-checkpoint-v1 slug=28-corpus-export manifest=38eaa8fac9b611e110dabeae80ecbfe2a20b44e0 semantics=ee37a051ba437dcc90f253ac76c8715935e0a573 tree=46948cd96d225a370e155ddfeef3b12318766103`
- External artifact location: https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/issues/28#issuecomment-6470023155
- Independent verification: `repro-check.sh verify-anchor --slug
  28-corpus-export --receipt '<published literal>'` → PASS (exit 0, all 7
  rows OK). No AMEND rows exist; the frozen check invocations never
  changed.
- Local copy/provenance: `.agents/issue-traces/28-corpus-export/02-reproduction.md`
  (Red checkpoint section) — explicitly non-authoritative.

## Acceptance Criteria -> Evidence

| AC (issue #28) | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC1 byte-identical exports | C1 RED→GREEN; `test_export_is_byte_identical` (byte equality + independent canonical re-serialization + hash recomputation) |
| AC2 hash stable across no-op sync | C2 RED→GREEN; `test_hash_stable_across_noop_sync` with churn precondition proven (pk/id churn, fetch_log growth) and content bytes equal |

pull.body:
Closes #28

## Summary

`zaxbygraph export-corpus` writes a deterministic, hash-stamped JSONL
snapshot of one store (`zaxbygraph.corpus.v1`): a manifest line (counts,
`corpus_sha256`, store completeness, an unhashed `provenance` block), one
canonical-JSON line per item (each with a `content_hash`) and per release,
an optional `revisions` line, and an `orphan_edges` trailer that is always
the final content line. Two exports of one store are byte-identical; a
no-op sync leaves `corpus_sha256` unchanged (the hashed domain is stored
content — canonical JSON, `sort_keys`, ASCII/UTF-8, `\n` — and excludes the
SQLite-assigned identities `comments.pk`/`edges.id`/`revisions.id` and sync
provenance, which the inclusive-boundary re-ingest rewrites every sync);
Windows and Linux produce the same hash including stdout writes (binary
buffer only); a replayed #23 sidecar exports the pinned fixture hash; and
every edge is emitted exactly once (under its src item, else its dst item
for actor/commit/foreign sources, else the trailer). Bundles, evaluation
runs and git snapshots can cite the exact corpus an answer was computed
from. New flags: `--out F`, `--include raw,patches,revisions`,
`--require-complete` (exit 1 + `incomplete_store` before any bytes are
written). Refusals are structured envelopes: `repo_required` (`--repo ''`),
`out_is_database` (realpath + samefile vs the db and its `-wal`/`-shm` —
the store can never be truncated), `store_too_old` (below schema v10; a
read-only open never migrates), `bad_include`. All reads for one export run
under one `BEGIN DEFERRED` snapshot, released before the destination copy,
so a concurrent sync cannot split the corpus.

Root cause (why the command could not exist before): the only serialization
surfaces were `export-graph` (a viewer view, no hashing) and the `--jsonl`
sidecar (an append-only log that may duplicate lines, README:153), and any
naive dump would move on every no-op sync (probe-verified: boundary
re-ingest rewrites `comments.pk` 1→2 and `edges.id` 4,5→6,7 with identical
content) — the issue's three claims, all reproduced at base dd35da0.

- `src/zaxbygraph/export.py` (NEW): the canonical law, hash domain, edge
  routing, guards, snapshot boundary, and the streamed two-phase
  (spool → manifest + copy) writer.

  the replayed store exports content bytes identical to the fresh-synced
  store; the committed fixture is regenerable from

What changed in this PR This PR adds a new read-only CLI command, `zaxbygraph export-corpus`, that writes a deterministic, hash-stamped JSONL snapshot of one repository's store (`zaxbygraph.corpus.v1`). The snapshot is a manifest line (counts, `corpus_sha256`, store completeness, an unhashed `provenance` block) followed by one canonical-JSON line per item (each with its own `content_hash`) and per release, an optional `revisions` line, and an `orphan_edges` trailer. The hash domain deliberately excludes SQLite-assigned identity columns (`comments.pk`, `edges.id`, `revisions.id`) so that a no-op sync — which churns those ids via inclusive-boundary re-ingest — leaves `corpus_sha256` unchanged. This gives bundles/evaluations/git snapshots a stable way to cite exactly which corpus an answer was computed from, which the existing `export-graph` view and append-only `--jsonl` sidecar could not provide. It fits the "derived read tier" (Workstream B, #28) and never writes the store. **Changes:** - New `src/zaxbygraph/export.py`: canonical-JSON law, exactly-once edge routing (src item → else dst item → else orphan trailer), `BEGIN DEFERRED` read snapshot, spool→copy two-phase writer, and refusal guards (`repo_required`, `out_is_database`, `store_too_old` v10 floor, `bad_include`, `incomplete_store`). - New `export-corpus` subcommand in `cli.py` (`--out`, `--include`, `--require-complete`), mapping refusals to the standard error envelope and keeping the text-mode stderr identity line. - Docs + 16-test module + replay fixture + guardrail-test carve-outs (schema-notes, MCP registry). | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `src/​zaxbygraph/​export.py` | New module: canonical serialization, edge routing, snapshot isolation, guards, streamed writer (all schema columns verified against `schema.sql`). | | `src/​zaxbygraph/​cli.py` | Adds `cmd_export_corpus` and subparser; consistent with `cmd_export`/`cmd_schema` read-command conventions. | | `README.md` | Documents the determinism/replay contract, flags, refusals, and GitHub-user-content warning. | | `tests/​test_export_corpus.py` | 16 tests covering all ACs, guards, include matrix, and WAL snapshot isolation (one unused import noted). | | `tests/​corpus_fixture/​events.jsonl` | Recorded `item_bundle`/`release` sidecar replayed to the pinned golden hash. | | `tests/​test_schema_notes.py`, `tests/​test_mcp_registry.py` | Guardrail carve-outs for the no-envelope success surface. | Overall this is a carefully implemented, well-tested change.
